artigo.texto: Preparation matters It’s fitting that World Alzheimer’s Month, National Preparedness Month and peak hurricane season all fall in September. Hurricane season reminds us to have an emergency plan in place, especially when you're caring for someone living with Alzheimer’s disease or other dementia. As a certified dementia practitioner and executive director of Respite Care Charleston, I’ve learned that one of the most valuable things we can offer is guidance. If you are caring for someone with Alzheimer’s or other dementia, start with the basics. Create an emergency kit with medications, medical information, important documents, water, food and emergency contacts — then think beyond the supplies. Dementia is more than memory loss; it affects judgment, communication and the ability to understand what’s happening around us. Evacuation to an unfamiliar environment, and a disruption in routine can be confusing and frightening for someone living with dementia, increasing the risk of wandering, anxiety and agitation. Help reduce those risks by packing familiar comfort items and taking a photo of your loved one each morning, so if you get separated, you’ll have a current picture to help find him or her. If you are caring for someone with dementia, you don’t have to figure it all out alone. Reach out to people you trust. Talk with your family and your neighbors. Connect with organizations that understand dementia and caregiving. If you are not caring for someone with dementia, consider learning more about dementia. Be the neighbor who checks in, or give a caregiver time to run an errand. Small acts of understanding make a big difference. Just as we can’t control the path of a storm, we can’t control the course of Alzheimer’s or another form of dementia. But we can control how prepared we are to meet the challenges that come our way. So why are our elected officials allowing more data centers to be built in our state? Why are they offering incentives for them? As global warming continues to raise temperatures around the world, our utility costs increase as well. This stresses the power grid and will lead to the construction of more nuclear plants. This also will increase our utility bills while depleting our precious water supplies. To make matters worse, data centers have been allowed in our state through deceptive tactics and remain unchecked. Please write to your lawmakers and let them know this is unacceptable. artigo.texto: Previsão para as Ações da Bloom Energy: BE dispara quase 11%, a demanda por energia de data centers de IA pode continuar impulsionando as ações? Em 29 de setembro (ET), as ações da Bloom Energy saltaram 10,8%, a US$ 291,25, impulsionadas pela alta demanda de data centers de IA por geração local de energia e parcerias estratégicas, como com a Oracle e a Brookfield. A receita do segundo trimestre disparou 165,5% ano a ano, atingindo US$ 1,065 bilhão, e a empresa elevou suas projeções para 2026. Apesar da forte expansão e do valuation elevado (P/S de 23,3x), os riscos incluem a execução de projetos, aprovações regulatórias e volatilidade técnica, com zona de resistência crítica entre US$ 302 e US$ 305. TradingKey - Em 29 de setembro (ET), a Bloom Energy (BE) fechou em alta de 10,8%, cotada a US$ 291,25, atingindo uma máxima intradiária de US$ 302,25, com o volume de negociação alcançando aproximadamente 23,69 milhões de ações, significativamente acima das médias recentes. Na sessão anterior, a BE havia recuado 8,95%, indicando um aumento acentuado na volatilidade do preço das ações em patamares elevados. [Fonte: TradingView] De acordo com informações divulgadas pela cidade de Fremont, a Bloom Energy adquiriu uma instalação local de aproximadamente 158.000 pés quadrados para expandir suas operações e prevê criar centenas de empregos em manufatura avançada. A finalidade específica, a capacidade adicional e o cronograma de produção ainda não foram anunciados. O analista David Arcaro, do Morgan Stanley, acredita que a expansão reflete a forte demanda contínua pelos produtos da empresa. O Jefferies manteve sua recomendação de "manutenção" (Hold) e elevou o preço-alvo de US$ 229 para US$ 264, valor que continua abaixo do último preço de fechamento da BE. Escassez de Energia em Data Centers de IA Impulsiona Demanda por Geração Local de Energia O consumo de energia por clusters de servidores de IA continua a subir, enquanto os ciclos de construção para conexão à rede elétrica e infraestrutura de transmissão permanecem longos, levando alguns data centers a adotarem soluções de geração de energia no próprio local. As células de combustível de óxido sólido da Bloom Energy podem gerar eletricidade nas instalações dos clientes, reduzindo a dependência de capacidade adicional da rede elétrica, embora os projetos ainda precisem garantir o fornecimento de combustível e obter as licenças necessárias. O contrato-máster de prestação de serviços assinado entre a Oracle e a Bloom Energy cobre até 2,8 GW em sistemas de células de combustível, dos quais 1,2 GW já foi contratado e teve sua implantação iniciada, com a capacidade remanescente dependendo de aquisições subsequentes e do progresso dos projetos. A Bloom Energy e a Brookfield também ampliaram sua estrutura de financiamento para projetos de infraestrutura de IA de US$ 5 bilhões para US$ 25 bilhões, com o capital específico a ser liberado à medida que os projetos avançarem. A Bloom Energy declarou que seu segmento de infraestrutura de IA atendeu a quase 24 clientes, representando aproximadamente 250 MW de capacidade. A administração da empresa também destacou que grandes hyperscalers dos EUA, além de mais de uma dúzia de provedores de nuvem para IA, laboratórios de IA e operadores de data centers, validaram e aprovaram suas soluções de suprimento de energia. Receita cresce 166% à medida que entrega de projetos se torna fundamental A receita da Bloom Energy no segundo trimestre atingiu US$ 1,065 bilhão, uma alta de 165,5% na comparação anual; a margem bruta GAAP subiu de 26,7% para 33,4%, e o fluxo de caixa operacional foi de US$ 226,4 milhões. A empresa elevou sua projeção de receita para 2026 para a faixa de US$ 3,9 bilhões a US$ 4,2 bilhões, com o ponto médio representando um crescimento anual de aproximadamente 100%; a projeção para o LPA não GAAP foi fixada entre US$ 2,55 e US$ 2,85. Com base em um valor de mercado de aproximadamente US$ 94,2 bilhões em 29 de setembro e no ponto médio da projeção de receita de US$ 4,05 bilhões, o índice preço/vendas (P/S) nos últimos 12 meses da BE é de aproximadamente 23,3x. O valuation atual exige que a empresa mantenha um crescimento relativamente rápido e conclua a expansão de capacidade e as entregas de projetos em grande escala conforme o planejado. As principais áreas de atenção daqui para frente incluem o uso pretendido e o cronograma de comissionamento da nova instalação em Fremont, se a capacidade restante de 1,6 GW sob o acordo com a Oracle pode ser convertida em compras firmes e as variações na margem bruta. Além disso, gasodutos de gás natural, licenças de qualidade do ar e o avanço da construção de projetos como o Project Jupiter também podem impactar a implantação de equipamentos e o cronograma de reconhecimento de receita. [Fonte: TradingView] Em caso de alta, a faixa de US$ 302 a US$ 305 é atualmente a principal zona de resistência. Se a BE fechar acima de US$ 305 com forte volume, o próximo nível a ser observado é de US$ 330 a US$ 331, correspondente ao nível de extensão de Fibonacci de 1,272; após um novo rompimento, a atenção pode se voltar para o nível de extensão de 1,618 em torno de US$ 367. artigo.texto: O status regulatório e as perspectivas econômicas da implementação do Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE) para o mercado de carbono foram discutidos, nesta segunda-feira (28), durante a 144ª reunião do Conselho Temático de Meio Ambiente e Sustentabilidade da Confederação Nacional da Indústria (CNI), a Coemas. Na ocasião, o presidente do conselho e vice-presidente da CNI, Marcelo Thomé, informou que a CNI representa o setor industrial no Comitê Técnico Consultivo Permanente (CTCP), da Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono (SEMC), do Ministério da Fazenda. A Confederação também participa ativamente dos grupos de trabalho dedicados aos aspectos para a implementação do SBCE. “A CNI e diversas associações do setor produtivo também vêm realizando reuniões bilaterais junto às equipes do Ministério da Fazenda para tratar de especificidades de cada subsetor industrial contemplado no SBCE, de modo a contarmos com regulamentações aderentes à realidade da indústria brasileira”, explicou. A secretária da SEMC, Cristina Fróes de Borja Reis, apresentou um resumo do andamento regulatório do SBCE, agradeceu a parceria contínua com a CNI e ressaltou que a regulamentação do mercado de carbono é imprescindível para a política industrial. Ela também defendeu que as regras devem ser desenhadas observando as capacidades internas e valorizando a resiliência e os avanços em sustentabilidade já alcançados pelo setor produtivo nacional. Cristina apresentou projeções que indicam que o SBCE poderá proporcionar um impacto positivo adicional ao Produto Interno Brasileiro (PIB) de 5,8% até 2040 e de 8,5% até 2050, além de contribuir para uma redução de até 27% nas emissões de gases de efeito estufa até 2050. “Nós estamos atuando fortemente para fomentar o mercado de carbono e estamos numa luta contra o tempo, mas sempre com muita seriedade e robustez técnica para publicar as normas infralegais”, afirmou. A secretária relatou os desdobramentos da consulta pública sobre a portaria de cobertura setorial inicial do mercado regulado, que recebeu quase mil contribuições do setor produtivo e do meio acadêmico, com subsídios para ajustes em segmentos como óleo e gás, resíduos e setor elétrico. Além disso, informou que, ainda em 2026, serão realizadas mais duas consultas públicas de dois decretos regulamentadores: do Programa Brasileiro de Monitoramento, Relato e Verificação (MRV) e o de Credenciamento de Metodologias para a geração de créditos de carbono. O superintendente de Meio Ambiente e Sustentabilidade da CNI, Davi Bomtempo, agradeceu a parceria com a equipe do Ministério da Fazenda e ressaltou que o diálogo com o setor privado foi iniciado ainda na elaboração do projeto de lei e se consolida agora, na etapa de regulamentação do mercado de carbono, por meio do trabalho conjunto em grupos técnicos para compreender as especificidades da indústria nacional. "Estamos juntos com a Secretaria desde a construção do projeto de lei, em permanente diálogo com o setor produtivo. Agora, nesta fase mais complexa de regulamentação do mercado de carbono no Brasil, a equipe segue trabalhando com a indústria brasileira, estudando em conjunto seus processos e formas de regulação”, enfatizou. Semana de Clima de Nova York e Preparação para a COP31 Davi Bomtempo também compartilhou os resultados da atuação da Susteinable Business COP (SB COP) durante a Semana do Clima de Nova York, realizada de 20 a 27 de setembro. O superintendente destacou a presença de mais de 500 participantes em fóruns proprietários, a assinatura da parceria oficial com o Climate High-Level Champions e a entrega formal da Carta de Prioridades do Setor Privado para as presidências da COP30 e da COP31. 17ª Conferência das Partes da Biodiversidade (COP17) O gerente de Recursos Naturais da CNI, Mário Cardoso, e o sócio-diretor da Consultoria Agroícone, Rodrigo Lima, detalharam o cenário de negociações para a COP17 da Biodiversidade, que acontecerá de 16 a 30 de outubro em Yerevan, Armênia. Ao apresentar os preparativos para a COP 17 da Biodiversidade, Mário Cardoso explicou que a conferência na Armênia vai discutir sobre o financiamento necessário para implementar as metas globais e a regulamentação do uso econômico de Informações de Sequência Digital (DSI). "O ponto central das negociações na Armênia será a mobilização de recursos. De nada adianta assumir compromissos se não houver financiamento para torná-los reais. Outro tema decisivo para o setor produtivo é a definição das regras de operacionalização do Fundo Cali para DSI, que atinge diretamente as empresas usuárias de dados genéticos e as diretrizes de governança da biologia sintética." Ele também destacou a Meta 15, que é uma das 23 estabelecidas pelo Marco Global de Biodiversidade Kunming-Montreal, adotado no âmbito da Convenção sobre Diversidade Biológica (CDB) da ONU. Trata-se de uma diretriz em acordos multilaterais globais que determina que os governos criem mecanismos para exigir que grandes empresas e instituições financeiras avaliem e divulguem regularmente seus riscos, impactos e dependências em relação à biodiversidade. Durante a COP17 da Biodiversidade, as nações negociarão os critérios e prazos nacionais para operacionalizar a Meta 15 na legislação de cada país.

artigo.texto: A infraestrutura computacional voltada ao processamento de algoritmos avançados e serviços de nuvem consolidou-se como um dos principais vetores de consumo de energia do planeta. De acordo com o relatório internacional intitulado “IA encontra a rede elétrica: moldando o cenário energético dos data centers”, divulgado pela Capgemini, a aceleração das atividades de data centers tem colocado pressão inédita sobre os sistemas de transmissão e distribuição de eletricidade. O levantamento indica que mais de 60% dos executivos do setor elétrico contam com ferramentas de inteligência artificial para destravar saltos expressivos de produtividade operacional e eficiência na gestão de fluxos de potência. A pesquisa da multinacional de consultoria e tecnologia entrevistou 612 diretores e executivos seniores do setor de energia elétrica envolvidos no atendimento a instalações de missão crítica, além de 175 lideranças proprietárias e operadoras de centros de processamento de dados e cerca de 20 especialistas industriais globais. O estudo abrangeu 21 nações distribuídas por América do Norte, Europa, Ásia-Pacífico e América Latina, incluindo o Brasil. A análise central apresentada pela organização pontua que o descompasso entre a velocidade de implantação de servidores de alta densidade e a expansão física da infraestrutura de transmissão exige uma reestruturação imediata dos modelos operacionais de utilidades públicas. Descompasso operacional e o panorama da infraestrutura elétrica Historicamente, a expansão das redes elétricas mundiais baseou-se em ciclos previsíveis de planejamento de longo prazo, com cronogramas de amortização de ativos que costumam variar entre 15 e 30 anos. Por outro lado, a evolução dos clusters de computação intensiva voltados ao treinamento de grandes modelos de linguagem opera em ciclos tecnológicos bienais ou trienais. As empresas responsáveis pelo fornecimento energético sustentam que essa discrepância temporal cria gargalos no atendimento a novos pontos de conexão, gerando filas de espera para interligação de novos complexos industriais de tecnologia em polos consolidados. No recorte da América Latina, e especificamente no mercado brasileiro, as alegações do estudo refletem tensões próprias do arranjo regional. Embora o parque gerador nacional exiba predominância de fontes renováveis — como hidrelétricas, parques eólicos e complexos solares —, as limitações nas linhas de transmissão interestaduais e a volatilidade climática exigem respostas rápidas de despacho. O documento da Capgemini argumenta que a corrida das empresas de tecnologia (hyperscalers) por contratos de fornecimento firme de energia verde intensificou a necessidade de soluções computacionais que monitorem o balanço entre oferta e demanda em tempo real, mitigando riscos de instabilidade sistêmica. Em termos setoriais, concessionárias enfrentam custos crescentes de modernização de subestações antigas e desafios regulatórios relacionados à integração de fontes distribuídas. A consultoria alega que, enquanto o consumo bruto de eletricidade impulsionado por cargas computacionais continuará em alta pelos próximos três a cinco anos, o setor de utilidades públicas opera com taxas de adoção de tecnologias digitais abaixo do potencial necessário para suportar essa carga sem perdas substanciais de receita ou interrupções de fornecimento. Métricas de implementação digital nas concessionárias de energia Os indicadores quantitativos reunidos pelo levantamento da entidade revelam um hiato entre o reconhecimento estratégico das novas ferramentas e sua efetiva aplicação prática nas concessionárias. Conforme os dados compilados no relatório internacional, menos da metade das companhias pesquisadas emprega ferramentas de aprendizado de máquina em suas rotinas de engenharia de rede: A pesquisa defende que a baixa taxa atual de uso de Agentes de IA — registrada em apenas 16% — evidencia que grande parte das redes mundiais ainda opera sob processos semiautomatizados ou reativos. Os agentes autônomos diferenciam-se de algoritmos convencionais de aprendizado por possuírem capacidade de percepção contextual, tomada de decisão algorítmica e execução de manobras de chaveamento sem dependência contínua de intervenção humana em centros de controle operacional (CCO). Conforme sustenta a organização responsável pelo diagnóstico, o plano de mais de metade dos operadores (58%) em ativar agentes nos próximos 24 meses visa conter custos operacionais associados à manutenção preventiva e aumentar a velocidade de restauração do sistema diante de eventos climáticos severos ou oscilações imprevistas de carga provocadas por data centers. Aplicações técnicas da automação algorítmica e impactos corporativos A introdução sistemática de soluções analíticas no segmento de utilidades tem o potencial de remodelar a produtividade corporativa em múltiplos elos da cadeia de valor. artigo.texto: Os projetos de instalação de centros de dados no concelho de Abrantes voltaram ao debate político na Assembleia Municipal, com a CDU a levantar dúvidas sobre os benefícios fiscais, os impactos ambientais e a capacidade dos promotores, enquanto o PS defendeu que o concelho não deve afastar oportunidades de investimento, desde que sejam cumpridas as exigências ambientais e conhecidos os respetivos impactos. Ana Paula Cruz, eleita pela CDU, centrou a intervenção no projeto inicialmente apresentado pela EDC One para os terrenos junto à antiga Central do Pego. A eleita questionou a experiência, capacidade financeira e conhecimento técnico da empresa promotora e recordou os benefícios fiscais associados ao investimento. O projeto recebeu, em setembro de 2025, o estatuto de Projeto Empresarial de Importância Municipal, tendo sido aprovado um pacote de isenções de IMI, IMT e Derrama que poderá atingir 16,2 milhões de euros. Parte destes benefícios só se concretizará caso o investimento avance e cumpra as condições contratualizadas. Jornal de Abrantes Ana Paula Cruz apontou ainda potenciais consequências ambientais associadas aos centros de dados, nomeadamente ao nível dos consumos de eletricidade e água, ruído e pressão sobre o rio Tejo. São preocupações que também têm sido levantadas por organizações ambientalistas, embora os consumos efetivos dos projetos de Abrantes ainda dependam das soluções tecnológicas e dos processos de licenciamento. A Quercus tem defendido uma avaliação dos impactos cumulativos dos dois projetos previstos para o concelho. Quercus A eleita da CDU quis, por isso, saber quando foi a Assembleia Municipal informada das vantagens e inconvenientes dos investimentos e dos compromissos assumidos pelo município. Questionou também se já são conhecidas as empresas ou consórcios com capacidade financeira e tecnológica para concretizar os projetos e qual a situação relativamente à classificação como projetos PIN. Ana Paula Cruz, eleita CDU Do lado do PS, Tiago Ricardo defendeu que Abrantes não deve «ficar à margem desta transformação», considerando possível compatibilizar investimento e transição energética com a proteção ambiental. O eleito socialista salientou, no entanto, que os estudos de impacto ambiental ainda não são conhecidos e defendeu informação pública sobre os resultados dos eventuais investimentos. Entre os indicadores apontados estão o emprego efetivamente criado, contratação de empresas locais, formação, retorno para o município e parâmetros ambientais. Tiago Ricardo sustentou que os territórios do interior não podem rejeitar oportunidades de investimento e, simultaneamente, lamentar problemas relacionados com emprego e perda de população, defendendo «prudência» e análise antes da concretização dos projetos. Tiago Ricardo, eleito PS Na resposta, o presidente da Câmara de Abrantes, Manuel Jorge Valamatos, reconheceu que ainda existem elementos por conhecer, nomeadamente quanto às necessidades de água dos projetos. O autarca rejeitou, por isso, que nesta fase possam ser dados como adquiridos determinados valores de consumo e remeteu a avaliação dos impactos para os procedimentos ambientais a realizar pelas entidades competentes. Valamatos defendeu ainda que as tecnologias atuais permitem soluções de circuito fechado nos sistemas de refrigeração e pediu que sejam aguardados os estudos e os processos de licenciamento antes de serem retiradas conclusões sobre os impactos concretos. O presidente da Câmara voltou também a justificar os incentivos municipais com os pressupostos económicos associados aos investimentos e apontou para a criação de cerca de 600 postos de trabalho no conjunto dos dois projetos atualmente considerados pelo município. O autarca colocou os centros de dados numa estratégia mais ampla de atração de indústria tecnológica para Abrantes, destacando como vantagens do território a disponibilidade de terrenos industriais, energia, recursos hídricos e conhecimento técnico. Manuel Jorge Valamatos, presidente CM Abrantes Atualmente estão em diferentes fases dois grandes projetos de centros de dados no concelho. O investimento inicialmente promovido pela EDC One prevê sete mil milhões de euros e recebeu benefícios fiscais municipais que podem atingir 16,2 milhões. O segundo, associado à Hyperion, recebeu parecer municipal favorável em sede de Pedido de Informação Prévia, não correspondendo essa decisão à aprovação definitiva do empreendimento. A situação relativa ao estatuto PIN tem sido um dos pontos de discussão. Na visita da ministra do Ambiente a Abrantes, em meados de setembro, ficou a saber-se que ambos os projetos têm estatuto PIN e ambos têm ligação à rede elétrica aprovada.

artigo.texto: The Instalco company Enervion begins work two large-scale battery storage projects in Finland The Instalco subsidiary Enervion Oy has commenced work on two battery storage systems in Kittilä in northern Finland. Work on site has now begun with groundworks and initial installations. The projects comprise turnkey delivery followed by ten years of operation and maintenance services. The assignment comprises two parallel battery energy storage projects, Sirkka and Köngäs, each with a power of 10 MW and a storage capacity of 20 MWh. The systems are based on Enico Jupiter Nova technology, developed specifically for demanding Nordic and Arctic climate conditions. Enervion is responsible for turnkey EPC delivery covering design, procurement, construction, installation and commissioning, followed by ten years of operations and maintenance services. The customer is wattss Services AG, a Swiss-based battery storage specialist with over six years of experience. "These projects are a clear testament to what Enervion and the Instalco Group can achieve within large-scale battery storage. Sirkka and Köngäs are two technically demanding projects carried out in parallel under challenging Arctic conditions in Lapland. By combining expertise from across the Group and our partner network, we are capable of undertaking increasingly large and advanced energy projects," says Anssi Laaksonen, CEO of Enervion. The contracts were signed in May 2026 and the order value of approximately EUR 10 million was included in Instalco’s order backlog at the end of the second quarter of 2026. The facilities are scheduled for completion and commissioning in summer 2027. Enervion is an Instalco subsidiary in Finland specialising in large-scale battery and energy storage projects. For further information, please contact: Fredrik Trahn, Head of Communications and Sustainability, Instalco +46 70 913 67 96 fredrik.trahn@instalco.se Instalco is one of Northern Europe’s leading installation companies in the areas of electrical, heating and plumbing, ventilation, industry, and tech & consulting. We design, install, service and maintain properties and facilities in Sweden, Norway, Finland and Germany. Operations are conducted through more than 175 subsidiaries with strong local presence, supported by a small central organisation. Instalco is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under the ticker INSTAL. For more information, visit www.instalco.se. Image Attachments Attachments The Instalco company Enervion begins work two large-scale battery storage projects in Finland

artigo.texto: Having been in the information technology field since 1969, I have been reading about data centers in Lancaster County and how candidates for political office are responding to questions about them. Data centers consolidate computer power in one place to process massive amounts of information for multiple businesses. If everything goes well, large corporations will not only be saving money but also making large amounts of money. However, these centers are risky. When servers of multiple corporations are housed under one roof, even one breach of security can open opportunities for private information to cascade from business to business. Data centers will result in the elimination of jobs. They often need a huge amount of water to cool the servers, draining water from the community rivers, lakes and wells while raising the temperature in rivers and other waterways, killing fish and other water life. In addition, the air conditioning needed to cool the buildings will demand high levels of electricity, raising electricity costs and creating significant noise. I support state Sen. James Malone saying that we must pause building data centers until we have a clear understanding of how they will impact our communities. I approve of Gov. Josh Shapiro’s statement that businesses must be responsible for the costs of operation. I am pleased to hear that Jess Branas, candidate for the 97th Pennsylvania House District, is speaking up against data centers, pledging to work across the aisle and with townships to attract businesses that help communities to flourish — while bringing down energy costs. Richard Wilson West Earl Township

artigo.texto: Xcel Energy proposes rules for data centers in Texas to protect residential customers AMARILLO, Texas (KVII) — Xcel Energy has asked Texas regulators to approve new rules for data centers and other large electricity users, saying the proposal would protect residential and business customers from bearing the cost of infrastructure needed to serve the projects. The utility submitted its proposed large-load tariff to the Public Utility Commission of Texas, Xcel Energy said Monday. If approved, the tariff would set terms for customers with major electricity needs, including data centers and industrial users. Xcel said those customers would be responsible for costs tied to the electric infrastructure needed for their projects, including transmission lines, substations, interconnection upgrades and new generation. The proposal would generally require long-term commitments of 15 years or more, backed by financial security if a project is delayed, reduced or never completed, the company said. Large users also would face minimum monthly payment requirements for infrastructure built and available to serve them, even if their electricity use increases gradually. Customers that leave service early could face termination charges intended to recover project-specific costs. “We know many of our customers are concerned about the scale of electricity needed to serve larger data center customers,” Brad Baldridge, interim president of Xcel Energy-Texas, New Mexico, said in a statement. “These rules make sure data centers and other large customers pay for the power they use and any necessary infrastructure so that it’s planned and built responsibly.” Xcel said requiring large customers to fund their incremental infrastructure costs could allow additional electricity sales to help spread existing fixed grid costs across a larger customer base over time. The Public Utility Commission of Texas must approve the proposal before it can take effect.

artigo.texto: [News] China Unveils 15th Five-Year Battery Plan, Targets Initial Large-Scale All-Solid-State Battery Deployment by 2030 China is setting out its next-stage roadmap for emerging battery technologies, with solid-state and sodium-ion batteries among the key areas targeted for further development. According to Xinhua News, China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and six other government departments released the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Development of the New Battery Industry on September 28. TechNews adds that the plan also calls for expanding the use of new battery technologies in areas including energy storage and data centers. By 2030, the plan targets breakthroughs in advanced electrode materials, novel electrolytes, and high-end auxiliary materials, alongside major progress in next-generation battery technologies. It also aims to achieve initial large-scale application of all-solid-state batteries, extend the cycle life of long-life lithium batteries to 15,000 cycles, and reduce product defect rates among leading companies to the parts-per-billion (PPB) level. TechNews adds that the plan seeks to expand new battery applications beyond the EV market. It calls for greater integration of new batteries with clean energy and energy-consuming equipment, extending their use to ships, aviation, intelligent robots, and construction machinery. For energy storage, targeted applications include power generation, power grids, industrial parks, and data centers, expanding the role of new batteries in next-generation power systems. Beyond the 2030 targets, Xinhua notes that the plan outlines 19 key tasks across five areas. These include developing intelligent production lines for key battery manufacturing processes, advancing new battery structures such as flexible and internally series-connected designs, improving battery lifecycle data management, accelerating industry standards, and strengthening intellectual property and trade-secret protections. The new roadmap comes as all-solid-state battery development continues to advance globally. According to TrendForce, the global all-solid-state battery (ASSB) industry is moving from laboratory development toward engineering validation and pilot production in 2026. Some leading companies have advanced to Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) 5–6, with Toyota, Honda, Nissan, and Samsung SDI slightly ahead in small-scale pilot production. Meanwhile, Chinese companies including CATL, BYD, and FAW are advancing their own pilot lines toward TRL 4–5. China Accelerates ASSB Pilot Production and Vehicle Validation China is seeing progress in ASSB pilot production and product validation. According to China Energy News, several domestic companies are advancing pilot lines in 2026. BYD’s first sulfide-based ASSB pilot line in Shenzhen entered operation in February with planned capacity of 2 GWh, while GAC’s ASSB pilot line has also begun operations and is expected to conduct small-scale vehicle testing in 2026. Gotion High-tech, meanwhile, has completed its first ASSB experimental line with designed capacity of 0.2 GWh. Vehicle validation is also moving forward. National Business Daily notes that BYD plans to begin demonstration deployment of ASSBs in vehicles around 2027 before moving toward large-scale adoption after 2030. Changan aims to begin vehicle validation in 2026 and gradually move toward mass production in 2027, while Chery plans targeted vehicle deployment in 2026 and batch vehicle validation in 2027. artigo.texto: A month after a tied vote on the issue, the Davidson County Board of Commissioners moved Monday night toward enacting a temporary pause on data centers. The commissioners approved setting a public hearing for Oct. 26 on a four-month moratorium. The 4-2 vote, with newly appointed Commissioner Steve Shook participating in place of the late Fred McClure and with Commissioner Todd Yates absent, followed a sometimes-heated debate that underscored the growing divide over the industry's potential benefits and risks. Commissioners Tripp Kester, Matt Mizell, Chris Elliott and Shook voted to move forward with a public hearing for a moratorium. Commissioners Karen Watford and Steve Shell voted no. The action represents a significant shift from Aug. 24, when a proposed six-month moratorium died on a 3-3 vote after a public hearing packed with residents urging county leaders to slow or stop data center development while county officials study potential impacts and developed zoning regulations. At Monday's meeting, Commissioner Tripp Kester asked that the commissioners revisit the issue, arguing that county staff and elected officials need additional time to research the concerns surrounding data centers as staff prepares a new zoning ordinance. County Planning and Zoning Director Lee Crook and his staff are currently drafting regulations that would establish where data centers can be and what restrictions there should be. "The issue is not whether we're for or against data centers," Kester said, emphasizing that he is seeking time for additional research and public input. There has not been a proposal for a data center, but the debate over data centers first surfaced in July when Commissioner Matt Mizell proposed a temporary moratorium amid growing public concern about the facilities' potential effects on water supplies, electric infrastructure, property owners and the county's rural character. Residents speaking during previous hearings questioned whether Davidson County was prepared to regulate an industry known for its substantial electricity demands and, in some cases, large water consumption needs. Others pointed to reports from communities around the country where neighbors have complained about persistent equipment noise and strain on local resources. Commissioner Chris Elliott reiterated those concerns Monday night. "I will tell you why I am for this," Elliott said. "I haven't talked with our state representatives or our federal representatives and asked them to come before this board and explain what the benefits are to these and what the risks are to national security if we don't do this. What are the protections for the environment and other concerns?" Elliott said state and federal officials have not given county leaders "the time of day" to discuss those questions even as they speak in favor of data center development. "It's like they're saying, 'Vote yes now and trust us later," Elliott said. "I don't like that." Board Chairwoman Karen Watford said she remains opposed to a moratorium, arguing that county staff is already developing regulations and that adopting a temporary ban could send the wrong message to prospective businesses. "I am very much against it and I think Mr. (Lee) Crook and his group is very much on their way to making the rules up and making everything so we are safe for the future," Watford said. "I personally think you are sending a message that we don't want to consider anything, whether it be a light one or a big one." Commissioners Steve Shell and Watford also noted that data centers can bring significant economic benefits. During the August discussion, Yates pointed out that one data center company previously interested in a site in Davidson County was projected to generate approximately $94 million in tax revenue while creating business opportunities associated with artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. Monday's discussion briefly became contentious when Shell reacted to local environmental activist Jeneen Sperduto, in the audience, smiling or laughing during Shell's comments. "You can laugh all you want, missy," Shell said to Sperduto, who responded with something that was hard to hear even on playback of the meeting video. "No, you don't know what you're talking about, and I would appreciate it if you would just shut up," Shell said. "It's not your time to speak." "Did you just tell me to shut up?" Sperduto asked. "Yes, I did," Shell said. "I don't stutter." Watford then asked a deputy to escort Sperduto outside to allow emotions to cool. Following further discussion, Sperduto remained in the meeting and the board continued its debate. Later Shell apologized for telling Sperduto to "shut up." Seeking a compromise, Kester reduced his request from a six-month moratorium to four months. "I am as passionate about the moratorium as Chairman Watford is in her beliefs," Kester said. "I am not saying I am against all data centers. What I am saying is that we need time to thoroughly investigate this situation and to let the citizens have input and to not just shove something down their throats." At the public hearing on Oct. 26, residents will have another opportunity to weigh in before commissioners vote to impose a moratorium.

artigo.texto: SPANISH FORK, Utah — A group of Spanish Fork citizens has filed for a referendum to be held on the Title 15 Amendment, which recently set requirements for data centers that generate their own electricity. City officials confirmed the application was submitted Monday afternoon. They now have 20 days to review the application, beginning Tuesday. Locals in Spanish Fork joined a growing number of Utahns who’ve fought back against a data center project coming to their community when a proposal started getting discussed at the mouth of Spanish Fork Canyon this summer. “The concern is not that data centers exist,” said Teresa Wood. “The concern is that they’re coming too quickly with too many unknowns and we’re playing a game of catch up.” The Provo-based company known as Volition was set to move in less than a mile away from Wood. She was among many who spoke up. On Sept.21, the council approved an amendment to the city's land use code, known as Title 15. “Title 15 took us as close as you could possibly get to full protection,” Wood said. “But nothing is as secure as distance.” She was beyond relieved when the company informed them that they would move the project miles away to an industrial area west of I-15 called Stockman Flats. While this plan isn’t set in stone yet, Volition CEO Jeff Chavez said he wanted to bring this project to this area to ease the minds of concerned neighbors. But his project may still face another roadblock. “I had a citizen reach out to my personal page and say, ‘Hey, we’re filing a referendum. Where do we start? What do we do?’” said Farrah Pliley. Pliley is with the Box Elder Accountability Referendum group, or "BEAR," which formed back in the spring when the Stratos project first caused an uproar. She said their efforts continue in far northern Utah. “We are just in the litigation process right now,” Pliley said, as they continue to appeal the denial of their own referendum application. Pliley and other BEAR members are using their experience to support other communities like Spanish Fork. So she amplified the call for a referendum on the Title 15 Amendment. “Make sure you put your voice out there because it does make a difference. We’re seeing that,” said Pliley. There is also a county-wide ordinance in the works. “Whether it's a data center or any industrial-type project, we want to make sure there are protections for our citizens,” said Utah County Commissioner Amelia Powers Gardner. She said they’ve been approached by six potential project groups just in the past year, so they’re looking to put those protections in for county lands before anything is built. “Number one, we want to make sure that any impact to infrastructure is paid for by the business,” Powers Gardner said. “Number two, we want to make sure we’re not negatively affecting our citizens, and number three, we want to protect the environment for future generations.” The commissioner said the ordinance will require developers to attend two public meetings before they can apply for a permit, and they will have to send postcards to anyone within a one-mile radius of the project. There are also requirements it will set for energy, water use and more. Powers Gardner said they’re taking lessons learned from elsewhere. “So that anyone who wants to come here knows that you’re going to come here as a benefit to the community,” said Powers Gardner. Powers Gardner said that data center ordinance is still with Utah County’s planning commission. They will meet to discuss it further in October.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich- During the 7th China Liaoning International Investment and Trade Fair, BYD Battery signed strategic cooperation agreements with the Yingkou municipal government, and separately with the Liaoyang government and Xiamen Xiangyu Group. The partnerships target zero-carbon demonstration projects, new-energy supply chain synergy, and logistics electrification. Image source: FinDreams Battery Under the Yingkou pact, both sides will advance the "Future Zero-Carbon Port City" initiative — a national-level smart energy and green transportation demonstration project. To electrify port-area transport, they will scale up pure-electric heavy trucks for short-haul container drayage and steel-plant transfers, backed by integrated solar-storage-charging stations. On the zero-carbon front, the plan calls for integrated source-grid-load-storage systems and carbon-emission monitoring platforms. The partners will also push battery recycling to build a green circular industrial system for the port area. Next up, Yingkou will map out application scenarios across ports, steel mills, and industrial parks, teaming up with BYD Battery to draft an annual construction schedule. That same day, BYD Battery, the Liaoyang government, and Xiamen Xiangyu Group signed a three-way strategic framework agreement. Drawing on Xiangyu's aluminum supply chain, the trio will expand ties in battery structural parts, body components, and new-material supply — while jointly exploring integrated "new-energy heavy truck plus solar-storage-charging" solutions. To keep the collaboration on track, they will establish a mechanism for annual high-level talks, dedicated task forces, and information sharing.

artigo.texto: By Vivian Emoni The University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN) says robust approval criteria are essential to protecting Nigeria’s interests in the carbon market. The Vice-Chancellor of the UNN, Prof. Simon Ortuanya, made the call at a stakeholders` workshop on draft review and validation of Nigeria’s Host Country Approval (HCA) criteria for carbon market operations, on Tuesday in Abuja. The workshop was organised by National Council on Climate Change (NCCC), and the Resource and Environmental Policy Research Centre (REPRC-EfD Nigeria). Ortuanya also called for clear, practical and transparent criteria for approving carbon market projects, while emphasising the need for evidence-based and transparent HCA criteria to strengthen Nigeria’s carbon market framework. He commended the NCCC and the Resource and Environmental Policy Research Centre (REPRC-EfD Nigeria) for convening the workshop. He said the collaboration demonstrated the importance of partnerships between government and research institutions in developing evidence-based policies. The vice chancellor, who was represented by Prof. Nnaemeka Chukwuone, Director, REPRC-EfD Nigeria, also appreciated the Partnership for Economic Policy (PEP) and Hewlett for supporting the project financially. He said the global carbon market offered opportunities to mobilise climate finance, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon economy. He said that such opportunities are particularly important for Nigeria as it pursued economic growth, industrial development and energy access and poverty reduction. “A well-governed carbon market could help mobilise resources needed to achieve those objectives while addressing the challenges of climate change. “the Federal Government has taken steps to institutionalise carbon market governance through the approval of the carbon market framework. “The next critical step is to support the framework with clear, practical and transparent HCA criteria for carbon market projects. “The criteria will guide project eligibility, screening and assessment, while clarifying institutional responsibilities and approval procedures,” he said. Ortuanya noted that the criteria would cover measurement, reporting and verification, environmental and social safeguards, and alignment with Nigeria’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). He said they would also address registry and transparency arrangements as well as carbon accounting, adding that the criteria must protect Nigeria’s interests. He said the proposed HCA criteria were developed from research, noting that effective public policies should be informed by credible evidence and stakeholder engagement. He said the workshop would allow participants to examine the proposed criteria from regulatory, institutional, investment, environmental, social and implementation perspectives. The vice-chancellor urged participants to identify gaps, clarify institutional responsibilities and propose practical solutions to strengthen the approval and authorisation procedures. He expressed confidence that the technical sessions, stakeholder discussions and plenary deliberations would generate recommendations for refining and finalising the HCA criteria. The Director General of the NCCC, Dr Omotenioye Majekodunmi, said that carbon markets could mobilise climate finance, unlock private investment, support green industrialisation and create jobs if underpinned by clear goals and transparency. Majekodunmi said the Climate Change Act 2021 provided the legal foundation for coordinated climate action, while the Nigerian Carbon Market Framework guided participation in carbon markets. She said the criteria must protect Nigeria’s national interests while providing certainty for credible investors and project developers, ensuring genuine mitigation outcomes and sustainable development. Majekodunmi said that the carbon projects must respect host communities, promote social inclusion and align with national climate priorities while protecting Nigeria’s ability to achieve its NDC. The director said the criteria should prevent double-counting, strengthen confidence in Nigeria’s carbon market and ensure communities received transparent, fair and enforceable benefits from carbon finance. She said the workshop would test whether the criteria were practical, legally sound and technically robust, urging participants to make frank and constructive contributions before declaring the workshop open. Prof. Adekola Adenikinju, Partnership for Economic Policy (PEP) Scientific Adviser, commended the NCCC and the REPRC-EfD Nigeria for convening stakeholders to strengthen Nigeria’s carbon market framework. Adenikinju said the global carbon market offered opportunities to mobilise climate finance, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and accelerate Nigeria’s transition to a low-carbon economy. He said the proposed criteria would guide project eligibility, institutional responsibilities, measurement, reporting and verification, environmental safeguards, NDC alignment, registry, transparency and carbon accounting. artigo.texto: [ESPAÑOL ABAJO | PORTUGUÊS ABAIXO] Governments across Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) threw their weight behind forest carbon programmes last week in New York City, even as they alluded to a broader range of Article 6 project options. In the world of LAC carbon markets, forest carbon was the star of Climate Week NYC. The Brazilian Minister of the Environment and Climate Change, Joao Capobianco, said he was “very optimistic” that the Tropical Forest Forever Facility (TFFF) a global initiative first backed by Brazil, would hit its $10 billion goal before the year is out. The fund is currently at $7.3 bln, he added. Reaching the target is a condition of Norway’s $3-bln contribution. Meanwhile, representatives from forest-rich LAC countries like Guyana, Ecuador, Bolivia, and Costa Rica joined partner governments like the UK and Norway, bringing attention to carbon markets, public funding, debt-for-swaps, and results-based payment as ways to mobilise finance for forest protection and restoration. “We see it as valuable resources to maintain an asset to save the world, fight climate change,” said Vickram Barrat, Guyana’s natural resources minister, referring to the country’s carbon credit agreement with US oil producer the Hess Corporation. Outside New York, Brazilian nature-based carbon removals (CDR) developer Mombak signed a multi-year offtake agreement with Salesforce. Mombak also launched the Amazon Reforestation Fund II, its second investment vehicle, aiming for $150 million. ARTICLE 6 IN MOTION Climate Week NYC was also abundant in Article 6 teasers and announcements, particularly from Chile, Brazil, and Colombia. Chile was already a LAC frontrunner, having issued several Letters of Authorisation (LoAs) under Article 6.2, as well as transitioned some 30 Kyoto Protocol-era carbon projects to the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM). Despite a transition earlier this year from the left-wing government of former President Gabriel Boric to the administration of far-right leader President Jose Antonio Kast, the country has shown no signs of stopping. Indeed, Cristina Vargas Figueroa, carbon pricing and markets coordinator at Chile’s Ministry of the Environment, expects her country to sign around 17 or 18 LoAs by the end of the year, she said at Climate Week. The country’s existing LoAs cover technology-based emissions reductions and removals, such as electric mobility, battery storage, fuel switching, and biogas. Brazil is also looking to engage Article 6, both through the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM) – to which it is transitioning some 92 projects – and through bilateral cooperative approaches. The environment ministry’s Capobianco noted that Brazil is preparing the requisite domestic regulatory framework needed to participate in Article 6. Capobianco also said Brazil is already in discussions with several interested buyer countries. One of these, sources anticipate, will be China. Alex Saer, CEO of Medellin-based carbon standard Cercarbono, even expects to see Colombia rise to the occasion, he told Carbon Pulse. The REDD+ powerhouse country has long expressed interest in Article 6, without striking any bilateral agreements or issuing regulations. This may soon change, Saer believes. Colombia’s environment ministry is seeking “some quick wins” under the new right-wing administration of President Abelardo De La Espriella, he said. For example, the government is resuming conversations with Singapore on the back of a 2022 memorandum of understanding. ALMOST TIME In Mexico, years of waiting for the full operationalisation of a ‘transitional’ emissions trading system (ETS) are coming to a close. Officials have signalled a definitive launch in 2027, and final decisions are being made. According to Diana Guzman, director of climate change mitigation and adaptation policies at SEMARNAT, the environment ministry, some free allocation of allowances will continue. “A formula was developed very closely with the [private] sectors,” she said on a webinar last week, specifically referencing Mexico’s COCOSCE, the public-private ETS consultative committee. This formula incorporates both a year-dependent emissions projection factor and a free allocation reduction factor, also subject to change on an annual basis. Authorities are still deciding what volume of allowances to auction, and what the preset price floor for these auctions will be. They are also still considering what share of carbon credits should be allowed into the system – likely removing the previous 10% cap. Sanctions for ETS non-compliance are also still under discussion, Guzman said. Proposals have included reducing future free allowances, or else financial penalties. En el mundo de los mercados de carbono de LAC, el carbono forestal fue la estrella de la Climate Week NYC. artigo.texto: Colombia’s newly appointed environment minister on Tuesday announced the revocation of a decree issued by the previous administration that introduced stringent rules for the country’s carbon markets, while signalling plans to remove a cap on the amount of credits allowed to offset the national carbon tax. “Today, I am revoking [ministerial] Decree 0973 … for legal reasons,” Fabio Arjona, head of the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (MADS), said during a panel at the Medellin Climate Week. Decree 0973/26 was issued on the last day of the previous administration, led by former President Gustavo Petro, an open critic of the voluntary carbon market (VCM). Citing social and environmental safeguards, the decree introduced stricter requirements for projects seeking to participate in the VCM, including several evaluation stages through the national RENARE registry – which is not fully operational – and crediting periods. It also established responsibilities for buyers of carbon certificates. Since the draft decree was opened for public consultation in June, several market participants voiced concerns over the rules, warning that they could seriously affect the continuity of the market. Some observers said the decree was too broad and that implementing several of its provisions would be difficult, while others described it as excessively restrictive and, in some cases, contradictory. Read more: FEATURE: Too detailed, too vague – Colombian observers pan VCM regs, for different reasons “From a technical standpoint, it was horrific. It was a depth charge placed under the possibility of a carbon market,” Arjona said in Medellin. Legal experts also told Carbon Pulse that the decree contained several potential procedural flaws, including the lack of prior consultation with all ethnic communities that could be affected by regulation of this scope, given the importance of REDD+ projects to Colombia’s domestic carbon market. The ministry also said in a Tuesday statement that the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and other relevant authorities with competencies did not provide a concept before the decree was published. Even before taking office, Arjona told local media his intention to revoke the decree. At the time of publication, the resolution revoking the decree had not yet been published on the MADS website. However, a source from MADS confirmed to Carbon Pulse that the revocation was already signed and is in publication process. According to a press release, the ministry will “correct the procedure and construct a new regulatory framework”. “We will build the new framework openly, through genuine public consultation and dialogue with the private sector, developers, and buyers. The rules are written with those who operate in the market, not behind their backs,” the minister said. REMOVING THE OFFSETTING CAP Arjona also gave an initial indication that he intends to remove the 50% cap introduced by the Petro administration in 2022 on the carbon tax’s non-causation (Spanish: no causacion) mechanism, which allows liable entities to avoid paying the levy by purchasing domestic carbon credits. “I am also announcing that, for the [National] Development Plan, I am proposing to restore 100% of the non-causation of the carbon tax,” he said in Medellin. In addition to revoking Decree 0973, the minister had also expressed an interest in removing the offsetting cap before taking office, with the aim of restoring demand for local certificates and reviving a market that has been under pressure. While revoking a ministerial regulation falls within the ministry’s powers, several market participants had previously said that restoring the non-causation mechanism to 100% would be more complicated, as the current cap was established through a law – the 2022 tax reform – and amid the government’s tight fiscal position. Minister Arjona will also propose the change in Congress, according to the press release. Proposing the change in Congress and for inclusion in the 2026-30 National Development Plan, the government’s overarching public policy framework which undergoes consultation with several ministries and civil society, would therefore represent a step in that direction. FIRST OFFICIAL SIGNAL Arjona’s comments in Medellin mark the first official signal from MADS on carbon markets under far-right President Abelardo De La Espriella. Officials also recently announced renewed talks with Singapore to revive the Article 6 memorandum of understanding between the two states. De La Espriella’s environmental policy is based on his ‘ABC Agenda: Water, Biodiversity, and Communities’, which takes a more supportive approach to carbon markets than the previous administration. Carbon Pulse learned that, during the presidential election campaign, market advocates presented proposals to the main candidates aimed at reviving demand. Their suggestions were particularly well received by De La Espriella’s team, and several were ultimately included in the ABC Agenda. By Juan Guerrero – [email protected] [ESPAÑOL] Ministro de ambiente de Colombia revoca decreto sobre mercados de carbono, propone devolver la no causación al 100% El recién posesionado ministro de ambiente anunció este martes que revocó el decreto de la anterior administración que establecía nuevas reglas para los mercados de carbono, mientras que propondrá eliminar el tope a las compensaciones permitidas bajo el impuesto al carbono. “Hoy estoy revocando el Decreto [ministerial] 0973 … por temas jurídicos,” Fabio Arjona, cabeza del Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible (MADS), dijo el martes durante un panel en el Medellín Climate Week. El Decreto 0973/26 fue expedido en el último día de la anterior administración, liderada por el presidente de izquierda Gustavo Petro, quien había sido abiertamente crítico del mercado voluntario de carbono (VCM). artigo.texto: Gotion High-Tech teams up with Volkswagen to pour 3.2 billion euros into building a battery factory, securing its entry ticket to the European market, yet the tight carbon footprint shackle has only just been put in place. Gotion High-Tech's joint venture factory in Europe with PowerCo brings opportunities as well as challenges including compliance requirements. Energy Foresight learned that on September 28, Gotion High-Tech and PowerCo, the battery subsidiary of Volkswagen, signed an agreement with a total investment of 3.222 billion euros, under which the two parties will set up three joint ventures in Valencia, Spain, Sulany, Slovakia, and Kenitra, Morocco. The day after the news was released, Gotion High-Tech hit the 10% price limit 8 minutes after the market opened, with pending orders exceeding 890,000 lots. What is worth noting about this matter is not the figures themselves. The global installed capacity of power batteries reaches nearly 1000GWh a year, and the planned production capacity of 37GWh is far from an unprecedented huge investment. What really deserves attention is the structure of this transaction: Gotion will contribute approximately 1.598 billion euros, while PowerCo will contribute approximately 1.624 billion euros, making the contributions of both parties almost equal. In terms of equity arrangement, for the 29.1GWh project in Valencia, PowerCo holds 51% of the shares to take the controlling stake, and Gotion holds 49%; for the 8.4GWh project in Sulany and the 100,000-ton cathode material project in Morocco, Gotion holds 51% of the shares and takes the controlling stake. This is not an ordinary overseas factory construction investment. It is a transaction concerning the access right to the European market. Volkswagen has delivered far more than just a factory The Valencia plant is not a project built from scratch by Gotion. The plant was previously led and promoted by PowerCo. The Spanish government has allocated more than 260 million euros in subsidies to the plant through the PERTEVEC program, of which 152 million euros are cash subsidies that the Valencia joint venture has obtained before this investment. Instead of directly acquiring the plant, Gotion enters the project by capital increase to PowerCoSpain, and participates in subsequent construction and operation. However, the construction progress of the plant has been repeatedly delayed. After years of independent development by PowerCo, the mass production of cells has never been realized. This situation is exactly the same as that of Northvolt. The once highly promising "top battery enterprise" in Europe declared bankruptcy after burning 15 billion U.S. dollars of investment, and the plan for the Heide plant in Germany was once stranded, before it was taken over and promoted by the U.S. company Lyten. According to data from the IEA, Chinese enterprises including CATL, BYD, and CALB control about 80% of the global battery production capacity. European automakers have calculated an account: the comprehensive production cost of large-scale mass-produced power batteries is about 30% higher than that in China, the electricity price is 3 to 5 times that of China, and the hourly wage of workers is 5 times that of China. Volkswagen's choice is very pragmatic. Rather than continuing to burn money in a project that cannot be operated smoothly, it is better to hand over the factory to the party that can make it run properly. The conditions for Gotion to take over are also clear: in exchange for a 49% equity stake, it obtains an existing base that has received government subsidies and is located in the core of Spain's automotive industry cluster. Spain is an important production base of the Volkswagen Group in Europe, and the geographical location of the Valencia plant determines that it serves Volkswagen's vehicle production lines in Southern Europe rather than Gotion's own business. The arrangements for Slovakia and Morocco are the opposite. Gotion holds a 51% controlling stake in these two projects, keeping the key link of cell manufacturing in its own hands, and at the same time using the 100,000-ton lithium iron phosphate cathode material production capacity in Morocco to provide upstream supply for European battery bases. The trade facilitation conditions between Morocco and the European Union itself serve as a buffer to avoid tariff barriers. The EU's carbon footprint rule is a hurdle that Gotion has not yet crossed However, obtaining the factory and equity does not mean getting the passport to enter the European market. The EU's mandatory carbon footprint declaration for energy storage batteries has come into effect on February 18, 2026, and the Digital Battery Passport will be implemented on February 18, 2027. What is more tricky is the design of the accounting rules: only two models, "national average power consumption mix" and "directly connected power", are retained for carbon footprint calculation, and the green certificates commonly purchased by Chinese enterprises are not recognized. This means that even if Gotion uses green power to produce cathode materials in Morocco, the carbon footprint data will still fail to meet the requirements if the power source is not recognized by the EU accounting system. Since August this year, the EU Customs has changed its regulation on the carbon footprint declaration of imported batteries from "pass after declaration" to mandatory random inspection. Several batches of battery products exported from China to the Port of Rotterdam have been detained because their green power certificates do not meet the requirements. Gotion's layout of cathode materials in Morocco and cell manufacturing in Spain and Slovakia follows the correct direction of localized production. However, from the compliance of raw material source codes and power mix factors to mineral due diligence and recycled material proportion, every item requires rebuilding the data system of the supply chain. artigo.texto: More than a third of car buyers reluctantly give up their car purchase plans, simply because there is no battery that meets their expectations. "37.1% of Chinese consumers admit that if their desired vehicle model is not equipped with CATL batteries, they will give up buying this car." In Nielsen IQ's 2026 Global New Energy Vehicle Consumer Research Report, this figure is particularly notable. After tens of thousands of new energy vehicle users and potential customers across the globe completed the survey, power batteries have become a core decision-making factor in car purchases. Nearly 40% of Chinese consumers prioritize CATL when choosing electric vehicles. This scenario is not uncommon in the era of fuel vehicles. People buy Honda for its reliable engine, and choose BMW for its outstanding power performance and handling. Nowadays, people prioritize batteries when buying electric vehicles, and the underlying logic is similar. Batteries are not only the largest part of the total vehicle cost, but also closely related to power performance, handling, safety, and energy replenishment experience. For automakers, batteries determine cost control, safety performance and sales conversion rate; for consumers, batteries represent quality endorsement and the fundamental guarantee of vehicle usage experience. This is not a simple brand preference, but a shift in the value anchor of automobile consumption, which exactly creates new opportunities for China's automobile industry and consumers. Engine = the measurement standard for fuel vehicles, battery = the measurement standard for electric vehicles In the era of fuel vehicles, consumers do not only buy a product with four wheels and two seats. They choose Honda for its engine, BMW for power and handling, and Toyota for its smooth and durable transmission. Engines and transmissions define the character of a fuel vehicle, and are also the core of brand premium. When automakers hold new product conferences, they cannot avoid talking about horsepower, torque, 100-kilometer acceleration time, and transmission gear numbers. Consumers may not fully understand technical terms, but they have a clear judgment in mind: the performance of the engine and the smoothness of the transmission determine whether the car is worth buying. In the new energy era, the core of this logic has been replaced. Electric motors are becoming increasingly homogeneous, electronic control systems can be upgraded via OTA, the cockpit can be equipped with various high-end configurations, and the screen can be made larger and larger. The factor that truly differentiates products is the battery. The battery is no longer just an energy storage component like a fuel tank. It acts as the power source, safety component, cost component, and experience component at the same time. Range, fast charging performance, low-temperature adaptability, service life, safety, and residual value are all related to it. For an electric vehicle, if the battery is poor, no matter how fancy other parts are, the overall product cannot be recognized by the market. Looking deeper, the battery also affects the overall vehicle design. The thickness of the battery pack, energy density, and thermal management capability directly affect the chassis layout, interior space, vehicle weight, and handling performance. Technical routes such as CTP and CTC are widely discussed in the industry precisely because the battery is no longer just a "part to be installed", but participates in the definition of the whole vehicle from the underlying level. Whoever masters the battery will have more power to define the product. Therefore, consumers begin to recognize battery brands just as they recognized engine brands in the past. When buying an electric vehicle, the first question they ask is: Whose battery is it? Is it a CATL battery? Does it mix batteries of different brands? This is not engineer thinking, but a common risk judgment for ordinary people. Batteries account for a high proportion of vehicle cost, and the replacement and maintenance cost is very expensive. Consumers cannot directly test safety, degradation performance, and consistency when purchasing, so what can they do? They can only refer to the brand, see which brand has passed large-scale market verification, and which brand has stable reputation. The most special feature of CATL is that it has developed from a To B company into a consumer-level trusted brand. It is no longer just a supplier, but an "invisible quality guarantee" for electric vehicles. For vehicles with the same price and same model, if the battery section is marked with CATL, half of consumers' concerns will be eliminated. For the same vehicle model equipped with different battery brands, it is equivalent to two completely different powertrains in the eyes of users. At the same price, when CATL batteries are placed together with other batteries, most consumers will choose the former. Once this perception is formed, it is difficult to reverse. Three thresholds for becoming a "consumer brand" If you run an automobile company or a mobile phone company, it is not rare to make your brand known to almost every household, because these brands are "consumer brands", which is "To C", "to customers", facing end consumers. But if you operate a component supplier, which is "To B (To Business)" facing the industry, and you can still be promoted to a "consumer brand", that is a real achievement, which means your product development and brand building have reached a very high level. In the consumer electronics field, the most typical example is Intel. The "Intel Inside" label back then even made Huawei, which entered the automotive industry decades later, admire and follow this marketing strategy. There are also Bosch's auto parts, Huawei's automotive components and communication equipment, all of which have achieved significant influence among consumer groups. artigo.texto: Zhang Yuegang, Professor of Tsinghua University: Solid-state batteries are stuck at the "two interfaces", while lithium metal batteries are trying to bypass this hurdle | Frontline Solid-state batteries are not necessarily the only answer for next-generation lithium batteries. Recently, at the 2026 Lithium Metal Battery Frontier Forum (LMBF 2026) held in Beijing, 36Kr had an exchange with Zhang Yuegang, the forum chairman and tenured professor at Tsinghua University. In the past few years, solid-state batteries have almost become one of the most popular technical directions in the power battery industry. However, in Zhang Yuegang's view, the industry first needs to clarify a basic concept: solid-state batteries and lithium metal batteries are not two technical generations that can be directly compared in the first place. The reason is that the two belong to different classification dimensions. The energy density of batteries is mainly determined by cathode and anode materials. The cathode can be lithium iron phosphate, high-nickel ternary, lithium-rich manganese-based or even sulfur, while the anode has evolved from graphite to silicon-carbon and lithium metal; the so-called solid state and liquid state distinguish the form of electrolyte. In other words, solid-state batteries change the electrolyte, while lithium metal batteries change the anode. It is still the cathode and anode that fundamentally determine how much energy a battery can store. Therefore, lithium metal anode batteries are also a key evolutionary branch of next-generation battery technology. In Zhang Yuegang's view, the currently booming solid-state battery route in the industry still has a number of material technical difficulties to overcome. As introduced, Zhang Yuegang is a tenured professor at Tsinghua University, an internationally renowned materials scientist with more than 30 years of experience in materials research at home and abroad. He has successively worked at the Nippon Electric Basic Research Institute, Stanford University in the United States, Intel, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Chinese Academy of Sciences and other institutions, and has achieved a number of important research results in the fields of nanomaterials, energy storage technology and other fields. Solid-state batteries are stuck at two "interfaces" The most attractive part of solid-state batteries for the industry is that they use solid electrolyte to replace flammable organic liquid electrolyte, so as to apply more cutting-edge cathode and anode materials and push the energy density up to the 500Wh/kg level. However, the interface problem of solid electrolyte still plagues the industry today, and Zhang Yuegang explained these difficulties in detail to 36Kr. Zhang Yuegang believes that the core problems can actually be attributed to two "interfaces". The first is the microscopic interface inside the cathode. The battery cathode is not a whole dense material, but composed of a large number of particles, with a large number of nano-scale pores inside. Liquid electrolyte can penetrate into these tiny spaces like water and fully contact with the cathode material; but solid electrolyte can hardly do this. If more solid electrolyte is added to improve ion transmission, it will take up the space of active materials that actually store energy, and eventually drag down the energy density of the whole battery. The second problem is the interface between the anode and the solid electrolyte as well as the lithium dendrite problem. A common judgment in the past was that solid electrolyte has higher mechanical strength and can physically block lithium dendrites. However, Zhang Yuegang believes that after more than ten years of research, various solid electrolytes still do not truly solve this problem at present. Solid materials naturally have microscopic defects, along which lithium will continue to grow. Once a penetration channel is formed, it may even quickly lead to internal short circuit. In addition, unlike liquids, solids cannot be fully wetted with each other, which is essentially closer to "point contact". In order to reduce the interface impedance, it is necessary to increase the proportion of electrolyte and the working pressure, but this contradicts the goal of improving energy density. Therefore, another evolutionary idea for the next generation of battery technology is to temporarily retain the liquid electrolyte and replace the anode with lithium metal first. The biggest obstacle for this route in the past was also lithium dendrites. It is difficult for lithium to always remain absolutely flat during the repeated deposition process, and it will gradually grow a structure similar to branches. Once the dendrites continue to grow and pierce the separator, it may cause an internal short circuit. Zhang Yuegang introduced that an important solution idea at present is to use additives in the liquid electrolyte to form a SEI protective film on the surface of lithium metal. When cracks appear in this film during the charging and discharging process, the additives can continue to react to dynamically repair the damaged area. In this way, dendrites can be controlled at the micron scale, which greatly reduces the risk of short circuit caused by their continuous growth. But the cost is also obvious: the continuous damage and repair of the SEI film means that the electrolyte will be continuously consumed. According to the progress given by Zhang Yuegang, relevant lithium metal batteries can now achieve hundreds of cycles, some high-specific-energy products at the 500Wh/kg level have exceeded 300 cycles, and products at the 400Wh/kg level can reach 600 cycles, but there is still a gap from the thousands of cycles generally required by new energy vehicles. The first batch of lithium metal batteries may "fly to the sky" first Zhang Yuegang judges that the more realistic commercialization path for lithium metal batteries is to enter drones and eVTOL
