artigo.texto: NineDot Energy has cut the ribbon on its largest battery energy storage system (BESS), a 19.6MW/78.3MWh development in Hunts Point, the Bronx, New York. The company said the system would be fully operational in time for summer 2027, when it will supply power during periods of peak demand and support the local Con Edison distribution grid. NYSERDA records show the development comprises four 4.896MW/19.584MWh lithium-ion systems on adjoining Casanova Street sites. The records identify CATL as the cell manufacturer and list combined state incentives of $9.8 million. NineDot itself has not announced the project’s capacity The company’s announcement did not disclose the project’s energy capacity, battery supplier or cost. Its website continued to list the Casanova project as under construction following the ribbon-cutting. Adam Cohen, co-founder and chief technology officer at NineDot Energy, said: “Hunts Point has historically been overburdened by high-emitting fossil fuels, and this battery storage facility marks an inflection point in improving the local environment and grid reliability.” The project occupies the former site of a fuel-oil trucking business. NineDot said the battery could help reduce dependence on nearby fossil-fuel peaking plants as electricity demand grows from the planned electrification of Hunts Point’s produce and fish markets and its commercial vehicle fleet. The developer has 11 operating projects totalling 39MW across six locations in Staten Island and the Bronx. It is targeting 400MW of storage in operation, under construction or in development by the end of 2026, with more than 60 additional projects and a development pipeline exceeding 1GW. NineDot’s nine operating battery projects exported almost 34MW during New York’s heatwave of 1–4 July 2026, according to the company. Photo: NineDot Energy and local representatives at the ribbon-cutting for the company’s Hunts Point battery storage development in the Bronx Credit: NineDot Energy

artigo.texto: A startup whose founder has vowed to "make nuclear great again" is planning to place hundreds of reactors on federal land in Utah, according to documents reviewed by NPR. Valar Atomics is planning what it calls "Project Beehive" on over 9,000 acres of land held under the Bureau of Land Management near Price, Utah. The facility would include data centers and some 456 small nuclear reactors, along with a facility to produce nuclear fuel and others for storing nuclear waste, according to a proposal from the company to federal regulators. In aggregate, the reactors would produce around 9.6 gigawatts of power for the data centers and even more thermal heat for other industrial applications. Currently, the entire state of Utah produces only around 4 gigawatts of electricity on average (though its peak capacity in summer can reach around 10 gigawatts). The project's timeline calls for nonnuclear construction to begin as soon as the end of this year, with the first reactors coming online sometime in 2028. Valar has also sought the use of around 650 acres of state land as part of the same project, according to state records. The Salt Lake Tribune first reported on the project's use of state land last week, but not the much larger proposed use of federal lands. The project has raised alarm among local activists, who are already facing a slew of data center proposals in the state. "It's concerning to see that the Trump administration, with the support of the state of Utah, is pushing this forward on significant acreage of public lands," said Neal Clark, wildlands director at the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance, a Utah-based nonprofit that seeks to protect public lands. "The coalition of people who are concerned about these things completely transcends political lines," added Lexi Tuddenham, the executive director of the Healthy Environment Alliance of Utah, which has tracked nuclear-related industries in the state. Tuddenham said that at the moment her primary goal is to raise awareness. "The biggest thing we can do right now is to let people know about it." In a written statement, the Bureau of Land Management's Utah office confirmed it had received an application from the company. "We are currently reviewing the application for completeness," it told NPR in an email. As the application moves through the required National Environmental Policy Act process, "we will make sure the public has meaningful opportunities to provide input," it added. Valar did not immediately respond to NPR's request for comment. In an interview with NPR in July, Valar CEO Isaiah Taylor said his company was committed to safety and community engagement. "We're doing it responsibly and accountably to this community," he said of a smaller test reactor that the company was operating in a neighboring county. Small reactors, big plan Project Beehive reveals the scale of the ambitions held by a new generation of companies planning a comeback for nuclear power. The companies are backed by the Trump administration, which has enacted a slew of regulatory reforms over the past year and a half to make their "small modular reactors" easier to test and build. Valar has been both closely involved with those reforms and a beneficiary of them. Taylor was in the room when President Trump signed a series of executive orders last year designed to accelerate the development of nuclear power, and his company was accepted into the Department of Energy's Reactor Pilot Program in August 2025. This past February, the U.S. military flew Valar's test reactor from California to Utah aboard a C-17 transport aircraft. The reactor, known as Ward 250, received rapid approval this year after the Department of Energy conducted a quiet overhaul of its internal safety and security regulations for nuclear reactors. It achieved criticality by reaching a self-sustaining nuclear reaction in June, in a tentlike structure in the Utah desert about 30 miles from the site of Project Beehive. At a press event on July 1, the company marked another milestone when it used Ward 250 to produce electricity. Taylor powered up the test reactor and used a simple thermoelectric system to run a single Nvidia microchip. "Ladies and gentlemen, Valar Atomics just became the first startup in history to make nuclear electricity right here," he told the crowd. The scale of Project Beehive vastly outstrips that July demonstration. Since the turn of the century, the U.S. has switched on just three new nuclear power plants, producing a total of around 3.4 gigawatts of electricity. Those reactors are far larger than the small modular reactors that Valar plans to use, and each costs many billions of dollars to build. Valar and other companies are hoping to upend the nuclear business model because small reactors can be mass-produced and placed in series, like a set of nuclear batteries. Valar's 25-megawatt electric units could be installed one at a time, allowing Project Beehive to be built in phases over a number of years. That in turn would reduce the cost and allow the site to enter operation relatively quickly. According to a document reviewed by NPR, the full site could be completed by 2032. Tuddenham said she thinks the use of federal lands for such a project is unprecedented. "In this case, I think it's bigger than the local community," she said. "If we have facilities like this on public land for waste storage, for massive nuclear development, for data centers, that's going to have tremendous implications for how public lands are used." NPR's Shannon Bond contributed to this report. Contact Geoff Brumfiel on Signal at gbrumfiel.13 Copyright 2026 NPR Loading...

artigo.texto: Data center developers, investors, and communities across California face a changing development landscape as new requirements impact some of the industry’s most consequential land use and infrastructure issues. Governor Gavin Newsom signed a package of seven bills (AB 1577 – Bauer-Kahan; AB 2383 – Zbur; AB 2469 – Papan; AB 2619 – Papan; SB 886 – Padilla and McNerney; SB 887 – Padilla; SB 1168 – McNerney) on September 21 addressing the electricity, water, and environmental impacts of data centers. The new laws impose additional reporting requirements, address responsibility for electric grid and water infrastructure costs, and establish conditions data center projects must meet to qualify for streamlined judicial review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). But the significance for developers extends beyond the individual requirements contained in the legislation. At the state level, California is establishing a framework seeking to address questions about power capacity, water supply, infrastructure, environmental review, and community impacts. At the same time, various cities and counties are taking their own approaches to data center development, creating a patchwork of local regulatory landscapes that can vary considerably from one jurisdiction to another. The result is an increasingly complicated development environment. While a site may appear suitable from a real estate or engineering perspective, depending on the local rules, the entitlement process can vary from straightforward to incredibly complex. Two near-identical sites in different locations may face entirely dissimilar entitlement paths depending on the jurisdiction’s rules, available infrastructure, and local response to data center development. Early diligence is thus key to a successful data center project. According to the state, the legislative package is intended to provide communities with more information about proposed projects while protecting utility customers from costs associated with data center growth. Specifically, the seven bills address data centers through three closely related areas: electricity, water, and environmental impacts. On electricity, the legislation addresses grid upgrade costs, energy procurement, and rate structures. The state says the new laws are intended to prevent costs associated with serving data centers from being shifted to other ratepayers, and the laws require projects to pay for necessary grid upgrades and comply with California energy procurement requirements. For water, proposed data centers must provide information to local governments and water suppliers about water use, supply, efficiency, and drought planning, and the projects will be responsible for upgrades needed to provide water service. Regarding environmental review, the legislation clarifies that data centers are not categorically exempt from CEQA. At the same time, the legislation also allows for expedited judicial review for qualifying data centers that meet certain environmental requirements. Projects must demonstrate that they meet state standards involving energy, water, and fuel consumption and will not shift costs to ratepayers before qualifying for that treatment. For developers, the new legislation means that infrastructure planning must become part of site selection and entitlement strategy early in the process. For example, data centers are energy-intensive, with the largest data centers typically including onsite power generation. However, proper energy planning also requires understanding available natural gas supplies, grid connectivity requirements with the local power provider, if desired, and a host of related regulatory requirements. California’s new framework is intended to prevent data center costs from being shifted to other ratepayers, meaning that when deciding whether a project is feasible, developers must consider all aspects of energy costs and availability early in the planning process. Water presents a similar issue. The new disclosure requirements mean that developers should be prepared to address anticipated water use and its relationship to local supply, efficiency, and drought planning. For developers evaluating competing sites, the relevant questions extend beyond whether water service exists. The availability and reliability of that supply, anticipated demand, and cost of necessary improvements may all affect project feasibility. CEQA adds another layer. The new legislation makes clear that developers should be prepared to engage in robust environmental review for virtually all data center projects, and that the potential for streamlined judicial review is deeply intertwined with questions about energy, water, fuel consumption, and infrastructure costs. Taken together, the laws reinforce a broader trend in data center development: data centers are no longer primarily a technology issue. They involve significant land use and infrastructure issues, with decisions about where and how facilities are developed increasingly tied to the capacity and priorities of the communities around them. Thus, California’s new laws make it clear that infrastructure and land use analysis should not be treated as separate tracks. They increasingly need to inform one another early in the strategy process. The new state laws establish a broader framework, but they do not create a uniform entitlement process across California. Developers must still navigate the land use requirements of the city or county in which a project is proposed. That local landscape is evolving rapidly. Some jurisdictions are reconsidering how, where, and even if data centers should be permitted, while others are continuing to process projects under existing rules. For a developer, that means statewide compliance is only one part of the regulatory analysis. artigo.texto: Sauk Rapids Reaches Agreement On NextEra Battery Facility, Accepts Limited Local Control SAUK RAPIDS (WJON News) -- The Sauk Rapids City Council has reluctantly approved a development agreement for a proposed battery storage facility. Monday night, the council voted 3-2 in favor of the agreement worked out between city staff and Mayhew Lake Energy Storage LLC, a NextEra Energy Resources company. All five council members are opposed to the project's location, but three members decided any agreement is better than no agreement at all. Under Minnesota law, the authority for the project rests solely with the Public Utilities Commission, and the city has limited authority over the project. Mayor Jason Ellering says the proposed battery energy storage facility would sit on prime land for city growth. It's smack dab in the middle of a significant development corridor for the city as we continue to grow. What the next 30 years look like for the city, I think that it is important to take that into consideration. What the property is going to look like, it'll be there indefinitely. The city council previously approved two objection letters to the PUC outlining the city's concerns with the proposed location. With the approval of the development agreement, the city will rescind the letter to the PUC citing its opposition to the project. Sauk Rapids City Attorney Adam Ripple says the agreement is an attempt to make lemonade out of lemons and to mitigate the impact on the city if the project moves forward. artigo.texto: Round Up: commissioners back two school grant bids, set data center moratorium hearing Davidson County commissioners voted this week to support grant applications for new high school buildings in both Lexington and Thomasville, and agreed to schedule an Oct. 26 public hearing on a temporary moratorium on data centers, in a meeting that ran more than three hours and included heated public comment. Lexington High School The board's longest discussion centered on Lexington City Schools' application to the state's Needs-Based Public School Capital Fund for a new Lexington Senior High School. The application is due Oct. 2. Lexington City Schools Superintendent Dr. Ron Anthony told commissioners the school, described by speakers as 73 years old and the oldest school building in the county, has water intrusion, aging systems, structural settlement, and accessibility and life-safety deficiencies. He presented three options: limited repairs at $15.5 million, a $58 million renovation, or new construction that would use a county match of about $41 million to unlock roughly $62 million in state funding. Anthony said the school has the third-highest performance data in Davidson County and is rated a B school, arguing that students are succeeding despite the building. The district says Lexington Senior High earned its first B under the state's school performance grades in the latest results, with a graduation rate of 91.7%. Anthony did not specify which schools the county comparison covers, and the claim could not be independently verified. Outside rankings are less favorable: U.S. News ranks the school 410th among 604 ranked high schools in North Carolina, and the nonprofit GreatSchools gives it a 3 out of 10 rating. Anthony also noted that the school's auditorium serves as a community emergency shelter. Lexington City Board of Education Chair Angela Mcduffie told commissioners that renovation "band-aids" are no longer responsible. A commissioner who is a former teacher cited leaking ceilings, buckling floors and barriers under the Americans with Disabilities Act. Commissioners spent considerable time on how to pay for the local share. Commissioners discussed a worst-case scenario for a $104 million project, in which the county would need to borrow about $15 million after applying lottery funds, existing capital money and a possible $10 million transfer from dredging funds. They noted that upcoming debt relief from the Oak Grove project could help support that borrowing. One commissioner put the county's requested contribution at $41,255,567. The county attorney, Adam Jones, cautioned that approving the application "as written" effectively certifies that the county has the required local funding available, which could commit it to the full project cost and roughly $42 million in local money. Project architect Miki Keller said the state's main focus is the match tied to the $62 million grant, about $15.5 million in local funds, and that the firm would reduce scope if costs change. Anthony said he would work with the architect within 48 hours to propose cuts, and he was willing to negotiate on a reduced estimate of about $90 million to $95 million. Commissioners clarified that the vote authorizes applying for the grant rather than approving construction, and they voted to approve the application. Thomasville High School Commissioners then approved Thomasville City Schools' application in about six minutes. Rodney Shotwell said the building scope of the revised proposal is intact but planned athletic upgrades and some renovations were cut. The plan requests $15.5 million in local funds to complete a $77.5 million new school. Shotwell also described severe problems at a closed career-technical building and the need for a $1.2 million infrastructure project. Commissioners said that if neither district wins a grant, they would revert to existing allocations and revisit renovation funding for Thomasville High and other schools. Data center moratorium The board voted 4-2 to schedule an Oct. 26 public hearing on a temporary moratorium on data centers. The vote did not adopt the moratorium itself, Jones stressed. A four-month moratorium was discussed. Supporters said a pause would give time to study impacts, gather citizen input, and let planning staffer Lee Crook finish a zoning text amendment for data centers. One commissioner said the county has no specific data center regulations and argued a pause would also give state and federal officials a chance to explain policies they have promoted without answering local questions. Another commissioner said a moratorium would allow time to design plans in which large data center investments could fund schools and reduce property taxes for long-term residents and seniors. Shell said commissioners already have authority to scrutinize applications and worried a moratorium could delay an acceptable project midstream, "handcuffing" future boards. One commissioner initially described the moratorium as sending an anti-business signal before saying the commissioner supported it as a pause. Planning and Zoning Director Lee Crook said regulatory work can continue during a moratorium and that private land sales to data centers cannot be blocked but would be subject to any adopted regulations. Jones warned that adopting a moratorium and a new ordinance simultaneously would undermine the moratorium's purpose. Jones and Hiller said the county cannot offer targeted tax relief without state legislation, though Cabarrus County uses economic development incentives to fund such programs. During the discussion, Shell told a member of the audience to "shut up" after a tense exchange, and other officials called for decorum. Shell later apologized. artigo.texto: O Atlético-MG fechou uma parceria na área de data center com a Huawei. A empresa chinesa será fornecedora de servidores, soluções de armazenamento de dados e sistemas de backup para a Arena MRV, estádio do clube mineiro, em Belo Horizonte. O contrato é de cinco anos e a instalação da infraestrutura de dados está prevista para começar em novembro. A implantação e o acompanhamento da operação serão feitos pela SYX-AI, integradora parceira tecnológica da Huawei no Brasil. O clube informou que, a partir desse contrato, a Arena MRV passará a operar integralmente com tecnologia da Huawei na área de infraestrutura de dados. Como parte do acordo, o vice-presidente de Negócios do Atlético-MG, Márcio Freire, e o diretor de Tecnologia, Leandro Evangelista, visitaram instalações da fornecedora na China. Com base na experiência, os executivos indicam que, nos próximos anos, soluções de Inteligência Artificial (IA) podem ser incorporadas à operação do estádio, como para monitoramento do público que frequenta os jogos de futebol. Segundo o Atlético-MG, além da infraestrutura tecnológica, a parceria poderá ser estendida para atividades relacionadas ao futebol, como análise de desempenho, dados e scouting. "Estamos sempre nos atualizando, e a Huawei está muito à frente no que se refere à tecnologia. Ficamos muito satisfeitos com essa oportunidade. Foi um momento de conhecer as estruturas da Huawei, as cidades, entender o que eles estão realizando e avaliar como podemos agregar essas tecnologias ao futebol e à Arena MRV", afirma Evangelista, em nota.

artigo.texto: WEG investe R$ 330 mi em fábrica de baterias A WEG, multinacional catarinense do setor eletroeletrônico, anunciou nesta sexta-feira (25) a ampliação do projeto de sua nova fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, denominado BESS, em construção em Itajaí, no Litoral Norte de Santa Catarina. O investimento total foi elevado para R$ 330 milhões, consolidando a aposta da companhia no mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil. A decisão ocorre em um momento estratégico, às vésperas do primeiro Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade de Armazenamento Nacional, previsto para dezembro de 2026. A empresa destacou que a ampliação do projeto da planta em Itajaí faz parte da estratégia da companhia de apoiar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil. O movimento reflete a confiança da WEG na expansão da demanda por soluções que integrem fontes renováveis à matriz elétrica, um desafio crescente para o setor energético nacional. Investimento reforça aposta em armazenamento O novo aporte eleva o compromisso financeiro da WEG com a unidade fabril, que já estava em construção. A atualização do projeto incorpora maior nível de automação e ganhos de eficiência industrial, o que permitirá ampliar a capacidade produtiva da planta. Com isso, a companhia busca se posicionar de forma competitiva para atender à demanda projetada pelo leilão de reserva de capacidade e por outros segmentos do mercado. O BESS (Battery Energy Storage System, ou Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias) é uma tecnologia essencial para os sistemas elétricos modernos. Ele permite armazenar energia nos momentos de maior disponibilidade — como em dias ensolarados ou com ventos fortes — e disponibilizá-la quando a geração é insuficiente ou a demanda é alta. Essa flexibilidade contribui para a estabilidade do sistema elétrico, maior eficiência operacional e melhor aproveitamento dos recursos energéticos. A decisão da WEG de ampliar o projeto também sinaliza uma leitura positiva do ambiente regulatório brasileiro. O Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade de Armazenamento, marcado para dezembro de 2026, é apontado como um marco para o setor, pois deve criar um mercado formal para sistemas de armazenamento em larga escala. A empresa, no entanto, não detalhou projeções de receita ou participação esperada nesse certame. Impacto para a indústria e comércio Para empresários e comerciantes do interior paulista, o movimento da WEG pode ter reflexos indiretos relevantes. A expansão da capacidade produtiva de baterias tende a impulsionar a cadeia de fornecedores de componentes eletrônicos, serviços de engenharia e logística, gerando oportunidades de negócios para pequenas e médias empresas. Além disso, a consolidação do armazenamento de energia pode reduzir custos operacionais para indústrias e comércios que buscam maior previsibilidade no fornecimento elétrico. Especialistas do setor apontam que o armazenamento em baterias é peça-chave para a integração de fontes renováveis, como solar e eólica, que são intermitentes por natureza. Com sistemas BESS, empresas podem armazenar energia excedente gerada em horários de pico de produção e utilizá-la em momentos de tarifas mais altas, otimizando a conta de luz. Esse benefício é especialmente atrativo para o agronegócio e a indústria de transformação, segmentos fortes na região noroeste paulista. A WEG não divulgou cronograma atualizado para a conclusão das obras da fábrica em Itajaí, tampouco a capacidade produtiva final após a ampliação. A fonte não detalhou se haverá geração de empregos diretos adicionais em decorrência do novo investimento. No entanto, a elevação do aporte sugere um compromisso de longo prazo com a produção local de sistemas de armazenamento, o que pode fortalecer a competitividade da indústria nacional no setor. Contexto do leilão de reserva O primeiro Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade de Armazenamento Nacional, previsto para dezembro de 2026, é aguardado como um divisor de águas para o mercado de baterias no Brasil. O certame deverá contratar potência e energia de sistemas de armazenamento, criando um fluxo de receita previsível para os investidores. A WEG, ao ampliar sua fábrica antes do leilão, demonstra intenção de participar ativamente desse novo mercado. Para as empresas do interior paulista, o leilão pode abrir espaço para projetos de armazenamento associados a usinas solares e eólicas, muitos deles localizados no estado de São Paulo. A redução de custos de baterias, impulsionada pela produção local, pode viabilizar sistemas de menor porte para comércios e indústrias, ampliando o acesso a essa tecnologia. A fonte não detalhou, porém, se a WEG pretende comercializar soluções BESS diretamente para o varejo ou apenas para grandes geradores e utilities. Em resumo, o aumento do investimento da WEG em sua fábrica de baterias em Itajaí reforça a tendência de crescimento do armazenamento de energia no Brasil. A iniciativa deve gerar efeitos positivos na cadeia produtiva e abrir novas oportunidades para negócios que dependem de energia confiável e de custo competitivo. Perguntas Frequentes Qual é o valor do investimento da WEG na megafábrica de baterias em Santa Catarina? A WEG elevou o investimento para R$ 330 milhões na megafábrica de baterias em Itajaí, Santa Catarina. Onde a WEG está construindo sua nova fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias? A nova fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, chamada BESS, está em construção em Itajaí, no Litoral Norte de Santa Catarina. Qual é o papel do BESS nos sistemas elétricos modernos, segundo a WEG? O BESS permite armazenar energia nos momentos de maior disponibilidade e disponibilizá-la quando necessário, contribuindo para a estabilidade do sistema elétrico, maior eficiência operacional e aproveitamento dos recursos energéticos, especialmente na integração de fontes renováveis como solar e eólica.

artigo.texto: NH Investment & Securities Signs Carbon Credit Cooperation Agreement with Trinity Aviation for Domestic and International Markets Cooperation in Supplying CORSIA Credits and Consignment Trading of Domestic Emission Permits Collaborating to Support Airlines Responding to Carbon Regulations NH Investment & Securities and Trinity Aviation signed a carbon market business agreement on the 21st at Trinity Aviation headquarters located in Gangseo-gu, Seoul. After the signing ceremony, Gunhoo Park, Head of Client Solutions Division at NH Investment & Securities (right), and Dongbin Seo, Executive Director of Management Support at Trinity Aviation (left), took a commemorative photo. Photo by NH Investment & Securities View original image NH Investment & Securities announced on September 28 that it had signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Trinity Aviation on September 21 for "mutual cooperation concerning the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and the Emissions Trading Scheme for greenhouse gases." This agreement marks the first case in which a domestic securities firm and an airline company have established a strategic partnership encompassing the supply of CORSIA credits and consignment trading of domestic greenhouse gas emission permits. Trinity Aviation plans to align with the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport’s aviation sector carbon reduction policy and the implementation direction of CORSIA, by linking NH Investment & Securities’ expertise in the carbon market and financial capacity to its own needs for procurement of emission permits. The company emphasized that the significance of this MOU lies in connecting airlines’ acquisition of emission credits and cost management for procurement to the specialized services of a financial institution. Purchasing emission credits requires not only consideration of the necessary quantity and timing, but also a careful review of market prices and trading conditions. Both companies will collaborate to establish stable and efficient procurement plans based on demand information and market analysis. As part of the collaboration, Trinity Aviation will first secure 20,000 tons of CORSIA credits through NH Investment & Securities, and plans to obtain at least 10% of the emissions that need to be offset, in stages, before the Phase 1 settlement deadline in January 2028. The two companies will use this transaction as a starting point for cooperating on CORSIA credit supply, sharing information such as projected mandatory quantity and procurement timing to strengthen the foundation for mid- to long-term procurement. The companies will also cooperate on establishing and operating a consignment trading framework for the domestic Emissions Trading Scheme (K-ETS). NH Investment & Securities will support Trinity Aviation’s smooth trading of carbon credits through its proprietary consignment trading system for emission permits, and provide specialized information on market analysis and policy trends. As a result, Trinity Aviation will be able to establish a systematic support system that covers both domestic emissions trading and procurement of CORSIA credits. Gunhoo Park, Head of Client Solutions Division at NH Investment & Securities, stated, "This agreement is meaningful as a strategic collaboration model that connects a securities company’s expertise in carbon finance with the real emission credit needs of airlines. We will support airlines’ stable acquisition of emission credits based on the supply of CORSIA credits and consignment trading of domestic credits, and expand customized carbon finance services that help respond to procurement costs and market fluctuations." artigo.texto: BYD unveils its first heavy-duty electric semi and it packs 1,000HP, charges in 20 minutes and carries a huge battery warranty Published on Sep 27, 2026 at 6:04 PM (UTC+4) by Ben Thompson Last updated on Sep 27, 2026 at 6:04 PM (UTC+4) Edited by Mason Jones BYD has unveiled its first heavy-duty electric semi, and it can be charged in 20 minutes. And that’s not the only impressive stat attached to the ET44. Capable of hauling 44-ton combinations and packing 1,000HP, there’s no questioning the power of this new offering from BYD. It’s enough to make us ask – should Tesla be worried? How BYD is on the rise If you’ve spent any length of time reading automotive news these past few years, the rip-roaring success of BYD won’t have passed you by. The Chinese carmaker has been flexing on its competitors for a long while now, whether it’s charging EVs in freezing cold temperatures or getting its SUVs to drive on three wheels. And that’s not forgetting their sales figures, which have been soaring around the world, from South America to Australia. With their back-to-back successes, it’d only make sense that the company would be looking to expand. And what better way to take on its primary rival – Tesla – than by putting out a semi truck? As you will undoubtedly know, the Tesla Semi has been making headlines all over the place, whether it’s being driven by Jay Leno or generating buzz for the weight of its battery. But after all that, is it about to get upstaged by the ET44? Let’s take a closer look. The ET44 is a heavy-duty semi to be reckoned with BYD has said the ET44 is capable of hauling a full 44-ton combination. It can’t be a coincidence that this is the maximum payload allowed on European roads. It also surely can’t be a coincidence that this is four tons more than what the Tesla Semi is capable of. Powered by an LFP Blade Battery, the ET44 can reach a peak power of 735kW (just under 1,000HP). It’s not just in physical capabilities that this semi poses a threat to Tesla – it’s also expected to be cheaper. It’s anticipated to arrive in Europe by 2027, with expansion in Canada, Australia, and the UK likely to follow. But it’s not such a clear-cut clean sweep for the ET44, as noted by YouTuber The Electric Viking. “[The Tesla Semi] charges at up to 1.2 megawatt with 548 or 822 kWh packs. So [BYD] has the charging edge and Tesla clearly has the bigger battery and will get significantly more range,” he explained. “The headline here is BYD’s own megawatt chargers. This truck pulls more than 1.5 megawatt and goes from 20 to 80% in about 20 minutes. So, it’s the fastest charging truck. “The real story here though, is BYD turning up with the truck, the battery, the megawatt charger, and the financing all under the same roof. Every other truck maker is waiting on someone else to build the chargers.” When asked whether he thought the ET44 posed a threat to the Tesla Semi, he gave a nuanced answer. “The short answer is that the ETT44 is the first serious competitor the Tesla Semi has faced in Europe and no threat at all in America — and even in Europe I expect the Semi to sell better. Tariffs decide the American half of that before the trucks do,” Sam Evans, The Electric Viking, told Supercar Blondie. “The ETT44 is a brand-new truck with no track record anywhere, no European factory named, and no customer deliveries until the second quarter of 2027. “Add the fact that the Semi enters Europe duty-free and BYD’s truck doesn’t, and I expect the Tesla Semi to outsell the ETT44 in Europe, not the other way round. “What BYD has really done is give Tesla its first proper competitor — a cheaper truck with a longer warranty and a one-stop package — and that will keep Tesla’s European pricing honest. “That’s good for every haulier in Europe, but it doesn’t make the ETT44 the better truck.” Timeline of BYD 1995: Founded by Wang Chuanfu with 20 employees, initially manufacturing nickel-cadmium batteries to compete with Japanese suppliers. 2000 – 2002: Becomes China’s first lithium-ion battery supplier to Motorola and Nokia. The company is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. 2003: Acquires Xi’an Tsinchuan Auto, to pair its battery technology with vehicle manufacturing. 2005: Releases its first mass-produced ICE vehicle, the F3 2008: First plug-in hybrid, the F3DM, is launched. 2013 – 2015: Introduces the ‘Dynasty’ line of plug-in hybrid and electric vehicles. 2022: The company stops producing ICE vehicles to focus on BEVs and PHEVs, while launching global expansion across Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. 2023 – 2024: Surpasses 3 million NEV sales and overtakes Tesla in quarterly global pure-EV sales. 2025 – 2026: Expands further, opening manufacturing hubs across Brazil, Thailand, and Europe. Ben joined Supercar Blondie in February 2025 after being published by international organizations including LADbible, The Sun, the New York Post, and the Daily Mail. He covers supercars, rare and collectible vehicles, aviation, luxury assets, and the fascinating people behind them. His reporting has explored everything from seven-figure supercars and historic Ferrari collections to unusual aircraft adventures and extraordinary automotive discoveries from around the world. Ben has also gained first-hand insight into vehicle craftsmanship and customization, including visiting specialist workshops to see bespoke vehicles up close.

A expansão faz parte da estratégia da WEG de acompanhar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil, em um momento de preparação para o primeiro Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade de Armazenamento, previsto para dezembro de 2026. Com a atualização, o projeto passa a incorporar maior nível de automação e ganhos de eficiência industrial, que, segundo a companhia, permitirão ampliar a capacidade produtiva da unidade. A WEG aponta o avanço das fontes renováveis e a necessidade de maior flexibilidade e segurança para o sistema elétrico como fatores que vêm impulsionando a demanda por soluções de armazenamento no país. “O mercado de armazenamento de energia vive um momento de forte expansão, impulsionado pelo crescimento das fontes renováveis e pela necessidade crescente de maior flexibilidade e segurança para o sistema elétrico”, afirmou Manfred Peter Johann, vice-presidente de Automação e Sistemas da WEG. “A ampliação deste projeto demonstra a capacidade da WEG de adaptar rapidamente seus investimentos para atender às necessidades do mercado e apoiar o desenvolvimento sustentável do setor energético brasileiro”, concluiu Johann. artigo.texto: A brief stop-work order was issued and then retracted for construction on the DC BLOX Thunderbird data center on Sept. 11 and 12. The order was issued after a nearby resident reported heavy machinery and work starting on the site without a posted permit. After an inspection, work was allowed to continue on the site under a drainage permit, which is required to be visibly posted on the site. While the construction continues, there are still concerns from some community members about the presence of private security and local police near the site. Frustrations have continued to rise after a lack of communication from DC BLOX. Megan Lapa is a member of Eastside Community Action (ECA), which has been organizing against the data center since it was proposed in July. “It’s the audacity of it,” Lapa said. “They want to come here and build this project, but they’re not telling us anything beyond what they’re required to. They’re not listening to our concerns or what we’re saying.” ECA has filed a petition for judicial review of the variance of use the Metropolitan Development Commission approved for development of the site. The petition says that the request did not adequately meet the requirements for a variance of use of a site zoned Industrial 3. “[The] goal is to get this [land] in the hands of the community,” Lapa said. “Whether that’s for a different industrial development or whatever it may be, we want to be able to have some [community input].” While the ECA has expressed its dislike of the project, some Butler students are experiencing the same issue in their own communities. Sophia McKinley, a sophomore philosophy and political science double major, is from Kokomo, Ind., a community an hour north of campus, which has also shown strong opposition to its own data center project. “Being at [Butler], so much of our curriculum is community-based,” McKinley said. “[Data centers] are an issue we’re seeing affect students in their hometown; we should carry that over [to] caring about it here.” McKinley sees the issue as an opportunity for students to get more involved in the local community. “This is the time you’re going to be most available to care, have the resources to [get involved] and be around people your age that care about similar things,” McKinley said. “If you’re seeing so many of your peers passionate about this, maybe it’s time to think about why that is.” While communities remain wary of data centers in their area, some involved are supportive of the initiatives, particularly the potential industrial and monetary benefits. Michael-Paul Hart is the city-county councilor for District 20, where the site is located. District 20 is also where Google withdrew a rezoning request for a data center last year after community disagreement and an expected no-vote from the City-County Council. “[Thunderbird Commerce Center] is a site that has power already,” Hart said. “It is surrounded by other industrial-type uses. If you were going to pick a site, [this] is a good site given its history of being a brownfield [and] being a manufacturing area.” Hart says that the development will provide benefits to District 20, allowing for further investment into the community as a result of potential tax abatements, commonly referred to as tax breaks, and community impact payments. “[The data center buildings] will be the smallest [ones] over there, but they will pay seven to 10 times more because of [the] equipment inside it, even under tax abatement,” Hart said. “In this case, the charity and community impact is between [$7 million] and $8 million. Without a tax abatement, I can’t get those checks.” While a vote for tax abatements for the DC BLOX site has not been scheduled, abatements were recently approved for the Sabey Decatur Township data center project and a vote on abatements for the Metrobloks site is scheduled for Oct. 21. DC BLOX could not be reached for comment at the time of publication.

artigo.texto: Arevon Energy marks construction milestone at 250 MW Cormorant battery storage project in Daly City, California Arevon Energy hit a construction milestone at its Cormorant Energy Storage Project in Daly City, California, on September 16, 2026. The celebration brought state and local officials, project partners, labor and business leaders, and community members to the site of what will become a 250 MW/1,000 MWh battery storage facility — big enough to power 321,000 homes for up to four hours at peak demand. Commercial operations are expected to begin in 2027. Arevon marks construction progress at Daly City battery storage site The September 16 milestone wasn’t just a photo op. It pulled together a genuinely broad group — state and local officials, California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) representatives, labor and business leaders, community members — all there to recognize how far the project has come since construction kicked off in March 2026. Arevon CEO Justin Johnson put the project’s purpose plainly: “Cormorant represents the kind of critical energy infrastructure California needs to meet growing electricity demand while strengthening grid reliability.” Store power when there’s plenty of it, deliver it when the grid needs it most. That’s the whole idea. Cormorant is a 250 MW/1,000 MWh battery storage project in Daly City, California, developed and operated by Arevon in partnership with Primoris Services Corporation. Daly City Mayor Glenn Sylvester echoed that framing, noting the project positions the city as an active contributor to statewide infrastructure goals — not merely a host community. Commercial operations remain on track for 2027. Project expanded and backed by long-term power agreement with MCE Cormorant didn’t start out at its current scale. Originally designed at 188 MW/752 MWh, it was later bumped up to 250 MW/1,000 MWh. That expansion came with a key partner: MCE, a community electricity provider serving more than 1.8 million residents and businesses across Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, and Solano counties, which contracted for the additional capacity under a long-term offtake agreement. The partnership goes beyond buying power. MCE’s Acting CEO Vicken Kasarjian noted that more than $500,000 from the contract will flow directly to local community programs. “This project has a direct community benefit,” he said — pointing to built-in funding for initiatives supporting Bay Area residents. On the construction side, Arevon is working with Primoris Services Corporation’s Renewables group, and at peak the project employs around 175 workers. Grid reliability and environmental benefits expected over project lifetime Battery storage projects like Cormorant absorb electricity during off-peak hours — when solar generation is high and demand is lower — then release it when the grid is under stress. That charge-and-dispatch cycle is what makes storage a reliability tool, not just a clean energy one. Cormorant uses lithium iron phosphate battery technology, which carries a strong safety record and a long operating life. Both matter for a project expected to run for decades. Over its lifetime, the facility is projected to avoid 191,800 U.S. tons of CO₂ annually and save more than 4.2 billion gallons of water — figures that reflect displaced emissions and the water savings compared to conventional thermal generation. The CPUC sees projects like this as essential. Energy Division Director Molly Sterkel said the agency expects more than 20 GW of new clean resources to come online by 2032, with battery storage described as “a critical part of that effort” — particularly for filling the reliability gap when solar drops off in the evening and demand stays high. Economic impact and community investment in Daly City Beyond the grid, Cormorant is expected to generate more than $73 million in property tax revenue over its lifetime, flowing to local schools, infrastructure, and public services. That’s a long-term fiscal benefit that outlasts the construction phase by a wide margin. Arevon has built relationships with more than a dozen local organizations throughout the project’s development. Partners include Bayshore Elementary School District, Jefferson Union High School District, Daly City Partnership, Pilipino Bayanihan Resource Center, Bayshore Community Center, Pacific Islands Together, and John’s Closet, among others. The company’s involvement has spanned donations, sponsorships, scholarships, memberships, and volunteer work — a range that signals sustained engagement rather than a one-time check. Mike Stancil, Executive Director of the Daly City Partnership, described Arevon as “a caring and compassionate corporate partner.” Arevon itself operates more than 6.3 GW of solar and energy storage projects across 18 states and holds the No. 1 developer ranking in Solar Power World’s 2026 Top Solar Contractors List for California. Cormorant is one of several recent California storage projects the company has brought through development and into construction. A long-term agreement with MCE Cormorant is a 250 MW/1,000 MWh battery storage project in Daly City, California, developed and operated by Arevon in partnership with Primoris Services Corporation. It operates under a long-term agreement with MCE, which serves the broader Bay Area, and is expected to reach commercial operations in 2027. The project can power 321,000 homes for up to four hours during peak demand. Projected outcomes include avoiding 191,800 U.S. tons of CO₂ annually, saving more than 4.2 billion gallons of water over its lifetime, and generating more than $73 million in local property tax revenue. More than $500,000 from the MCE contract is earmarked for community programs in the region. artigo.texto: BYD Says Its New Solid-State EV Battery Tech Is Nearly Ready For The Open Road Switching from lithium-ion to solid-state batteries promises to extend the range and charging speeds of electric vehicles, and Chinese car maker BYD believes it's in a "leading position" to commercialize the technology. BYD's Executive Vice President Stella Li shared the claim in a recent interview with Carwow's Spanish outlet, alongside the news that BYD would release its first car with a solid-state battery in 2027. "Talking about solid-state batteries, BYD is in the leading position," Li said. "We're in the leading position for commercialization and technology. So to prove that, next year, we have one model that will be the first one with that technology." Li's comments further confirm plans shared by Sun Huajun, the Chief Technology Officer of BYD's battery subsidiary FinDreams, at a battery conference in February 2025. At the time, Sun said BYD would offer its first demonstration and installation of solid-state batteries in 2027 before the technology enters mass production around 2030, CarNewsChina reports. While that means people will be able to buy cars with the company's sulfide solid-state batteries, that doesn't mean its traditional lithium batteries will be phased out, BYD Chief Scientist Lian Yubo shared at the same conference. "Solid-state batteries will be mainly used in high-end models, empowering each other with lithium iron phosphate batteries, and used in vehicles of different levels," Lian said. In comparison to lithium-ion batteries, which move ions between positive and negative terminals through a liquid solution of dissolved lithium salts, solid-state batteries replace the liquid with solid electrolytes made from oxides, polymers or sulfides (the kind BYD is developing). Solid electrolytes give solid-state batteries higher energy density, which opens up the possibility of smaller, lighter batteries and a longer range on a single charge. Solid-state batteries are also theoretically safer because they're far less prone to catching fire and they're able to operate at extreme temperatures, an issue current lithium-ion batteries struggle with. Advertisement The problem with using the battery technology as it exists now is cost, which is why BYD suggests you'll see its solid-state batteries on more expensive models first, like possibly a future version of its Denza Z. The company is one of several car makers planning to ship a vehicle with solid-state batteries in the next few years. For example, Toyota committed to offering cars with solid-state batteries by 2027 or 2028; Mercedes-Benz began testing a solid-state EQS model and shared that it would ship the technology before the end of the decade; and Stellantis began road testing a solid-state Dodge Charger in 2026. Earlier this year, Honda struck up a new partnership with QuantumScape to develop solid-state batteries it hopes will help it reach carbon neutrality by 2050. The potential for solid-state battery technology is exciting, but most car makers are only in the first leg of the race. artigo.texto: - China has prioritized breakthroughs in all-solid-state technologies to accelerate the roll-out of next-generation batteries. - The plan also calls for improving sodium battery performance and supporting corporate mergers and restructuring. China aims to achieve initial large-scale use of all-solid-state batteries by 2030, accelerating the transition of next-generation battery technology from research to commercialization. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) on Monday released its new battery industry development plan for the fifteenth five-year period, setting a roadmap for 2026 through 2030. The document, dated September 14, was jointly issued by 7 government agencies, including MIIT, the National Development and Reform Commission and the Ministry of Transport. The plan calls for steady growth in China's new battery industry through 2030, alongside breakthroughs in advanced electrode materials, new electrolytes and high-end auxiliary materials. Beyond the all-solid-state battery deployment target, it sets goals for long-life lithium batteries to reach 15,000 charge-discharge cycles and for leading manufacturers to achieve product defect rates at the parts-per-billion (PPB) level. All-solid-state batteries are a key technological priority. The document calls for faster breakthroughs in commercialization technologies, focusing on improving ionic conductivity and cycling stability while optimizing costs. Specific measures include improving interfacial contact, extending cycle life, advancing pressure-system engineering and scaling up production of high-performance solid electrolytes. The plan also calls for combining high-voltage, high-capacity cathode materials with new lithium-metal-based anodes and anode-free designs, while developing manufacturing equipment such as isostatic presses for solid-state batteries. China plans to build a supply system centered on lithium batteries, complemented by sodium and flow batteries, while strengthening its ability to commercialize all-solid-state and ultrafast-charging batteries. For sodium batteries, the document emphasizes cost, safety and resource availability advantages, calling for the development of cold-resistant, high-energy-density power batteries and energy storage batteries with long cycle lives. Industry consolidation and supply chain security are another focus. The document supports corporate mergers and restructuring and calls for faster exploration and development of domestic lithium, cobalt and other mineral resources. On recycling, the plan requires companies to establish used-battery collection systems aligned with their sales volumes. It also encourages them to build recycling capacity in major export markets where conditions permit. The document proposes a digital identity management system for products including new energy vehicle (NEV) power batteries, exploring internationally accepted battery passport arrangements and promoting mutual recognition of carbon footprint data. The battery plan follows China's September 11 release of its fifteenth five-year development plan for the intelligent connected NEV industry, which targets a 70% share for NEVs in domestic new passenger vehicle sales by 2030. The earlier automotive plan also called for tighter management of power battery production capacity. The latest battery plan further defines priorities for technology development, manufacturing upgrades and broader applications.

artigo.texto: Off-grid battery storage is growing fast because of increased demands in rural electrification, renewable energies, decentralized energy production, and access to electricity. Off-grid battery storage makes it possible for residential areas, commercial buildings, telecommunication masts, industries, and remote locations to store electrical energy independently of grid connectivity. The growth of lithium-ion, flow, hybrid, and smart battery storage is enhancing capacity, cycle life, and scalability of the batteries. According to SNS Insider, the Off-Grid Battery Storage Market was valued at USD 22.62 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 219.07 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 25.49% from 2026 to 2035. Global off-grid battery storage capacity was estimated at approximately 45 GWh in 2025, reflecting increasing deployment across renewable-energy and rural electrification applications. Gain Actionable Intelligence on the Off-Grid Battery Storage Market – Request a Free Sample Report Renewable Energy, Rural Electrification, and Advanced Batteries Drive Demand The rising growth of renewable energy installations is leading to increased demand for off-grid energy storage due to the nature of the solar and wind sources which require energy storage for providing electricity during periods where the source does not generate electricity. According to the report, off-grid battery storage capacity increased by about 23% in 2025 due to factors such as rural electrification, integration of renewable energy, and rising demand for reliable decentralized electricity production. Systems with medium capacity, falling within the range of 10-100 kWh made up about 45.67% of the market in 2025. Their favorable ratio of cost to energy storage makes them suitable for homes, telecoms infrastructure, and small business establishments. Systems that use solar power made up approximately 53.84% of the market in 2025, owing to falling prices of solar technology and its wide usage in decentralization of electrical power. The hybrid systems are expected to have the fastest growth of approximately 32.05% CAGR since integration of several renewable sources and energy storage increases reliability in cases of fluctuating solar and wind power production. The residential segment had a share of approximately 37.56% in the market in 2025 due to electrification of households, roof-top solar power systems, and increasing desire for self-sufficiency in energy. Companies Advancing Global Off-Grid Battery Storage CATL CATL is one of the leading battery manufacturers in the world for applications such as electric cars, renewable energy sources, and energy storage applications. With its high scale of production, cell to pack technologies, battery chemistry know-how, and logistics systems, CATL caters to residential, commercial, industrial, and large-scale energy storage applications. In April 2025, CATL unveiled its Naxtra sodium-ion battery for energy storage applications. The battery technology uses abundantly available materials with emphasis on energy density and safety. BYD BYD integrates batteries production, electric vehicles technology, and stationary power storage systems within its vertically integrated company structure. Blade battery technology focuses on safety, lifetime, energy density, and scalability within residential and commercial applications. In March 2025, BYD launched its Battery-Box HVE and Battery-Box HVB residential storage system based on Blade battery technology. Modularity in their design provides flexibility in storage capacity, thus ensuring that BYD is well-positioned to meet growing needs of solar and renewable energy standalone systems. LG Energy Solution LG Energy Solution is an advanced producer of lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems which are used in automotive sector, homes, commercial, industrial and large-scale applications. The company specializes in development of battery technologies, safety, energy efficiency and storage scalability. In May 2025, LG Energy Solution launched innovative containerized LFP energy storage system in Europe and signed a deal on provision of 981 MWh of the system to PGE company in Poland. Global Off-Grid Battery Storage Outlook Through 2035 The global off-grid battery storage market is expected to grow significantly up until 2035 due to the increasing usage of renewable energy sources, rural electrification, microgrids, distributed generation, and energy independence requirements. The off-grid battery systems with renewable energy sources account for around 32% of all installations in 2025, which reflects the increasingly developing connection between the energy storage and the renewable energy deployment. Expensive investments, installation difficulties, and the absence of the required infrastructure in remote locations remain among key problems. However, advancements in battery technology, modularity, government assistance, and EPC services may have a positive influence on the growth of the market. Reaching up to almost USD 219.07 billion by 2035, lithium-ion batteries, flow batteries, hybrid technologies, large-scale batteries, and off-grid EV chargers may provide numerous opportunities for the Off-Grid Battery Storage Market. Manufacturers of batteries, modularity, integration with renewable energy resources, smart energy management, safety, and installation services may be considered successful market players in the fast-growing global market.

artigo.texto: Li Auto's Li Xiang Responds to "De-CATL" Debate: In-House Development Isn't About Opposing Suppliers, But Deep Collaboration Li Auto (02015.HK) Chairman and CEO Li Xiang published a public statement on September 28 responding to the recently heated industry debate over "de-CATL-ization." He stated clearly that interpreting in-house development as "de-XX-ization" and positioning oneself against suppliers reflects zero-sum thinking, and that Li Auto has never used such an approach to define its self-development strategy. Li Xiang emphasized in his post that outstanding Chinese smart EV companies would never define their strategies with such a narrow mindset. He cited examples: Apple's A-series chips, Nvidia's and Qualcomm's flagship chips are mostly designed in-house and manufactured by TSMC; Tesla's self-developed batteries are produced in collaboration with CATL (300750.SZ), LG, and Sunwoda (300207.SZ). This model has not weakened TSMC, CATL, or Sunwoda—it has made them stronger. "Automakers define product experience, system architecture, and quality standards more deeply, while partners leverage their professional capabilities in engineering, manufacturing processes, and scaled delivery," Li Xiang wrote. "A good OEM-supplier relationship is not about who replaces whom, but about making products better through deeper collaboration." The Threefold Logic of Self-Development Li Xiang further elaborated on three core reasons Li Auto insists on deep battery self-development. First, to deliver user experiences that lead industry standards and build solutions for unmet needs first. He noted that users don't care about underlying electrochemical terminology—they care about whether range holds up, how long long-distance charging takes, whether performance stays stable in extreme heat or cold, and how safety baselines are guaranteed. From the industry's first extended-range large battery to the physics-defying 5C ultra-fast charging, to improvements in LFP battery low-temperature performance, state-of-charge accuracy, and longevity, these hardcore battery metric breakthroughs often have no ready-made solutions on the market. Second, to make the battery an integrated part of the intelligent vehicle, achieving a "1+1>2" whole-vehicle experience. Li Xiang believes the battery is by no means an isolated component—it and the vehicle must form a complete living organism with full end-to-end connectivity. Deep integration of cells, PACK, BMS, thermal management, electric drive, and vehicle control not only improves system-wide safety and quality, but also enables continuous OTA evolution years after delivery—charging strategies can be optimized, energy management can be refined, and low-temperature performance can keep improving. Third, full-lifecycle data connectivity so users don't have to pay for supply-chain division of labor. Li Xiang stated that the physical battery must ultimately become a data battery; connecting battery and vehicle data represents a higher level of battery specialization. The value of this data connectivity lies in: any微小 anomaly during production can trigger early warnings and be resolved before installation and delivery; problems can be solved before users even sense potential risks. This also ensures absolute consistency in after-sales service and repair standards. Thanking "Comrade-in-Arms" CATL In his post, Li Xiang specifically mentioned the partnership with CATL. He revealed that Li Auto established its battery R&D team back in 2015, and when certain product definitions were doubted by everyone, it was CATL that collaborated on joint development and turned the impossible into reality. "Here, I want to especially thank our comrade-in-arms CATL. It was Li Auto's deep product definition, our joint development, and CATL's strong support that helped Li Auto create products that continue to lead the industry," Li Xiang wrote. The context for this statement is that as more automakers begin in-house development and manufacturing of core components like batteries, views such as "de-CATL-ization" have emerged in the market, sparking considerable controversy. Li Xiang's response aims to clarify: self-development does not mean cutting ties with suppliers, nor does it mean replacing them. "Li Auto never wants to 'de-XX-ize' anything. On the contrary, we welcome every outstanding partner to achieve deep integration with Li Auto and together push user experience to the extreme," Li Xiang stated. "Times are changing, and the only standard by which we evaluate change is whether it can create greater value for users: delivering better products, providing better services, and bringing better experiences. Changing for users is the ultimate starting point of all of Li Auto's choices." The Pace of Self-Developed Battery Rollout Li Auto plans to equip all models with self-developed batteries once production capacity successfully ramps up. Li Xiang previously stated that in the long term, batteries and chips will be the company's most important technological barriers and moats. "Self-development represents our hope to hold future-facing core technology barriers in our own hands, like Apple and Huawei." From an industry perspective, Li Xiang's statement reflects the deep restructuring currently underway in China's new energy vehicle supply chain. The trend of automakers extending upstream and self-developing core components is increasingly evident, and how to balance self-development with external supply chain relationships is becoming a strategic question every automaker must answer. Li Xiang's answer: self-development is not about becoming an island, but about pulling the best partners closer and together making the user experience better. This stance is consistent with Li Auto's long-standing product-first philosophy. artigo.texto: Gotion High-tech Teams Up with Volkswagen on €3.2 Billion Lithium Battery Bases in Europe and Africa Gotion High-tech (002074.SZ) has taken a decisive step in its overseas power battery strategy. After the market close on September 28, the Chinese battery maker announced plans to jointly invest approximately €3.222 billion (approximately $3.7 billion) with PowerCo, the battery subsidiary of Volkswagen Group, to form joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia and Morocco for lithium battery and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode material production. The same day, a wholly owned subsidiary of Gotion also signed engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contracts with PowerCo Spain worth a combined €1.094 billion (approximately $1.2 billion). According to the announcement, Gotion High-tech and its wholly owned subsidiaries Gotion High-Tech (HK) Limited, Gotion GmbH and Gotion Power Africa S.A.S. plan to sign an investment agreement with Volkswagen AG and its wholly owned subsidiaries PowerCo SE and Power Holdco Lux S.A. to establish three joint ventures in Valencia, Spain; Šurany, Slovakia; and Kenitra, Morocco. Total project investment is estimated at approximately €3.222 billion (approximately $3.7 billion), of which the Gotion side will contribute approximately €1.598 billion (approximately $1.8 billion) and the PowerCo side approximately €1.624 billion (approximately $1.8 billion). Gotion's contribution will be funded by its own capital and self-raised funds. The three projects differ in capacity planning and equity structure. The Valencia JV hosts the largest lithium battery project, with planned annual capacity of 29.1 GWh and total investment of approximately €2.262 billion (approximately $2.6 billion); upon completion, Gotion will hold 49% and PowerCo 51%, with PowerCo as the controlling party. The Šurany JV will run an 8.4 GWh lithium battery project with total investment of approximately €480 million (approximately $546.3 million); Gotion will hold 51% and PowerCo 49%, with Gotion as the controlling party. The Morocco JV focuses on the upstream materials segment, with planned annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes of LFP cathode material and total investment of approximately €480 million (approximately $546.3 million); Gotion will likewise hold 51% and control the venture. The capacity and investment structure of the three projects is summarized below: The two European battery plants have combined planned annual capacity of 37.5 GWh, and cathode material produced by the Morocco project will be prioritized for supply to these two plants. The equity arrangements form a clear complementary structure: the Valencia base is controlled by PowerCo, deeply integrating Gotion into Volkswagen Group's core European cell supply system; the Slovakia and Morocco projects are controlled by Gotion, helping the company establish self-directed manufacturing footholds in the European and African markets. Beyond equity stakes, the announcement disclosed several arrangements material to the transaction: the Valencia project does not involve a newly established company — instead, the Gotion side will acquire a 49% stake in the existing PowerCo Spain through a capital increase, with PowerCo retaining control after the transaction. The construction scope of all three projects excludes land and factory buildings, and each project is expected to take no more than five years to build. The announcement also clarified that cells produced by the two European battery plants will prioritize meeting Volkswagen Group's demand in Europe, with specific purchase volumes and supply guarantee arrangements to be determined in subsequent formal agreements. In addition, the investment agreement has not yet been signed; the plan was approved by Gotion's board of directors on September 28 but still requires shareholder approval and government clearances in China and abroad. Beyond the equity investment, the EPC contracts add another business dimension to the partnership. Gotion Spain, a wholly owned subsidiary of Gotion High-tech, plans to sign with PowerCo Spain a Phase 1 drying room turnkey contract and a Phase 2 EPC contract for the 29.1 GWh Valencia lithium battery project, with a combined contract value of €1.094 billion (approximately $1.2 billion). The Phase 1 contract is valued at €295 million (approximately $335.7 million) and the Phase 2 contract at €799 million (approximately $909.3 million), both on a fixed lump-sum basis. This means Gotion will participate not only as a shareholder but also as the EPC contractor, directly generating construction-phase revenue. Because Volkswagen (China) Investment Co., Ltd. holds 24.28% of Gotion High-tech and is its largest shareholder, Volkswagen Group and its subsidiaries constitute related legal persons of the company, making both matters related-party transactions. The announcement shows that connected directors abstained from voting, and the relevant proposals still require shareholder approval and government clearances in China and abroad. Gotion said in the announcement that the investment will be deployed in phases and that project implementation remains subject to government approvals in China and abroad, with some uncertainty. The company is deeply engaged in lithium battery R&D, manufacturing and sales, and has in recent years been steadily expanding its overseas power battery footprint. By jointly building production bases in Europe with Volkswagen Group and taking on EPC work, Gotion aims to deepen the long-term strategic partnership, participate in the construction of Volkswagen Group's core European cell bases, generate business revenue while accumulating experience in contracting large-scale European battery plant projects, and optimize its business structure and profit model. artigo.texto: CATL's Choco-Swap Network Tops 2,500 Stations in China Ahead of National Day Free Trial CATL (03750.HK) subsidiary Choco-Swap hit a critical juncture on the eve of China's National Day holiday. With the official completion of the Lanzhou Chengguan North Binhe East Road station, Choco-Swap's cumulative nationwide station count surpassed 2,520 as of September 29, covering 200 cities across 31 provinces, with nearly 20,000 brand-new CATL batteries deployed into inventory. From September 30 to October 7, Choco-Swap will launch a "99-Second Swap Across China" free battery-swap trial program, giving new energy vehicle (NEV) owners a chance to experience the efficiency advantage of the swapping model during peak travel season. Network Expansion: From Core Cities to County-Level Penetration Since the start of this year, Choco-Swap has maintained an industry-leading expansion pace. First- and second-tier cities in China now have full coverage, small and medium-sized cities account for more than 80% of stations, and over a quarter of the cities where stations are located rank first in the industry for station density. The network layout is spreading outward from core hub cities in contiguous clusters, penetrating deeply into the "capillary" markets of small and medium-sized cities and county-level areas. The highway swap network is breaking new ground simultaneously. According to plan, 1,000 highway swap stations will be deployed between 2026 and 2027, creating an "11 vertical, 9 horizontal" highway swap backbone grid, aiming for an average of one pair of swap stations every 100 kilometers, with support for multi-brand and multi-model sharing. Battery Management and Technical Safeguards On the battery side, a full-lifecycle digital management and digital-twin monitoring system tracks and evaluates the health status of every battery in inventory in real time, ensuring the safety and stability of swap services. The dual-track network buildout—urban and highway—is accelerating in tandem. The breadth and density of urban station coverage, combined with the planned highway backbone grid, constitute the two core growth curves for Choco-Swap in the charging infrastructure space. Industry Impact and Competitive Landscape Battery swapping, as one of the key pathways for NEV energy replenishment, is transitioning from early pilot exploration to large-scale deployment. Leveraging its cost and technology advantages on the battery manufacturing side, CATL is deeply binding its swap network with battery asset operations, creating differentiated competitiveness distinct from third-party swap operators. Note: Data as of September 29, 2026, sourced from official Choco-Swap disclosures. As swap network density increases, user perception of refueling convenience will strengthen further. The launch of the free swap program during the National Day holiday serves both as a concentrated showcase of network capability and as a market strategy to drive user awareness and cultivate swapping habits. For NEV owners, a parallel energy-replenishment landscape of swapping and charging is taking shape at an accelerating pace. artigo.texto: Seven Chinese ministries issue 15th Five-Year Plan for next-gen batteries: accelerating all-solid-state battery industrialization, improving recycling systems Seven Chinese government agencies led by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology jointly issued the "15th Five-Year Plan for the New-Type Battery Industry" on September 28, laying out arrangements across two main fronts—technology breakthroughs and recycling utilization: on one hand accelerating breakthroughs in all-solid-state battery industrialization technology and making forward-looking arrangements for next-generation battery systems; on the other hand improving the spent battery recycling and utilization system to promote efficient use of recycled resources. The plan calls for deepening research on fundamental and forward-looking scientific questions in new-type batteries, and strengthening original innovation and disruptive technology breakthroughs. It promotes collaborative process innovation across battery materials, structural design, manufacturing technology, and system integration, aiming to improve intrinsic safety, energy and power density, structural strength, and lightweighting. For all-solid-state batteries, the plan explicitly focuses on improving ionic conductivity and cycling stability, optimizing costs, and other key directions to accelerate breakthroughs in industrialization technology. It also makes forward-looking arrangements for next-generation battery systems including new alkali metal-ion batteries, multivalent-ion batteries, metal-air/sulfur batteries, multifunctional composite structural batteries, and nuclear batteries. In the recycling segment, the plan requires implementation of the extended producer responsibility system, pushing companies to establish spent battery recycling systems—whether self-built or commissioned—that match their product sales volumes, and accelerating the construction and operation of recycling service outlets. Specific measures include: supporting R&D and industrial application of technologies and equipment for refined dismantling of new-type batteries, low-cost utilization, and efficient extraction of valuable elements; improving the refinement and automation levels of spent battery dismantling, crushing, sorting, and smelting processes; guiding localities to rationally allocate processing capacity commensurate with regional spent battery generation volumes, and promoting resource concentration toward competitive enterprises. Additionally, the plan proposes guiding companies to deploy spent battery comprehensive utilization capacity in major export markets for new-type batteries where conditions permit, in order to enhance resource security capabilities.
