artigo.texto: A Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia, informou que sua sede em Kiev foi atingida por um ataque russo no domingo (27), sem vítimas no local. A Rússia afirmou ter atingido também um data center da Vodafone, que não comentou o caso. Outros centros de dados da capital foram alvo de bombardeios. Segundo autoridades ucranianas, uma dessas ações feriu um adulto e duas crianças; interrupções ao longo da semana teriam deixado cerca de 100 mil residências sem conexão. O governo ucraniano alerta que os ataques à infraestrutura de comunicação podem prejudicar a distribuição de avisos sobre mísseis e drones. Kiev e cidades próximas estão entre as áreas afetadas pela perda de acesso à internet. O ex-procurador especial Jack Smith defendeu nesta terça-feira (29), no Senado americano, os processos contra Donald Trump. Afirmou que reuniu provas de “crimes graves contra a nação” e negou motivação política. As acusações envolviam tentativas de reverter a eleição de 2020 e retenção de documentos confidenciais. Os casos foram arquivados após a vitória de Trump em 2024, diante da regra contra indiciar presidentes em exercício. Foto: Sargento Nathan Mitchell/Marinha dos Estados Unidos A Marinha autorizou o navio Atlantic Explorer, dos Estados Unidos, a realizar pesquisas na Plataforma Amazônica entre 3 e 13 de outubro. A portaria foi publicada no Diário Oficial da União nesta terça-feira (29). A embarcação pertence ao Instituto de Ciências Oceânicas das Bermudas, ligado à Universidade Estadual do Arizona. Os estudos serão realizados em parceria com a Universidade de São Paulo. Donald Trump afirmou nesta terça-feira (29) que teria feito um “trabalho de merda como presidente” se o America.gov fosse a maior realização de sua gestão. Apesar da declaração, ele elogiou o novo portal de serviços do governo americano. A plataforma usa inteligência artificial para responder a perguntas e facilitar o acesso a informações oficiais. Segundo o site, conversas e dados de localização serão apagados automaticamente após cada consulta. A Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos autorizou nesta terça-feira (29) a retomada das deportações de imigrantes para países diferentes dos de origem. A decisão é provisória e permite ao governo Trump continuar o programa enquanto sua legalidade é analisada. O tribunal ouvirá os argumentos em dezembro, com decisão final prevista para o próximo ano. A discussão envolve a possibilidade de os imigrantes contestarem o envio e apresentarem riscos de perseguição ou tortura no destino. Três senadores democratas enviaram nesta terça-feira (29) uma carta a Marco Rubio cobrando o reconhecimento do resultado das eleições brasileiras e relações diplomáticas normais com qualquer candidato eleito. Os parlamentares acusam o governo Trump de interferência e dizem que pressões diplomáticas, econômicas e políticas ameaçam as instituições brasileiras. A carta cita tarifas sobre produtos do Brasil e sanções contra ministros do STF.

artigo.texto: COEP Technological University and JSW Projects have signed an agreement to establish an indigenous lithium-ion battery technology centre at the university’s research facility in Chikhali, Pune district, in a project estimated to cost ₹800 crore. The centre will be developed in two phases and is planned to include battery prototyping, pilot-scale research and development facilities. According to the report by Loksatta, the project will support the development of lithium-ion battery cell technology within Pune’s academic and engineering ecosystem. The agreement was signed by COEP registrar Dr D. N. Sonawane and JSW Group executive vice-president Naresh Lalwani. COEP vice-chancellor Prof Sunil Bhirud, Dr S. P. Mahajan, dean Prof P. A. Sadgir, Dr Ranjit Date, professor of practice Dr Sarika Kelkar and other university officials attended the signing. JSW senior vice-president Amitabh Singh, associate vice-president Chandrakant Mahalingam and deputy general managers Vijay Chaudhary and Sudeep Sarkar were also present. Bhirud said the centre could help develop an indigenous alternative to imported batteries and contribute to India’s effort to build domestic capability. He said students would receive opportunities to learn advanced battery technology and work on practical applications, while the facility would provide a wider platform for research, innovation and technology development. The project places an engineering university at the centre of a technology area that has implications for electric mobility, energy storage and industrial manufacturing. However, the supplied report does not specify the proposed capacity of the facility, the exact timeline for either phase, the technologies to be developed, or whether the centre will manufacture commercial battery cells. JSW Group chairman Sajjan Jindal said India had spent substantial foreign exchange on crude oil imports over several decades and needed to develop advanced skills and capabilities to manufacture batteries domestically. He described the partnership with COEP, which has a 172-year engineering history, as a collaboration that could create new opportunities across industry, research and education. The agreement marks a new industry-academia initiative for Pune’s research landscape. Its eventual impact will depend on the execution of the two phases, the research infrastructure established at Chikhali, and the translation of laboratory and pilot-scale work into deployable battery technologies. The next milestones will be the detailed implementation of the project and the development of the proposed centre.

artigo.texto: COEP Technological University (COEP Tech), Pune, and JSW Projects, a JSW Group company, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to establish an Advanced Battery Research & Development Centre at COEP Tech’s Chikhali Research Park. The Centre marks India’s first indigenous battery prototyping and pilot-scale R&D platform, bringing lithium-ion cell technology development onto an academic campus in Pune for the first time. The collaboration positions COEP and Maharashtra as India’s battery-technology hub, with the potential to catalyse over 1,000 battery ecosystem-related jobs. It is a step towards Aatmanirbhar Bharat and India’s Net Zero 2070 ambition, anchoring the electric vehicle, grid storage and clean-energy future in Indian innovation. The partnership addresses one of the most persistent gaps in India’s innovation ecosystem: the distance between university research and industrial application. Under the MoU, COEP Tech’s faculty and students will work alongside JSW’s engineers on live, commercially critical technology, in an industry-academia collaboration model at the scale India needs. Prof. Sunil Bhirud, Hon’ble Vice Chancellor, COEP Technological University said, “This collaboration has the potential to create a strong indigenous alternative to imported batteries and make a significant contribution to India’s journey towards self-reliance. For students, it will provide a unique opportunity to learn and work on cutting-edge battery technologies. The scale and scope of the Phase I and Phase II collaboration between COEP Technological University and JSW make it a landmark industry-academia initiative. At a time when next-generation battery technologies are receiving significant research attention across the country, the partnership places research, innovation and technology development on a much larger platform. The collaboration has the potential to develop technologies that can reduce dependence on imported batteries and contribute to the vision of a self-reliant and developed India. The scale of this initiative makes it a significant step forward in strengthening India’s battery technology ecosystem. We are grateful for the valuable support extended by the Government of Maharashtra and the Board of Governors of COEP Technological University in enabling this important initiative.” Mr. Sajjan Jindal, Chairman, JSW Group, said, “Cell is the new oil. Just as oil powered the last century, battery cells will power this one, from electric vehicles to the grid. For decades, India has spent precious forex importing oil. This time, we must build the cutting-edge skills and capabilities to make these cells right here, for a new India. Our partnership with COEP Tech, with its 170-year legacy of engineering excellence, will bring industry and academia together to design, test and validate cells built for Indian conditions, and help shape India’s clean energy future.” A Shared Ambition Across the JSW Group The initiative draws on ambitions across the JSW Group, one of India’s most diversified industrial conglomerates. JSW Energy is aggressively building out grid-scale battery energy storage (BESS) alongside its renewable power business, while JSW Motors is expanding rapidly into electric mobility across every vehicle segment. Batteries sit at the heart of both ambitions, and JSW Group has committed to lead the indigenous value chain in this domain. Talent development, R&D capability, and a battery ecosystem at home are foundational to both the Group’s and India’s future. About the Engagement The project will be built in two phases, with a combined investment of more than ₹800 crore. Phase 1 will establish a Cell Research & Development Centre to design, simulate and prototype indigenous Li-ion and other advanced chemistry cells, including Sodium-ion. Phase 2 will scale this into a Cell Validation Centre capable of producing cells from 100-600 Ah. The batteries developed at the Centre are targeted to perform at par with the best in the world, while being built for India-centric climatic conditions and applications. The facility will serve as a foundation for joint research, publications, projects and IP development, taking India’s battery technology from lab to industry, on campus. Why This Matters - Pilot lines are what separate success from failure at giga-scale. The Centre allows JSW to de-risk the foundation before committing to giga-scale manufacturing. - It fulfils the Government of Maharashtra’s vision for COEP’s Chikhali Research Park as a hub for automotive and allied technology development. - It addresses India’s biggest structural gap in clean energy—with over 90% of the global Li-ion supply chain controlled by China—by building indigenous capability. - It positions COEP and Maharashtra as India’s battery-technology hub, with the potential to catalyse over 1,000 battery ecosystem-related jobs. - It is a step towards Aatmanirbhar Bharat and India’s Net Zero 2070 ambition, anchoring the EV, grid storage and clean-energy future in Indian innovation. This partnership between one of India’s most dynamic industrial groups and one of India’s most historic technical institutions marks the beginning of a journey that will shape the nation’s energy independence for decades to come.

artigo.texto: Vivo V80 launches with 7200mAh battery and 144Hz display Vivo is set to expand its mid-range smartphone portfolio with the launch of the V80 on October 6, 2026, introducing significant upgrades in battery capacity and display performance. Next-Generation Battery and Display Technology Vivo is set to expand its mid-range smartphone portfolio with the launch of the V80 on October 6, 2026, introducing significant upgrades in battery capacity and display performance. The most notable enhancement is the inclusion of a massive 7,200mAh battery, a substantial increase from the 6,500mAh cell found in its predecessor, the V70. This 11 percent boost in capacity is engineered to deliver extended usage times, addressing one of the primary demands of modern smartphone users who require reliable all-day performance without frequent recharging. Complementing the large battery is a 90W fast-charging capability, which Vivo claims can replenish 50 percent of the battery in just 30 minutes under laboratory conditions. This rapid charging technology mitigates the inconvenience of a large battery, ensuring that users can quickly top up their devices during short breaks. The physical dimensions of the phone have been carefully managed despite the larger battery; the V80 measures 7.69mm in thickness and weighs 203g, representing only a marginal increase over the V70. The visual experience is driven by a 6.59-inch AMOLED display with a 1.5K resolution of 2750 x 1260 pixels. The most significant display upgrade is the increase in the maximum refresh rate from 120Hz to 144Hz, providing smoother scrolling and more responsive interactions in supported applications. This high refresh rate is particularly beneficial for mobile gaming and navigating complex user interfaces, positioning the V80 as a compelling option for multimedia consumption and interactive entertainment. Advanced Camera System and Imaging Capabilities Vivo continues its partnership with ZEISS to deliver a sophisticated rear camera system on the V80. The primary setup features a 50MP main sensor with optical image stabilization, ensuring sharp and stable footage even in challenging lighting conditions. This is paired with a dedicated 50MP telephoto lens that offers 3x optical zoom and its own stabilization system, allowing users to capture detailed portraits and distant subjects without the quality degradation typically associated with digital cropping. The camera array is completed by an 8MP ultrawide lens, providing versatility for landscape and group photography. While Vivo advertises digital zoom capabilities up to 100x, the practical utility of the system lies in its high-resolution optical lenses. The front-facing camera is equally robust, featuring a 50MP autofocus sensor that ensures high-quality selfies and clear video calls, a critical feature for social media engagement and remote communication. Video recording capabilities include 4K resolution at 60 frames per second, alongside a Cinematic Video mode that applies movie-style color grading and depth-of-field effects. The integration of AI-powered lighting effects and tools for converting live photo elements into stickers adds a layer of creative flexibility, appealing to content creators and casual users alike. These software enhancements leverage the powerful hardware to provide a comprehensive imaging suite that competes favorably with higher-tier devices. Processing Power and Market Positioning Under the hood, the Vivo V80 retains the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 processor, the same chipset that powered the V70. While this means there is no generational leap in raw processing power, the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 remains a highly capable mid-range chipset, offering excellent thermal efficiency and sufficient performance for everyday tasks and demanding mobile games. The decision to retain the processor allows Vivo to optimize the software experience and maintain a competitive price point. The V80 is positioned to compete in a highly contested segment of the Kenyan smartphone market, where consumers are increasingly demanding premium features at accessible prices. The combination of a massive battery, high-refresh-rate display, and versatile camera system addresses the core needs of the target demographic. Competitors in this space, including offerings from Tecno and Infinix, will need to match these specifications to remain relevant. As the October 6 launch approaches, industry observers will be watching the pricing strategy and local availability of the V80. The success of the device will depend not only on its hardware specifications but also on Vivo's ability to provide robust after-sales support and software updates. For consumers seeking a balanced device that prioritizes battery life and imaging without compromising on display quality, the Vivo V80 presents a formidable option in the evolving mid-range landscape. artigo.texto: Processing and storing data is now pushing the frontier of economic development around the world, and huge amounts of capital are flowing into building out the infrastructure to support this big bet on cloud computing and Artificial Intelligence. The race to establish an advantageous position on the digital frontier is driving a major capex boom in the United States and elsewhere, and this wave has now fully arrived in Southeast Asia. Data centers require substantial land and resources, like electricity and water, and they need reliable connectivity such as access to subsea cable networks. Countries that have land, reasonably well-developed energy and telecommunications infrastructure and friendly regulatory environments are attracting investors and developers looking to ride the data center wave. Affordable inputs, like electricity, can sweeten the deal. It just so happens that many countries in Southeast Asia fit this bill. Malaysia is leading the pack. Clear policy guidance, well-developed infrastructure and close proximity to land-constrained Singapore are helping fuel a boom in data centers. The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone has seen a flurry of activity, but it is part of a broader phenomenon. In the first quarter of 2023, the Department of Statistics recorded a cumulative $11 billion of foreign investment in the information and communication sector, accounting for 5 percent of total foreign investment. By first quarter of 2026, this figure had risen to $32.5 billion, equal to 12 percent of total inbound investment. And there is no sign of slowing. According to the Malaysian Investment Development Authority, the body that reviews and approves investment projects, between 2021 and the first quarter of 2026, $96 billion worth of data center and cloud computing projects were approved, including $24 billion in the first half of 2026 alone. These are project approvals rather than realized investment, but it gives a sense of the speed and scale at which the data center boom is unfolding across Malaysia. Indonesia is also seeing an uptick in data center investment. Like Malaysia, some of this is driven by demand from Singapore, particularly in and around the island of Batam. Nongsa Digital Park is a Special Economic Zone that offers eligible projects tax and other fiscal incentives. Combined with Batam’s strong subsea cable connectivity, this has fueled a wave of new data center construction in the area. There is also a lot of investment activity in and around Jakarta where a number of large industrial scale data centers are being developed by state-backed players such as Telkom, as well as private sector firms and investors. As reported by Antara News, Indonesia’s current data center capacity sits around 580 MW and the plan is to grow it to 1.3 GW in the near-term. Government data shows that investment in information services jumped from $967 million in 2023 to $3.4 billion in 2025 and it looks set to keep climbing. Thailand is also now rushing to add more data centers, with several large industrial-scale projects in the pipeline. According to the Board of Investment, in 2025 they received $24 billion worth of applications across 151 projects in the digital industry, mainly data centers. Not all of these projects will be approved and become operational, but it again gives a sense of the speed and scale with which this industry is moving. Vietnam is following suit, with local media reporting that the government plans to reach 870 MW of data center capacity by 2030. The trend is clear: data centers are beginning to pop up all around Southeast Asia, attracting billions of dollars in investment and uncorking a major construction boom. But a bigger, perhaps more fundamental, question is whether demand for digital services can justify these enormous outlays and the resources they will absorb. Investment is pouring into Southeast Asian digital infrastructure, with the expectation that businesses and consumers will spend billions of dollars on cloud computing, AI and other digital services in the years ahead. This is not unique to Southeast Asia, of course. The same assumption about future demand has been driving eye-popping capex investment in data centers and cloud computing all around the world, raising similar questions. What we can say for sure is that the data center boom has reached the major economies of Southeast Asia. Whether these massive bets on future demand for digital services pays off is anybody’s guess. But considering the amounts of money involved, how this plays out is something we should all be watching very, very closely in the months and years ahead.

artigo.texto: da Agência iNFRA Dados da empresa norte-americana Cushman & Wakefield apontam crescimento de 91% na capacidade operacional de data centers em São Paulo em um ano. No primeiro semestre deste ano, a capacidade chegou a 661 MW (megawatts), ante 346 MW no mesmo período de 2025. Com o avanço, São Paulo se tornou o terceiro maior mercado primário das Américas, atrás apenas de Atlanta e Virgínia, nos Estados Unidos. A empresa lembra que o desempenho do setor ocorre em meio à criação do Redata (Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter), sancionado em 15 de setembro, que prevê a suspensão de tributos federais, como Imposto de Importação, PIS/Cofins, PIS/Cofins-Importação e IPI (Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados), sobre equipamentos destinados à instalação, ampliação e modernização de empreendimentos de data centers. No eixo São Paulo-Campinas, a capacidade dos empreendimentos em construção cresceu de 148 MW para 250 MW. Além disso, há 2.066 MW em projetos planejados para a região. Esse volume equivale a mais de três vezes a capacidade atualmente em operação, mas não significa que toda essa capacidade será efetivamente construída. A concretização dos projetos depende de fatores como disponibilidade de energia e acesso à rede de transmissão, equipamentos, conectividade, licenciamento e existência de clientes interessados em contratar a capacidade. Apesar da expansão da oferta, a vacância permaneceu baixa, em 4,1%, o que significa que cerca de 96% da capacidade de colocation estava ocupada. Nesse contexto, segundo a Cushman & Wakefield, o Redata pode contribuir para a viabilização dos projetos planejados ao reduzir os custos de aquisição de equipamentos destinados aos empreendimentos elegíveis. A empresa projeta que esse crescimento deve se estender para além de São Paulo. Regiões do país com oferta de energia renovável ou de baixa emissão, conexão de alta capacidade e terrenos preparados poderão disputar os próximos investimentos em data centers.

artigo.texto: By Brian Kennedy Pew Research Center Americans have grown more negative toward the possible environmental and economic effects of data centers since the beginning of the year. And a majority say they’d be uncomfortable if a new data center started operating in their area, according to a new Pew Research Center survey. The survey comes as protests against new data center construction have spread and as some state and local politicians have spoken out against data centers. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump has been a vocal supporter of data centers. More than half of Americans (54%) now say data centers are mostly bad for the environment, up from 39% in January. Half say they are mostly bad for home energy costs, up from 38%. And 49% say they are mostly bad for people’s quality of life nearby, up from 30%. The new survey was conducted from July 20 to Aug. 9 among 10,548 U.S. adults. Just 4% of Americans think data centers have a mostly good impact in each of these areas. Similar shares (between 21% and 24%) say data centers are mostly good and mostly bad for these things. Since January, there have been increases of 9 percentage points in the shares of Americans who say data centers are mostly bad for local jobs (from 15% to 24%) and local tax revenue (from 12% to 21%). Many Americans are still unsure or unfamiliar with data centers altogether. Shares ranging from 18% to 32% say they are not sure how data centers impact the five things the survey asked about. And overall, 12% say they haven’t heard of data centers. Americans in a variety of demographic and partisan subgroups have become more negative in their views of data centers. Men and women alike, as well as adults across age groups and education levels, have become more likely since January to say data centers have a mostly bad impact on the things the survey asked about. For example, rural Americans have become more likely to say data centers are mostly bad for the environment (from 32% in January to 50% in August), home energy costs (32% to 46%) and the quality of people living nearby (28% to 45%). Most data centers currently being planned or under development will be in rural areas. Americans in urban and suburban areas have also become more likely to say data centers are mostly bad for these things. As was the case earlier this year, Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents are more likely than Republicans and Republican leaners to view the impacts of data centers negatively. Still, Republicans’ views have also turned more negative: In the new survey, for example, 42% say the facilities are mostly bad for the quality of life of people nearby, up from 24% in January. Republican elected officials have staked out varying positions on data centers. While Trump has consistently supported their construction in his second term, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott previously supported expansion but issued a statewide moratorium on new data centers in August. Some Democrats, such as Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro and Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, have also recently shifted their positions to support additional rules and oversight on data center construction and operation. Among Democrats and Republicans alike, views on the effects of data centers on local jobs and tax revenue are somewhat more negative than they were at the start of the year. But many people in both partisan groups either say that they’re not sure or that the effects are neither good nor bad. More Democrats now say the effects of data centers in these two areas are mostly bad than mostly good. Liberal Democrats have primarily driven this shift: For example, 34% of liberals now say data centers are mostly bad for local tax revenue, up from 19% in January. More Republicans continue to say the effects of data centers on local jobs and tax revenue are mostly good than mostly bad. Still, Republicans are now 7 percentage points more likely than in January to say the effects in both areas are mostly bad. The new survey also finds that 60% of Americans say they would be not too or at all comfortable with a new data center operating in their area. Much smaller shares say they would be somewhat comfortable (19%) or extremely or very comfortable (7%) with this. Just over half of Republicans (54%) and about two-thirds of Democrats (68%) say they’d be not too or not at all comfortable with a new local data center. Liberal Democrats stand out, with 81% saying they’d be uncomfortable. Majorities of urban, suburban and rural Americans say they would be not too or not at all comfortable with a new data center in their area. Americans are more aware of data centers than they were earlier in the year. The share of Americans who say they have heard or read a lot about them has increased from 25% in January to 35% today. About 9 in 10 adults (88%) have now heard at least a little about data centers.

artigo.texto: Trinity Airways(091810) said on the 28th that it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on mutual cooperation regarding the carbon offset and reduction scheme for international aviation (CORSIA) and the emissions trading system with NH Investment & Securities. It is the first business agreement signed in Korea between an airline and a financial company in the fields of CORSIA and the emissions transaction system, and the two companies said they plan to expand cooperation across the entire carbon credit market. The agreement was prepared to proactively strengthen CORSIA response capabilities and establish a cooperation framework for the carbon credit market in line with the carbon reduction policy for the aviation institutional sector promoted by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the overall direction of CORSIA implementation. The MOU centers on multifaceted cooperation, including the exchange of information and the establishment of a joint response system for CORSIA and the domestic greenhouse gas carbon credit market and policies; the joint promotion of projects related to carbon credits; and various activities for the development of the carbon market. CORSIA offsetting is carried out by securing eligible carbon credits corresponding to the required offset amount within the set implementation period and then retiring them in the registry. Retiring credits means permanently deleting the secured carbon credits from the registry so the credits cannot be used again. Trinity Airways purchased 20,000 tons (t) of CORSIA-eligible carbon credits and signed a contract to retire those credits to proactively prepare for the obligation. It also plans to gradually secure more than 10% of the Phase 1 volume that must be offset by Jan. 2028 by additionally purchasing eligible credits by the end of this year to ensure stability in complying with greenhouse gas regulations and to ease uncertainties in the supply and demand of carbon credits. The signing ceremony was held on the 21st at Sono Trinity Commons in Gangseo-gu, Seoul, and was attended by Seo Dong-bin, executive in charge of corporate management support at Trinity Airways, Park Geon-hu, head of the Client Solutions Division at NH Investment & Securities, and other key officials from both companies. Seo said, "Through cooperation with NH Investment & Securities, we will strengthen our capabilities in sourcing and managing credits and build an efficient response system from a mid- to long-term perspective."

artigo.texto: A California AI company that signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge, and vows to protect Oklahoma ratepayers from paying for the power used at the facility announced Sunday plans to build a new data center at MidAmerica Industrial Park (MidAmerica) near Chouteau in Mayes County, Oklahoma. The company is expected to pay an estimated $500 million in taxes over the next 10 years based on current rates, and the project is expected to create up to 1,000 construction jobs and up to 100 permanent positions. In compliance with Oklahoma’s Data Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act, Lambda said it will take full responsibility for the resources and infrastructure needed to operate the facility, including paying 100 percent of its energy costs. We’re going to keep listening, keep showing up, and let our work here speak for itself.” “When developed responsibly, data centers can create lasting economic opportunities and investments in the communities where they operate,” said Michel Combes, Chief Executive Officer of Lambda. “Our responsibility is to ensure that this project delivers value to Mayes County while respecting the community’s resources, infrastructure, and priorities. We are committed to meeting that responsibility at every stage of the project.” Lambda’s Commitments - Ratepayer Protection: Lambda will protect local ratepayers by paying for all electricity the facility uses and ensuring the project meets Oklahoma’s requirements under the state’s ratepayer protection laws. The company has also signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge, and is working to design the project to be a more flexible grid customer with the ability to shift or reduce certain computing loads during periods of peak demand. - Water Stewardship: The facility will implement closed-loop cooling technology that dramatically reduces water use compared with traditional data center cooling. - Siting Away from Residents: The project is being built at the existing MidAmerica Industrial Park with infrastructure designed to minimize impacts on surrounding residential areas. “Oklahoma is leading the nation in building the modern economy, bringing major investments to our state and creating opportunities that will benefit our people for generations to come,” said Governor Kevin Stitt. “Lambda has committed to taking responsibility for the energy costs associated with its facility, ensuring those costs are not passed along to residential customers while generating hundreds of millions in tax revenue and economic growth right here in Oklahoma. These are commitments that reflect the kind of responsible investment we want to see in Oklahoma.” “Major investments like this demonstrate the opportunity we have to continue growing Oklahoma’s economy and attracting innovative companies to our state,” said Oklahoma Department of Commerce CEO John Budd. “Lambda’s decision to build here is a vote of confidence in Oklahoma’s workforce, infrastructure and business-friendly environment. We look forward to supporting this project and the new opportunities it will create for Oklahomans, while continuing to build an economy that can compete for investment and high-quality jobs for years to come.” “Lambda’s decision to build in Mayes County represents a transformative commitment to economic development in our community,” said Chouteau Mayor Brenda Cunningham. “This project will bring an estimated $500 million in tax revenue to our county over the next decade, which will go toward supporting our schools, public services and local priorities. artigo.texto: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer BYD has confirmed plans to introduce its first electric vehicle equipped with a solid-state battery in 2027. The company says it is in a leading position in the development and commercialisation of the technology. Solid-state batteries could offer higher energy density, lower weight, longer driving ranges and improved safety compared with conventional lithium-ion batteries. Key Overview - Company: BYD - Technology: Solid-state batteries - First model: Planned for 2027 - Initial application: Higher-end electric vehicles - Battery development: BYD’s FinDreams battery division - Expected mass production: Around 2030 - Existing batteries: Lithium iron phosphate batteries will continue across other vehicle segments BYD Confirms 2027 Solid-State Battery Plans BYD has confirmed that it plans to introduce its first electric vehicle using solid-state battery technology in 2027. BYD Executive Vice-President Stella Li said the company is in a leading position in both the technology and its commercialisation. The announcement follows plans previously outlined by BYD’s battery division, FinDreams, which indicated in 2025 that the company intended to demonstrate and install solid-state batteries in vehicles from 2027. Solid-State Batteries Could Improve EV Performance Solid-state batteries differ from conventional lithium-ion batteries primarily through the use of a solid electrolyte instead of a liquid one. The technology has the potential to provide higher energy density, which could allow electric vehicles to use smaller and lighter battery packs while maintaining or increasing driving range. Solid-state batteries are also expected to offer safety advantages because solid electrolytes are less prone to the thermal runaway associated with some conventional lithium-ion battery systems. The technology could also provide improved performance under certain temperature conditions. BYD Previously Targeted 2027 for Demonstration The 2027 timeline is consistent with plans announced by BYD in February 2025. At the time, Sun Huajun, technical director of BYD’s FinDreams battery division, said the company planned to begin demonstrating and installing solid-state batteries in vehicles in 2027. Mass production was expected to follow around 2030. BYD’s latest comments therefore reinforce the company’s previously stated development timeline rather than introducing a completely new target. Higher-End Models Expected to Use the Technology First The high cost of producing solid-state batteries remains one of the challenges facing wider adoption. Because of this, BYD is expected to initially use the technology in higher-end models. BYD Chief Scientist Lian Yubo previously said solid-state batteries would mainly be used in high-end models while lithium iron phosphate batteries continue to serve vehicles across different segments. This means the introduction of solid-state technology is not expected to replace BYD’s existing battery technologies across its entire vehicle range. Context is everything. The company’s approach is to use different battery technologies according to the requirements and positioning of individual vehicles. Solid-state batteries could therefore initially serve vehicles where their higher energy density and potential range benefits can justify higher production costs. As production technology develops, costs could become an important factor in determining how widely solid-state batteries are adopted. Other Automakers Are Developing Solid-State Batteries BYD is among several major automotive companies working on solid-state battery technology. Toyota has previously targeted 2027–2028 for vehicles using solid-state batteries. Mercedes-Benz has also been testing solid-state battery technology, while Stellantis has been conducting road testing involving a solid-state battery-powered electric vehicle. Honda has also been working with QuantumScape on solid-state battery development. The activity across several automakers reflects continued investment in battery technologies that could increase electric vehicle range and improve battery performance. Cost Remains a Major Challenge Despite the potential advantages, solid-state batteries remain more expensive to produce than established lithium-ion battery technologies. Manufacturers must also develop production processes capable of producing the batteries at automotive scale. For BYD, the initial use of solid-state batteries in higher-end vehicles could allow the company to introduce the technology while continuing to use established battery systems across its broader vehicle lineup. The company has not indicated that traditional lithium-based batteries will be phased out following the introduction of solid-state technology. artigo.texto: India’s carbon market is being built under pressure from a trade system in which emissions are becoming a direct cost of exporting. The European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, which entered its definitive phase in January 2026, requires importers to account for the carbon embedded in selected goods. For Indian steel, aluminium, cement and fertiliser producers, the issue is no longer only how much they manufacture or sell, but how much carbon is associated with every unit reaching a foreign market. That shift changes the meaning of industrial competitiveness. An Indian factory can comply with conventional export requirements and still face a commercial disadvantage if its production is more carbon-intensive than that of competitors. The EU importer pays the border charge, but the cost can travel back through lower margins, higher prices or reduced demand for Indian goods. The United Kingdom is preparing a similar mechanism for January 2027, widening the number of markets in which carbon intensity could influence export economics. India’s response is centred on the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, or CCTS, and on efforts to make domestic carbon pricing part of a broader industrial transition. The policy objective is twofold: retain some carbon-related economic value within India and reduce the emissions that generate charges abroad. The second objective is harder. A domestic market can allocate a price to emissions, but it cannot by itself provide the clean electricity, transmission, storage and production technologies required to lower emissions at scale. The size of the exposure makes this more than a climate-policy question. India’s merchandise exports reached $441.78 billion in FY26, according to the supplied report, while metals remained a major export category. The European mechanism currently covers iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen. These sectors are closely tied to heavy industry, energy consumption and the infrastructure of industrial production. NITI Aayog’s Trade Watch Quarterly, as cited in the report, puts India’s annual metals exports at about $34.8 billion in 2025. Iron, steel and aluminium accounted for roughly 78% of that trade. The EU represented approximately 22% of India’s combined steel and aluminium exports, while the EU exposure for iron and steel stood at 39.3%. That means the European market is not a marginal destination for Indian metal producers. For steel exporters in particular, changes in the cost of carbon can affect a substantial part of their external market. The export numbers also show why the timing matters. India exported 6.94 lakh tonnes of finished steel worth ₹5,541.2 crore in August 2026, according to the report, with volume up 31.3% and value up 41.5% from August 2025. Between April and August, finished-steel exports reached 29.86 lakh tonnes worth ₹23,646.6 crore, representing increases of 34.1% in volume and 32% in value. Strong export growth can increase exposure to carbon-related trade costs if production systems remain emissions-intensive. The structural difficulty lies in how Indian metals are produced. NITI Aayog’s Trade Watch Quarterly for April-June, or Q1 FY27, said Indian metals have notably higher carbon intensity than the global average. The report attributed this largely to the continued importance of coal-based Blast Furnace–Basic Oxygen Furnace routes in primary steelmaking and coal-fired Direct Reduced Iron processes, rather than cleaner gas-based or Electric Arc Furnace routes. This production profile means the carbon problem cannot be solved through documentation alone. Indian exporters need to measure and verify embedded emissions, but lower paperwork does not equal lower emissions. The trade system may reward accurate reporting in the short term, yet the lasting competitive advantage will come from changing the energy and technology used in factories. A June 2026 working paper by the Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations estimated that India’s steel exports to the EU could fall by 24% under CBAM. The estimate is based on simulations using the ICRIER Samriddhi Model, a GTAP-E-based general-equilibrium model. It is therefore a modelled scenario rather than an observed fall in exports, but it illustrates the scale of the risk facing a sector with significant European exposure. India has begun building the administrative architecture needed to respond. The Central government notified the CCTS in June 2023 under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act. The scheme is overseen by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and uses emissions-intensity targets rather than an absolute production cap. Targets become stricter each year and operate in two-year compliance cycles beginning in FY 2025-26. According to a Press Information Bureau release cited in the report, the system covers more than 700 industrial units across seven emissions-intensive sectors, including steel, aluminium and refining. Companies that perform better than their assigned targets can earn tradeable Carbon Credit Certificates, with each certificate representing one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent reduction. Companies that fail to meet their targets can face penalties. The framework has also expanded to include sectors such as petroleum refining, petrochemicals, textiles and secondary aluminium. The design reflects an attempt to connect industrial performance with market incentives. Yet the value of that incentive will depend on the strength of the market and the price attached to each reduction. Ajay Srivastava, founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative, said the EU carbon price was about €75 per tonne of carbon dioxide, compared with roughly $10 in China, while India’s emissions-trading system would take time to become fully operational. His assessment was that recognition of India’s system overseas would not necessarily remove the border charge because a substantial price gap could remain.

artigo.texto: Os bombardeios russos deste domingo (27) atingiram em cheio a espinha dorsal das telecomunicações ucranianas: a sede da Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia móvel do país, e data centers de concorrentes e provedores de internet foram alvos de ataques na região de Kiev. Segundo a Reuters, a Kyivstar informou à agência Interfax Ucrânia que sua sede na capital foi atingida, sem registro de vítimas. Horas antes, o Ministério da Defesa da Rússia havia declarado ter destruído um data center pertencente à Vodafone Ucrânia, segunda maior operadora celular do país. A companhia não respondeu aos pedidos de comentário. O presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy afirmou que um data center em Kiev foi bombardeado duas vezes na manhã deste domingo, deixando dois menores e um adulto feridos. Na semana anterior, ataques a data centers de provedores de internet ucranianos já haviam interrompido o serviço para cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev e na região vizinha, conforme o Ministério Digital da Ucrânia. O ministro das Relações Exteriores, Andrii Sybiha, escreveu no X que Moscou tem como alvo os principais data centers do país para interromper o fluxo de informações, e que alertas rápidos sobre ameaças de mísseis e drones são essenciais porque salvam vidas.

artigo.texto: Lao Cai se prepara para participar do mercado de créditos de carbono florestal. Na tarde de 29 de setembro, o Sr. Phan Trung Bá, Vice-Presidente do Comitê Popular Provincial, presidiu uma reunião para discutir o desenvolvimento de serviços de sequestro e armazenamento de carbono, a redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa e a exploração eficaz do potencial e das vantagens florestais, preparando assim as condições necessárias para que Lao Cai participe do mercado de créditos de carbono florestal. Estiveram presentes na reunião líderes dos Departamentos de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, Finanças, Indústria e Comércio, Construção, Ciência e Tecnologia; do Subdepartamento de Proteção Florestal e do Fundo Provincial de Proteção Florestal e Ambiental. Segundo um relatório do Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, na implementação do Decreto Governamental nº 180/2026/ND-CP sobre serviços de sequestro e armazenamento de carbono florestal, a província de Lao Cai está gradualmente concluindo seu banco de dados e preparando as condições necessárias para o desenvolvimento de projetos de carbono florestal. Até o momento, a província concluiu o levantamento do estado das florestas e das reservas de carbono florestal em 48 municípios e distritos da região norte. Os resultados indicam uma reserva total de carbono de 14,33 milhões de toneladas. O Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente finalizou o esboço e o orçamento para o levantamento do estado das florestas para o período de 2026-2027 em 51 comunas e distritos da região sul, servindo como base para a construção de linhas de referência para projetos de carbono na província. Além de investigar e avaliar o potencial, a província está preparando as condições necessárias em termos de mecanismos, projetos e recursos para desenvolver créditos de carbono florestal. O Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente prestou consultoria sobre o desenvolvimento de conteúdo relacionado à gestão e ao uso de créditos de carbono; elaborou o documento do projeto "Transformando os Resultados da Redução de Emissões e a Gestão Florestal Sustentável no Vietnã, Província de Lao Cai", financiado pelo Fundo Verde para o Clima (GCF). Simultaneamente, está desenvolvendo o plano técnico e o orçamento para o projeto de créditos de carbono em florestas de propriedade de toda a população. Você também pode gostar Segundo o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, os projetos de desenvolvimento de carbono florestal são uma área nova, sendo implementados pela primeira vez na província. O processo de implementação ainda requer aprimoramento em diversas áreas, principalmente no que diz respeito aos requisitos técnicos, padrões econômico -técnicos, sistemas de medição, relatórios, avaliação e verificação dos resultados da redução de emissões. Na reunião, os delegados concentraram-se na discussão da investigação e desenvolvimento de uma base de dados florestal e de carbono; métodos de medição, monitorização e digitalização de dados; recursos para implementação; e as condições necessárias para a implementação do projeto de crédito de carbono florestal na província. Ao concluir a reunião, o Sr. Phan Trung Bá, Vice-Presidente do Comitê Popular Provincial, enfatizou que o desenvolvimento de créditos de carbono florestal está passando da fase de pesquisa para a implementação concreta, com demandas cada vez maiores em relação a dados, base legal, recursos e capacidade de implementação. Portanto, o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente precisa assessorar proativamente e preparar dados de entrada suficientes sobre florestas, como base para a integração com o sistema geral de dados e para servir à gestão e ao desenvolvimento do mercado de carbono. O camarada solicitou ao Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente que continue investigando e atualizando o estado atual das florestas em 51 comunas e distritos; e, ao mesmo tempo, revise e delimite especificamente as áreas florestais, especialmente naquelas onde a entidade gestora não foi claramente identificada. Com isso, o objetivo é completar gradualmente o banco de dados florestal e preparar as condições para o desenvolvimento de créditos de carbono na província. Você também pode gostar Em relação aos recursos para implementação, o camarada Phan Trung Bá solicitou ao Departamento de Finanças que revisasse e assessorasse sobre a alocação de verbas para atividades de proteção florestal, levantamentos do estado das florestas e implementação de projetos de carbono florestal. Quanto ao orçamento proposto, ele enfatizou que se trata apenas de uma estimativa inicial, servindo de base para o desenvolvimento de um plano e orçamento detalhados. O uso dos recursos deve ser calculado com base em normas estabelecidas, conteúdo e etapas reais de implementação, garantindo a conformidade com as normas e a eficácia. O vice-presidente do Comitê Popular Provincial também enfatizou que a gestão e a exploração de informações e dados sobre carbono florestal devem ser realizadas com rigor. Organizações e empresas que necessitem realizar levantamentos e avaliações de recursos florestais para projetos de carbono devem ser orientadas de acordo com as normas, prevenindo o risco de exploração indevida de levantamentos e avaliações para fins de exploração, troca ou transferência de informações e dados sobre recursos de carbono. Além disso, o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, em coordenação com o Departamento de Ciência e Tecnologia, está pesquisando soluções tecnológicas e equipamentos para apoiar a investigação, medição e coleta de dados sobre florestas; e preparando informações para integrar e digitalizar gradualmente os dados florestais da província. O vice-presidente do Comitê Popular Provincial, Phan Trung Bá, solicitou que os departamentos e agências continuem a coordenar pesquisas e a fornecer consultoria sobre a avaliação da capacidade de absorção de carbono das florestas; proponham soluções para melhorar a qualidade e o valor das flor

artigo.texto: No dia 29 de setembro, a Academia Vietnamita de Ciências Florestais, por meio do Centro Vietnamita de Certificação de Gestão Florestal (VFCC), em colaboração com a Forest Trends, organizou um workshop de consulta sobre "Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (SbN) para a Restauração Florestal Após a Extração Mineral e Oportunidades de Participação no Futuro Mercado de Carbono". Restauração florestal após mineração: abrindo oportunidades para participar do mercado de carbono. (Chinhphu.vn) - De acordo com especialistas, a aplicação de soluções NbS não só ajuda a regenerar a vegetação nativa e a restaurar ecossistemas danificados pela mineração, como também abre grandes oportunidades para que empresas e localidades participem do mercado de carbono no futuro. Durante o workshop, especialistas argumentaram que, embora muitas commodities que representam risco de desmatamento, como madeira, café, borracha, soja e óleo de palma, estejam sujeitas a requisitos de controle cada vez mais rigorosos, as atividades de mineração, apesar de seu impacto significativo nas florestas, ainda não foram inseridas em uma estrutura de governança proporcional. O Dr. To Xuan Phuc, especialista da Forest Trends, observou que o impacto da mineração na vegetação e nos ecossistemas florestais está se tornando cada vez mais evidente, mas os minerais raramente são reconhecidos como uma "mercadoria com risco de desmatamento". Isso cria uma lacuna nas políticas públicas, já que a cadeia de suprimentos de minerais ainda não atende aos requisitos equivalentes em relação à responsabilidade pela proteção e restauração florestal. Essa ausência cria uma lacuna significativa em termos legais e políticos. Enquanto os produtos de madeira e café passam por rigorosos processos de due diligence para verificar sua origem não desmatada antes de entrarem em mercados exigentes, a cadeia de suprimentos de minerais carece de obrigações comparáveis em relação à proteção e restauração florestal. Segundo especialistas, as atividades de mineração podem levar à perda de vegetação, perturbar a estrutura do solo, fragmentar habitats, aumentar o risco de deslizamentos de terra e poluir fontes de água. Análises de sensoriamento remoto também mostram um declínio na cobertura vegetal em muitas áreas de mineração, enquanto a infraestrutura que serve à mineração pode aumentar a pressão sobre as florestas próximas. No Vietnã, foram emitidas regulamentações sobre a conversão de terras florestais e os depósitos para restauração ambiental, mas sua implementação ainda é limitada. A restauração pós-florestamento em algumas áreas não restaurou completamente as funções ecológicas da floresta e não está intimamente ligada aos padrões de manejo florestal sustentável. Integrar a restauração florestal na governança da mineração. Dr. Tran Lam Dong , Vice-Diretor da Academia Vietnamita de Ciências Florestais. Conclusão: É hora de as agências reguladoras mudarem sua mentalidade e considerarem o controle do impacto da indústria de mineração nas florestas como parte integrante da estratégia nacional de proteção florestal e resposta às mudanças climáticas. Especialistas propõem considerar os minerais como um fator de controle de risco para o desmatamento, estabelecer padrões obrigatórios de responsabilização e avaliações de impacto florestal para projetos de licenciamento de mineração; fortalecer os mecanismos de coordenação intersetorial e conectar estreitamente as agências de gestão de recursos minerais e as agências de gestão florestal ao longo de todo o ciclo de vida do projeto de mineração, desde o planejamento e licenciamento até o fechamento da mina e a restauração ambiental. Uma das abordagens discutidas no workshop foi a aplicação de Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (SbN) para restaurar áreas florestais impactadas pela mineração. O professor Vu Tan Phuong, diretor do Centro de Certificação de Gestão Florestal do Vietnã (VFCC), afirmou que a aplicação de soluções de NbS não só ajuda a regenerar a vegetação nativa e a restaurar ecossistemas danificados pela mineração, como também abre grandes oportunidades para que empresas e localidades participem do mercado de carbono no futuro. Segundo o Professor Vu Tan Phuong, as áreas onde as operações de mineração são restauradas, se devidamente reflorestadas e restauradas ecologicamente de acordo com os padrões de Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (SbN), gerarão um sequestro significativo de carbono. Esse aumento nos estoques de carbono pode ser medido, relatado e verificado (MRV) para ser convertido em créditos de carbono florestal de alta qualidade. Isso oferece um benefício duplo: apoia as empresas no cumprimento de suas responsabilidades sociais e ambientais, ao mesmo tempo que gera financiamento adicional com a venda de créditos de carbono nos mercados nacional e internacional, criando um incentivo econômico intrínseco para o reflorestamento pós-mineração. artigo.texto: The Clackamas County Board of County Commissioners will hold two public hearings to consider adopting a temporary moratorium on data center development in unincorporated Clackamas County. The hearings give community members a chance to share their opinions on the potential moratorium and provide concerns and other feedback about data centers. Public hearing dates: Wednesday, Oct. 21, 6 p.m. Board Meeting Room, 4th floor Clackamas County Public Services Building 2051 Kaen Road Oregon City, OR Thursday, Oct. 22, 10 a.m. Board Meeting Room, 4th floor Clackamas County Public Services Building 2051 Kaen Road Oregon City, OR Can't attend in person or virtually? You can submit written testimony to bcc@clackamas.us, and it will be included in the record. What to expect County staff will provide information about the criteria for establishing a moratorium. The staff presentation will focus on those criteria. Staff will not propose changes to county code related to data centers during these hearings. If the Board adopts a moratorium, public input received during the hearings could help inform the Board's consideration of future code changes. About data centers Data centers are facilities that house computer systems and related equipment used to store, process, and manage digital information. The growth of artificial intelligence and cloud computing is contributing to increased data center development nationwide. Data centers can involve considerations related to land use, energy, water, infrastructure, noise, and other factors. The National Association of Counties (NACo) has developed an informational resource for county officials that provides an overview of data center development and topics counties may consider as they evaluate local regulations. Learn more: NACo Informational Primer and County Considerations: Data Centers

artigo.texto: A WEG anunciou a ampliação do projeto da nova fábrica de sistemas BESS, de armazenamento de energia em baterias, em construção em Itajaí. Anunciada em fevereiro deste ano, a unidade terá investimento estimado de R$ 330 milhões e capacidade anual de 4 GWh. A nova fábrica vai atender à demanda ligada à transição energética e tem início das operações previsto pro segundo semestre de 2027. O projeto reforça a estratégia da empresa de acompanhar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil, que está prestes a lançar o primeiro leilão de baterias, previsto ... O projeto reforça a estratégia da empresa de acompanhar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil, que está prestes a lançar o primeiro leilão de baterias, previsto pra dezembro. Na atualização do projeto, a WEG incorporou maior nível de automação e ganhos de eficiência industrial que permitirão ampliar a capacidade produtiva. Continua depois da publicidade A fábrica contará com linhas automáticas e semiautomáticas de montagem, além de robôs móveis autônomos para movimentações internas. O complexo também terá um laboratório de testes, desenvolvimento e qualificação de produtos, responsável por aprimorar processos, garantir o controle de qualidade e acelerar a criação de novas soluções em baterias. Segundo o vice-presidente de automação e sistemas da WEG, Manfred Peter Johann, o investimento está alinhado à forte expansão do mercado de armazenamento de energia, impulsionado pelo crescimento das fontes renováveis e pela necessidade de maior flexibilidade e segurança pro sistema elétrico. “A ampliação deste projeto demonstra a capacidade da WEG de adaptar rapidamente seus investimentos para atender às necessidades do mercado e apoiar o desenvolvimento sustentável do setor energético brasileiro”, comenta. As baterias produzidas em Itajaí vão ajudar na estabilidade do sistema elétrico, na eficiência operacional e no aproveitamento dos recursos energéticos. O BESS, sigla em inglês para Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias, é uma tecnologia avançada que armazena energia elétrica em grandes baterias. A solução tem papel importante nos sistemas elétricos modernos, principalmente na integração de fontes renováveis, como solar e eólica, permitindo guardar energia nos momentos de maior disponibilidade e ofertá-la quando necessário.

artigo.texto: Kern supervisors approve new solar, battery storage near California City BAKERSFIELD, Calif. (KGET) – The Kern County Board of Supervisors have approved a new solar project for the county. The Board approved the request to build a solar facility called the Galaxy Solar PV and Storage Project, which developers say will bring millions of dollars to the county. With the Board's new approval, Terra-Gen, the solar development company, can take the next step forward in constructing the solar facility, which will generate 600 megawatts of electricity and four gigawatt-hours of battery energy storage. Craig Murphy, director of the Kern County Planning & Natural Resources Department, told the Board of Supervisors on Tuesday, Sept. 29, that the project is proposed to be built on 184 parcels – about 3,519 acres – of land in California City. He said the project would be built and live on the southern side of Highway 58, approximately 2,900 feet east of Highway 14, straddling both the north and south sides of Silver Queen Road. County documents show that project's site is on privately owned land in unincorporated areas of southeastern Kern County. Sam Sours, Terra-Gen's vice president of solar development, told the Board on Tuesday afternoon that the Galaxy Solar project is estimating about $16.1 million in property taxes during its first full year of operation. He said the project is expected to generate about $120 million in property tax contributions over the facility's 35-year lifespan. Sours added that the project would help the state meet its goal of 60% of electric retail sales by 2030. He said the project will employ about 350 people – 650 workers during peak times of construction – and that the facility's employees will be hired through a local union labor, adding that the worker's agreement has already been signed. With the project's approval representatives from Terra-Gen said that Joshua Trees in the vicinity of the project will be moved wholly and rerooted in a tree sanctuary in Los Angeles County. artigo.texto: Schneider Electric Unveils World's First Software-Defined Medium Voltage Switchgear to Expand AI-Ready Data Center Power Portfolio - World's first fully Software-Defined Medium Voltage architecture enables up to 3× faster ordering and manufacturing, up to 2× faster commissioning and zero-downtime upgrades - RM AirSeT™ 38 Software Defined extends Schneider Electric's SF₆-free medium-voltage technology to 38 kV for high-density, scalable data center architectures "The challenge facing data center operators today is not just keeping pace with AI growth, but building the resilient, efficient and scalable power infrastructure needed for an increasingly digital world," said Frédéric Godemel, Executive Vice President, Software-Defined Medium Voltage establishes a new category of power infrastructure Building on its broader Software-Defined Energy vision, Based on the comparison documented in Schneider Electric White Paper 303, the approach enables up to 3× faster ordering and manufacturing, up to 2× faster commissioning and onsite acceptance testing, compared with conventional engineered-to-order medium-voltage switchgear. It also reduces system complexity: in the 20-panel comparison, the software-defined configuration used 87% less control wiring, 91% fewer terminals and 85% less copper in that wiring, while providing digital connectivity and analytics for greater operational visibility. Key elements of the Software-Defined MV architecture include: - Standardized, configurable infrastructure: Replaces highly customized, engineered-to-order systems with modular hardware that can be standardized and deployed more quickly. - Software-enabled functionality: Shifts capabilities from hardware into software, allowing customers to add new features and performance improvements without physical modifications. - Digital-first deployment: Standardized modules, automated testing, and intuitive interfaces help streamline ordering, manufacturing, commissioning, and onsite acceptance. - Lifecycle flexibility: Over-the-air updates enable system upgrades without hardware replacement or operational downtime, while software-enabled capabilities support ongoing optimization and AI-powered predictive maintenance through EcoCare Services. The Software-Defined MV approach has been deployed in live operation through a pilot with Equinix in a colocation data center environment. Pilot programs continue through 2027, with broader availability to follow in 2028. To learn more, visit the Software-Defined MV switchgear page or read the Software-Defined MV white paper. To receive product and availability updates, register your interest. RM AirSeT 38 Software Defined extends SF₆-free MV gas-insulated switchgear to 38 kV As AI, high-performance computing and large-scale digital infrastructure drive rising power densities, many operators are planning 36/38 kV MV architectures to support higher power capacity, simplified MV backbone design, and scalable campus deployment. RM AirSeT 38 meets that need, giving hyperscalers and colocation providers greater flexibility as they modernize their electrical distribution strategies. RM AirSeT 38 is designed to support high-density, scalable deployments through: - SF ₆ -free technology: Uses pressurized pure air insulation and vacuum interruption technology instead of SF₆ (sulfur hexafluoride, a potent greenhouse gas), fluorinated gases, or proprietary gas mixtures. - Compact GIS design: Supports space-constrained, high-density installations while enabling standardized, repeatable MV architecture across data center deployments. - Software-defined capabilities: A standardized digital architecture designed to simplify configuration, accelerate commissioning and support lifecycle evolution. - Operational visibility: Digital monitoring and sensing options provide visibility into system performance, configurable to each customer's cybersecurity requirements. Order intake is planned to begin in 2027, with first deliveries expected in 2028. To receive updates on RM AirSeT 38, register your interest. Galaxy VXL brings high-density As AI deployments drive higher rack densities and more dynamic load profiles, data center operators need power infrastructure that responds quickly to fluctuating demand while maximizing white space. Galaxy VXL helps customers maintain reliable, high-quality power delivery for scalable growth and continuity in AI and high-performance computing environments. Key benefits include: - Industry-leading power density: Delivers up to 1.25 MW in a single frame while using up to 70% less space than predecessor systems, helping customers maximize IT capacity and floor space. - Optimized efficiency and sustainability: Galaxy VXL is designed to drive energy-efficient operations, lowering total cost of ownership, and support long-term sustainability initiatives – delivering a 31% reduction in lifecycle CO₂ emissions compared with its predecessor. - Validated for AI workloads: Designed for the dynamic power profiles associated with AI clusters and high-density compute environments, helping ensure power quality, resilience, and availability. - Scalable, service-friendly architecture: Schneider Electric's third-party verified Live Swap technology lets operators add, upgrade, or replace power modules without planned downtime, supporting future expansion while maintaining uptime. - Digital-first operations: Integrated EcoStruxure™ monitoring and digital services provide visibility, predictive maintenance, and lifecycle optimization across critical power infrastructure. Availability Galaxy VXL is available globally and supports both Lithium-ion and VRLA battery technologies, providing customers with flexible energy storage options to meet their resiliency, performance, and sustainability requirements. artigo.texto: Volkswagen Group, PowerCo and China's Gotion have agreed plans for three battery joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia and Morocco, involving combined estimated investment of approximately €3.22bn ($3.65bn). Gotion is expected to invest about €1.59bn, while PowerCo – Volkswagen's battery manufacturing subsidiary – will contribute approximately €1.62bn. The ventures are planned to produce lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells and cathode materials in Valencia, Šurany and Kenitra. Volkswagen Group technology management board member and PowerCo supervisory board chairman Thomas Schmall said: "This marks a major breakthrough for both companies and brings us one step closer to the forefront of electric mobility. "Volkswagen is the first European automotive manufacturer to cover the entire battery value chain, from development and cathode materials through to production." In Valencia, PowerCo's under-construction gigafactory is expected to transfer into a joint venture producing LFP cells, with an annual capacity of 29.1GWh. PowerCo will hold 51% and Gotion 49%, making the venture a controlled PowerCo subsidiary. Gotion is expected to invest about €1.1bn for its stake. The Valencia facility is intended to serve as a European production hub for Volkswagen's LFP-based Unified Cells. Gotion's planned cell factory in Šurany will also transfer into a joint venture. The facility will have an annual capacity of 8.4GWh and produce LFP cells for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Gotion will own 51%, with PowerCo holding 49%. In Kenitra, the companies plan to establish a facility producing 100,000t of LFP cathode material annually. Gotion will retain a 51% stake, while PowerCo will own 49%. The project is intended to diversify supply sources for key cathode active materials. PowerCo is expected to contribute approximately €470m to the Šurany and Kenitra projects by 2030 for its 49% stake in each project. The agreement extends a partnership that began in 2020 and covers joint procurement and sales activities in Europe. The transactions remain subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, including approval from Gotion shareholders and governmental approvals in China and overseas. Gotion said implementation would take place in phases. Volkswagen Group, through its subsidiary Volkswagen (China) Investment, has also entered definitive agreements to sell a 5.3% equity stake in Gotion. The company said its voting rights, board representation, nomination rights and position as a strategic investor would remain unchanged after completion.

artigo.texto: Companies sign MOU to explore collaboration on deployable structures, spacecraft integration and scalable architectures for in-orbit Artificial Intelligence and edge computing LAS VEGAS , Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sophia Space and Redwire Corporation (NYSE: RDW), a global leader in aerospace and defense technology solutions, today announced they have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to advance the development and deployment of scalable computing infrastructure in orbit, combining Sophia Space's modular orbital compute architecture with Redwire's extensive technology solutions in deployable space systems, solar power generation and distribution, heat management and rejection, spacecraft integration, avionics, and systems engineering. Under the MOU, the companies will explore collaboration across near-term demonstration missions and longer-term orbital data center architectures. Sophia Space is developing a new class of computing infrastructure designed specifically for the space environment. Its modular TILE architecture integrates high-performance computing, solar power and passive radiative thermal management into scalable systems designed for Artificial Intelligence (AI) inference, data processing and other compute-intensive workloads in orbit. By combining Sophia Space's compute architecture with Redwire's space infrastructure and engineering capabilities, the companies aim to address one of the central challenges facing the emerging orbital computing market: moving from individual technology demonstrations toward the repeatable, scalable infrastructure needed for the global build-out of orbital data centers. "We're past the point of asking whether high-performance computing belongs in orbit," said Rob DeMillo, CEO and Cofounder of Sophia Space. "The question now is how quickly we can scale it. Redwire brings the deployment and systems expertise that can help us move from individual missions to persistent computing infrastructure in orbit. That is the transition we're building toward now." "The demand for global computing is scaling exponentially, and the advancement of orbital data centers represents an exciting paradigm shift where space infrastructure can scale critical capacity beyond the constraints of terrestrial infrastructure," said Al Tadros, Chief Technology Officer, Redwire Space. "As a leading space infrastructure provider, Redwire is translating the maturation of the orbital data center market into exciting opportunities to build next-generation architectures that could unlock significant economic value. Sophia Space and Redwire intend to jointly pursue select U.S. government and commercial opportunities, including potential programs involving DARPA, the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL), the Space Development Agency (SDA) and the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO). Areas of potential collaboration include concept development, joint proposals, internal research and development activities, customer engagement, and international market opportunities. --- About Sophia Space Inc. Sophia Space is building the future of orbital computing and in-space data centers. Its modular TILE technology enables passive computing alongside in-situ data processing, AI acceleration, and edge computing for satellites, defense systems, and commercial space stations, dramatically reducing latency and delivering actionable insights where and when they are needed. Learn more at www.sophia.space About Redwire Redwire Corporation (NYSE: RDW) is an integrated space and defense tech company focused on advanced technologies. We are building the future of aerospace infrastructure, autonomous systems, and multi-domain operations leveraging digital engineering and AI automation. Redwire's approximately 1,400 employees located throughout North America and Europe are committed to delivering innovative space and airborne platforms transforming the future of multi-domain operations. For more information, please visit RDW.com.
