artigo.texto: PowerCo Advances St Thomas Gigafactory with EllisDon Appointment and Phased Development Approach - EllisDon appointed as general contractor as construction advances, with on-site workforce ramping toward ~1,300 at peak - Project progressing through a phased, demand-aligned build, with production ramp-up to scale over time - Major Canadian investment supporting jobs, suppliers, and long-term economic growth across the region ST. THOMAS, ONTARIO – September 24, 2026 – PowerCo Canada today announced it has selected leading Canadian construction firm EllisDon Corporation as general contractor for its St. Thomas gigafactory, marking a key milestone as the project advances into its next phase of construction. The appointment enables work on-site to continue building on steady progress since groundbreaking in 2025. Construction is now moving into core infrastructure and structural phases that will support future production. Joel Karlsberg, Chief Procurement Officer, PowerCo Canada, said: Today’s announcement is an important step forward for St. Thomas, “Partnering with EllisDon allows us to keep construction moving while ensuring we retain the flexibility to scale the facility in line with market demand and long-term industry evolution.” Initial works are focused on the first phase of development, including core building structures and site-wide infrastructure needed to support future production. Construction includes the production-building shell, mechanical, electrical and plumbing installations, energy and utility systems, and supporting site services. Approximately 60 EllisDon workers are currently on site, expected to ramp up to roughly 1,300 workers at peak, alongside additional personnel supporting parallel project activities. Max Mantha, President, Construction, EllisDon, said: The PowerCo facility represents a transformative investment in Canada’s industrial future, and EllisDon is proud to play a role in its delivery, “As a Canadian-headquartered, employee-owned company, we are committed to building the infrastructure that will help support Canada’s growing electric vehicle and battery manufacturing sector. This project will create opportunities for skilled tradespeople, local businesses, and communities across southwestern Ontario, and we look forward to working with PowerCo and our partners on this landmark development.” In parallel, PowerCo is aligning the project’s timeline and product strategy with evolving market demand, technological advancements, and the Volkswagen Group’s long-term strategy. St. Thomas is now expected to begin operations in 2029 to accommodate next-generation battery technology, while retaining the flexibility to scale over time as market conditions evolve. Karlsberg, said: The St. Thomas gigafactory remains a cornerstone of our North American strategy, “We are continuing to build now while determining how and when the facility scales over time. This is about getting the pacing right—not stepping back—to protect our long-term investment, support regional jobs, and position Canada, Ontario, and St. Thomas to benefit in a dynamic and evolving market.” READ the latest Batteries News shaping the battery market PowerCo Advances St Thomas Gigafactory with EllisDon Appointment and Phased Development Approach, source

artigo.texto: Advait Battery Ecosystem Private Limited, a subsidiary of BSE and NSE listed Advait Energy Transitions Limited, has entered into a Master Supply Agreement with HiTHIUM for the supply of lithium iron phosphate battery cells. The agreement will support Advait’s planned 2.5 GWh annual capacity cell to container Battery Energy Storage System assembly facility in Gujarat. HiTHIUM to supply 314 Ah LFP cells Under the agreement, HiTHIUM will supply its 314 Ah lithium iron phosphate prismatic cells to Advait. The arrangement is structured to support cell offtake of up to 1 GWh over the next year. It is expected to create a high volume supply framework as Advait scales domestic BESS assembly for utility scale, commercial and industrial and renewable energy applications in India. The cells will form part of Advait’s planned capabilities covering module and pack assembly, container integration and system commissioning. Advait building domestic BESS manufacturing capacity Advait’s 2.5 GWh BESS cell to container assembly facility is under development in Gangad, Gujarat. The facility is scheduled to begin commercial production soon. The company said the plant is being developed to serve grid scale energy storage, commercial and industrial applications and renewable energy integration projects. The Hithium agreement will provide a supply framework as the facility moves towards commercial production and volume manufacturing. Partnership strengthens integrated energy storage platform Advait said the agreement is part of its strategy to build an integrated battery energy storage manufacturing ecosystem in India. The company has also entered into a strategic collaboration with Adaptive Engineering for engineering design, Energy Management System architecture, PLC and SCADA systems and integration capabilities. With the latest agreement, Advait aims to combine cell sourcing, engineering, module and pack assembly, container integration and system commissioning under its domestic BESS platform. Advait Energy Transitions expands clean energy portfolio Advait Energy Transitions is a Gujarat based power and renewable energy company. Its portfolio includes battery energy storage manufacturing, green hydrogen project development, electrolyser manufacturing, fuel cell manufacturing and clean energy EPC services. The Hithium agreement supports the group’s wider expansion across energy transition technologies and related infrastructure.

artigo.texto: As fabricantes de baterias Moura e WEG, além da Associação Brasileira da Indústria de Máquinas e Equipamentos (Abimaq), defenderam que a exigência de conteúdo nacional no leilão de reserva de capacidade de baterias alcance também equipamentos incorporados aos sistemas ao longo dos 15 anos de contrato, inclusive em substituições e ampliações destinadas a compensar a degradação dos ativos. As propostas foram apresentadas nas consultas públicas da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) sobre os dois leilões de baterias previstos para dezembro. A exigência de nacionalização é específica do certame do dia 2 de dezembro, quando há exigência de conteúdo nacional. Outros pontos, como a aferição da eficiência dos sistemas e as penalidades previstas nos contratos, foram discutidos nas duas consultas. Pela minuta do edital do leilão nacional, o empreendedor deverá comprovar junto ao Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) o atendimento aos requisitos de nacionalização e conteúdo local aplicáveis aos sistemas de armazenamento. WEG e Abimaq propuseram deixar expresso que a obrigação continuará válida durante todo o período de suprimento, de 1º de agosto de 2028 a 31 de julho de 2043. Assim, equipamentos, módulos, sistemas ou componentes incorporados posteriormente para ampliação, substituição, recomposição ou manutenção da capacidade contratada também teriam de atender às mesmas exigências previstas para a implantação inicial. As entidades argumentam que a operação por 15 anos poderá exigir novos equipamentos em razão da degradação das baterias e que a ausência de uma regra específica para essas substituições pode permitir tratamento diferente para componentes instalados posteriormente. “A ausência de previsão expressa para a aplicação dos requisitos de conteúdo local às futuras aumentações poderá criar uma assimetria regulatória”, afirmam as contribuições. A Moura apresentou proposta semelhante. A empresa pediu que a exigência também seja aplicada a substituições e ampliações feitas durante o período de suprimento, por degradação, reinvestimento, defeito ou falha de equipamentos. Eficiência das baterias A forma de medir a eficiência total dos sistemas, ou round-trip efficiency (RTE), também recebeu propostas de alteração. As diretrizes estabelecem eficiência mínima de 85%, enquanto a minuta contratual prevê apuração mensal de ressarcimento quando o desempenho ficar abaixo desse patamar. A Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (Absae) propôs que os efeitos financeiros sejam apurados anualmente, mantendo a medição mensal para acompanhamento. Segundo a entidade, o resultado mensal pode ser influenciado pelo perfil de despacho, temperatura, consumo auxiliar, tempo em espera e quantidade de ciclos realizados no período. A Associação Brasileira dos Produtores Independentes de Energia Elétrica (Apine) também sugeriu apuração anual. A entidade argumentou que meses com poucos ciclos ou longos períodos sem despacho podem não refletir adequadamente o desempenho do sistema e pediu que o cálculo considere os consumos necessários para manter a bateria disponível, como climatização, proteção e controle. A Associação Brasileira dos Investidores em Autoprodução de Energia (Abiape) propôs uma janela móvel de 12 meses e uma regra específica para períodos com baixa quantidade de dados. A Huawei também sugeriu apuração financeira anual, com acompanhamento mensal, e propôs uma referência de eficiência de 87% nos primeiros 36 meses de suprimento e de 85% a partir do 37º mês. A Sungrow apresentou outra metodologia. A empresa sugeriu aferir uma RTE de referência por meio de um ciclo padronizado de carga e descarga, com parâmetros definidos para potência, estado de carga, temperatura e consumos auxiliares. O resultado serviria de referência para a apuração econômica mensal. Penalidades do leilão As regras para indisponibilidade e descumprimento dos despachos do Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) também foram alvo de contribuições. Apine e Abiape pediram que um mesmo evento operacional não resulte em penalidades cumulativas. A Apine também propôs que as sanções sejam calculadas sobre a potência contratada, e não sobre a potência total instalada, caso o empreendimento tenha capacidade adicional. A Absae questionou a previsão pela qual o resultado parcial de um teste de disponibilidade solicitado pelo ONS pode produzir efeitos sobre todas as horas do mês. A associação sugeriu limitar a penalidade ao período em que a indisponibilidade estiver comprovada e permitir novo teste após a correção do problema. A entidade também pediu tratamento específico para situações em que o atendimento ao despacho seja afetado pelo estado de carga da bateria decorrente de comandos do ONS ou de outras condições operativas impostas ao sistema. Em outro ponto, a Absae questionou a possibilidade de uma mesma indisponibilidade provocar redução da receita fixa e, ao mesmo tempo, outras penalidades por falha de desempenho. A associação propôs retirar a redução adicional da receita ou impedir a acumulação de efeitos financeiros sobre o mesmo evento. A Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE) também sugeriu ajustes nas fórmulas de penalidade. Para a Câmara, a injeção de potência acima do montante determinado pelo ONS também deve ser considerada descumprimento do despacho, por poder reduzir a energia disponível para atendimento posterior. A CCEE propôs ainda que, quando o despacho em tempo real for reduzido por indisponibilidade da própria bateria, a penalidade considere o valor originalmente programado. Quando a alteração decorrer apenas de comando do ONS, sem responsabilidade do agente, deve ser considerado o montante efetivamente determinado em tempo real.

artigo.texto: Rússia ataca maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia e atinge data centers Cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev tiveram os serviços interrompidos Internacional|Da Reuters LEIA AQUI O RESUMO DA NOTÍCIA Produzido pela Ri7a - a Inteligência Artificial do R7 A Rússia atacou neste domingo (27) a sede da Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia, informou a empresa à mídia local, enquanto Moscou seguia com bombardeios a data centers e infraestrutura de comunicações ucranianos. A Kyivstar informou à agência de notícias Interfax Ucrânia que sua sede em Kiev havia sido atingida, mas não houve vítimas. O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia também informou neste domingo que atingiu um data center pertencente à Vodafone Ucrânia, segunda maior operadora de telefonia celular do país. A Vodafone Ucrânia não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, afirmou que a Rússia atacou um data center em Kiev duas vezes na manhã deste domingo, ferindo duas crianças e um adulto. Veja Também Moscou também atingiu data centers pertencentes a provedores de internet ucranianos na semana passada, causando interrupções no serviço para cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev e na região circundante, de acordo com o Ministério Digital da Ucrânia. “A Rússia tem como alvo os principais data centers ucranianos, buscando interromper o fluxo de informações. Alertas rápidos sobre ameaças de mísseis e drones são essenciais -- eles salvam vidas”, escreveu o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha, no X na quarta-feira. artigo.texto: RABAT (MOROCCO) (ITALPRESS) – Morocco is becoming increasingly integrated into new European industrial supply chains. The joint venture announced in Kenitra between Gotion High-Tech and PowerCo—a Volkswagen Group company—marks a new step in the Kingdom’s integration into the strategic supply chain for electric mobility batteries. According to the Moroccan news site Le360, the new plant involves an investment of approximately €480 million and will produce LFP (lithium iron phosphate) cathode materials, with a capacity reaching up to 100,000 tonnes per year. Most significant is the intended destination of this output: Kenitra will be linked to other industrial projects developed by Gotion and Volkswagen in Spain and Slovakia, effectively creating a production chain that spans both shores of the Mediterranean. The project illustrates the growing industrial complementarity between Morocco and the European Union; alongside traditional automotive manufacturing, the country is increasingly producing batteries, advanced materials, and technologies linked to transport decarbonization. The Kingdom’s geographical location, the competitiveness of its industrial platform, its infrastructure, and its growing reliance on renewable energy all boost its appeal at a time when Europe is aiming to diversify and build greater resilience into its supply chains. With this Gotion-Volkswagen investment, Kenitra is establishing itself not merely as an automotive hub, but as a key new Euro-Mediterranean node in the battery industry. – photo Pexels.com – (ITALPRESS).

artigo.texto: Arcadis innovates with sustainable solutions for data centers: engineering that transforms digital infrastructure. The company is embracing advanced technologies and energy efficiency to build sustainable data centers, reducing environmental impact and driving global digital transformation. São Paulo – As demand for digital infrastructure grows, data center energy consumption and environmental performance are receiving greater attention. With the goal of creating innovative and efficient solutions, Arcadis, a global leader in sustainable design, engineering, and consulting, is adopting technologies that combine sustainability, energy efficiency, and high performance in its projects. With the acceleration of digitalization, data centers can consume up to 50 times more energy than commercial buildings of the same size, accounting for up to 3% of global electricity consumption, according to industry data. Arcadis sees the transition to more sustainable digital infrastructure as both an environmental imperative and a smart business strategy. The company believes it is possible to combine high performance with technological innovation while reducing carbon emissions. “The growing demand for cleaner and more resilient digital infrastructure has driven a true revolution in data center design. At Arcadis, we combine our expertise in engineering and sustainability to support clients in building more efficient, future-ready solutions with a lower environmental impact. Arcadis’ approach to data centers takes a systemic, one-stop-shop view, which also addresses the challenges of electrical connections, water supply, and fiber,” says Isabel Rando, head of industry solutions at Arcadis. Innovative solutions for energy efficiency Arcadis has implemented various technologies to increase data center efficiency and minimize environmental impact. Key solutions include: - Energy and water optimization: Both are fundamental resources for data center operations, particularly in the pursuit of sustainability and net-zero goals. As major priorities for clients in the technology sector, the efficient use of these resources is becoming increasingly essential in data center deployment projects. - Smart environmental monitoring: Technologies that expand the thermal operating range of equipment without compromising durability, in accordance with American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) guidelines. This approach helps reduce energy consumption in cooling systems. - Use of battery energy storage systems (BESS): Replacing diesel generators with energy storage batteries contributes to data center decarbonization while providing greater efficiency and energy autonomy. Independent and strategic engineering for data centers In addition to technological solutions, Arcadis offers specialized independent engineering and owner’s engineering services, ensuring that projects meet clients’ technical, timeline, financial, and operational objectives. Through a strategic and impartial approach, the company helps protect the owner’s interests while treating sustainability, health, and safety as non-negotiable priorities. It also supports the minimization of technical and financial risks, strategic schedule management to meet project milestones, and alignment with industry best practices and client quality standards. A prime example of how Arcadis applies its innovative solutions is SINES DC in Portugal. With a capacity of 1.2 GW and 100% renewable energy, SINES DC is one of the largest data center campuses in Europe. The facility uses seawater cooling systems, taking advantage of its strategic location on the Portuguese coast to optimize energy efficiency and reduce its carbon footprint. “Arcadis is at the forefront of the transformation of data centers, delivering sustainable and innovative solutions to the challenges of digital transformation. With projects across various regions, such as Latin America and Europe, Arcadis leads the way in creating more efficient, resilient, and environmentally responsible digital infrastructure,” concludes Isabel. Accelerating a positive future for the planet.

artigo.texto: Data Center Insights: David Shepard, Chemelex-Raychem The Data Center Frontier Executive Roundtable features insights from industry executives with lengthy experience in the data center industry. Here’s a look at the Q3 2026 insights from David Shepard, Global Head of Data Center Business, Chemelex-Raychem. David Shepard is Global Head of Data Center Business at Chemelex-Raychem, a company with 44 offices in 28 countries. In this role, he is responsible for building and leading the company's data center business worldwide. Prior to his current position, David served as Vice President of Sales for Chilldyne, where he built global partnerships, drove the sales pipeline to nearly $200 million, and helped orchestrate the company's acquisition by Daikin Corporation. During more than 30 years in the technology industry, David has worked across all aspects of IT, from field engineering to the C-suite, with a focus on data center sales and operations, cloud services and IaaS, enterprise software, managed services, outsourcing, multi-vendor support, and professional services sales and operations. Reducing cost and complexity through the strategic use of technology has been a central theme throughout David's career. As an entrepreneur, he has worked in startup and turnaround environments, building and operating data centers and multi-cloud environments, optimizing workloads, developing secure cloud IaaS and PaaS solutions, conducting IT performance audits, and designing business continuity programs. He has also delivered disaster recovery solutions to help organizations meet critical business continuity requirements. David has extensive experience building sales organizations across global markets, including the Americas, Asia-Pacific, and EMEA, and has successfully brought technology solutions to market worldwide. Throughout his career, he has carried a sales quota, led services and sales organizations, rebuilt businesses, and established successful global partnerships. A U.S. Air Force veteran, David is also actively involved in supporting veteran-focused causes and initiatives. Data Center Frontier: What is AI infrastructure exposing that the data center industry could get away with overlooking at lower densities — and which traditional design or redundancy assumptions now need to be reconsidered? David Shepard, Chemelex-Raychem: The deployment and rapid adoption of AI infrastructure is beginning to expose a few areas of risk that were previously not top of mind with operators. Holding aside the “new normal” of extended supply chain issues, deploying IT infrastructure that is, say, 10 times more dense and 10 times more expensive puts a lot of pressure on operators to mitigate this new level of risk and protect these now far more expensive assets. As a for instance, we do leak detection in the white space. Leak detection SOP 5 years ago was ropes or point sensors on the floor, or under the raised floor. With AI infrastructures, those individual racks run between $2-7M per rack. That means traditional leak detection is simply not good enough, and “in rack, in CDU, in server” has become necessary. Data Center Frontier: As data centers become larger, denser and more power-constrained, where is the definition of “critical infrastructure” expanding — and are the interfaces between power, storage, cooling, controls and other systems becoming the real reliability risk? David Shepard, Chemelex-Raychem: “Critical infrastructure” – once simply power and connectivity – now must be thought of more holistically, and must now include adjacent technology like leak detection, freeze protection and Data Center Infrastructure Monitoring (DCIM). Data Center Frontier: With time-to-power compressing development schedules, where can operators safely accelerate deployment — and where do commissioning, testing and operational visibility need to become more rigorous rather than less? David Shepard, Chemelex-Raychem: Deployments on a smaller scale, where possible, enable the operators to gain real world operational competence. When done that way, the scale up is more easily managed, though it is always a challenge. And managing it is far more rigorous. Practically speaking, think of it like this: Operator A is a large colocation provider. The million square feet under management today are handled by expert staff who know the gear and the process. The operator wants to deploy AI infrastructure in a secure, well-run environment and introduce risk (density/cost, water/plumbing, etc…) into a massively risk-averse environment. Starting up a smaller version of the final deployment, building competency and comfort around the new infrastructure, will pay dividends. According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Natural Graphite Anode Material market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global natural graphite anode material (NGAM) market is positioned for transformative growth over the 2026-2035 forecast period, underpinned by the relentless expansion of lithium-ion battery megafactory capacity for electric vehicles and grid-scale energy storage. As the primary active anode ingredient in most commercial lithium-ion cells, NGAM sits at the core of the energy transition, and its demand trajectory is tightly linked to battery production volumes. China currently hosts over 70% of global NGAM processing capacity, spanning spheronization, purification, and carbon coating, creating a pronounced supply concentration that is reshaping trade policy and investment incentives worldwide. Prices for coated spherical graphite fell 30-40% during the 2023-2024 correction, resetting the pricing base for 2026 and compressing margins while opening volume demand from cost-sensitive battery segments. The market is bifurcating into standard-purity CSPG for LFP batteries and premium grades for high-energy NMC cells, with the former growing faster in tonnage. Environmental compliance costs and synthetic graphite substitution remain key challenges, but the overall outlook points to robust expansion through 2035. The baseline scenario for the natural graphite anode material market anticipates sustained double-digit growth through 2035, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 18% in volume terms. This outlook assumes continued global EV adoption, supportive government policies, and the gradual diversification of supply chains outside China. Demand will be primarily driven by lithium-ion battery production for electric vehicles, which account for the largest share of NGAM consumption, followed by stationary energy storage systems. The market is expected to see a shift toward higher-purity, coated spherical graphite as battery manufacturers demand improved performance and consistency. Supply-side constraints, including permitting delays and capital intensity for new purification plants outside China, may tighten availability in the short term, but ongoing investments in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific are expected to alleviate these bottlenecks by the late 2020s. However, the fundamental demand drivers remain strong, and the market is poised for significant growth. Electric vehicle batteries represent the dominant end-use sector for natural graphite anode material, accounting for the majority of global demand. As automakers ramp up production of EVs to meet emissions targets and consumer demand, the need for anode materials surges. artigo.texto: Biggest US Grid’s Data-Center Plan Accepted With 5-Month Pause (Bloomberg) -- US energy regulators accepted but suspended a plan by the country’s biggest electric grid to accelerate the addition of new power supply in a region struggling to meet demand from data centers. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission said Tuesday that it would accept the filing of grid operator PJM Interconnection LLC’s plan to procure new capacity but would suspend it until Feb. 28 and establish a paper hearing on unresolved issues. The regulator also encouraged PJM to submit a new filing that answers the issues it raised, which could shorten the delay. A PJM spokesperson didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment outside normal working hours. The artificial intelligence boom is driving the fastest growth in power demand in decades for PJM, which is home to the biggest US concentration of digital warehouses. The regulator agreed PJM needs more generation quickly and approved many parts of the operator’s plan, but said cost allocation, collateral and exit-rule issues need to be fixed before it can proceed. “This Commission will not be forced into accepting a deeply flawed, 11th-hour procurement mechanism with billion-dollar implications for consumers,” Commission Chairperson Laura Swett said in the order. “We are prepared to promptly act on a subsequent proposal that addresses the concerns raised in this order and meets the standards of the Federal Power Act. The region’s reliability hangs in the balance.” PJM’s struggle to keep up with demand growth prompted the Trump administration to call for changes. The FERC, in particular, in recent months has been pushing for reforms. State governors, utilities and investors have also criticized PJM’s response to the AI boom. In an effort to address those concerns, PJM plans to hold a one-time auction to cover a 6.8-gigawatt shortfall. In an earlier auction this year, it failed to attract sufficient commitments to satisfy power demand on peak-usage days. Early this year, the Trump administration pushed for a one-time auction with 15-year instead of annual contracts. PJM’s proposal is contentious because other consumers would bear the costs in the event of data center failures, according to Monitoring Analytics, the grid’s independent watchdog. “Existing customers should not be left paying costs attributable to new demand,” Commissioner Lindsay See said in the order. ©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

artigo.texto: Mercedes-Benz is taking another step toward next-generation electric vehicle batteries after signing a joint testing agreement with ProLogium Holding Inc. The agreement gives Mercedes-Benz priority access to ProLogium’s latest Gen4 battery cells for extensive testing as the automaker evaluates advanced battery technology for future EV applications. The partnership builds on nearly a decade of cooperation between Mercedes-Benz and ProLogium, which has included battery development, validation and testing of multiple cell formats and technologies. Under the new agreement, ProLogium’s Gen4 battery technology will undergo electrical, thermal and safety testing at Mercedes-Benz facilities as well as specialized independent testing institutes. The testing is expected to provide Mercedes-Benz with data needed to determine whether the new battery technology could eventually be integrated into future electric vehicles. ProLogium Gen4 Battery Targets Higher Energy Density and Faster Charging ProLogium’s Gen4 battery platform is designed around five key objectives: intrinsic safety, high performance, increased energy density, scalable production and a competitive cost structure. The battery architecture uses a non-flammable inorganic electrolyte and ceramic separator technology. ProLogium also incorporates its proprietary active safety mechanism, which is intended to improve the overall safety characteristics of the cells. Alongside safety improvements, the Gen4 technology is being developed to deliver fast charging, high power output and improved performance in low-temperature conditions. These characteristics could be particularly important as automakers continue working to reduce charging times while increasing EV range and performance. ProLogium says its approach is designed to move advanced battery technology beyond laboratory development and toward large-scale commercial production. “Over nearly a decade, our collaboration with Mercedes-Benz has evolved from early cell development and validation to testing our latest Gen4 technology for future vehicle applications,” said Vincent Yang, founder and CEO of ProLogium. Yang added that the company is focused on turning years of battery development into scalable manufacturing and commercially viable products, with its European expansion supported by Mercedes-Benz as well as the French government and European Union. Mercedes-Benz and ProLogium Have Worked Together Since 2016 The relationship between the two companies dates back to 2016. Since then, their collaboration has expanded from early hybrid-solid-state Gen3 battery development and joint validation toward potential applications in future vehicle platforms. Mercedes-Benz has become a long-term global automotive partner and strategic investor in ProLogium. The German automaker has also supported the development and validation of several lithium ceramic battery formats, including pouch cells, next-generation prismatic cells and ProLogium’s Bi-Polar technology. Jörg Burzer, member of the Board of Management of Mercedes-Benz Group AG and chief technology officer for development and procurement, said the partnership combines ProLogium’s solid-state battery technology with Mercedes-Benz’s expertise in battery development, testing and vehicle integration. The latest testing agreement therefore represents another stage in a partnership that has increasingly focused on technologies that could be used in future electric vehicles. ProLogium Expands Battery Manufacturing in Europe Large-scale manufacturing is a key part of ProLogium’s strategy. The company’s Taoke Gigafactory in Taiwan has completed GWh-scale manufacturing validation and supports C-sample production, demonstration vehicle programs and future commercial production. In Europe, ProLogium is developing a planned gigafactory in Dunkirk, France. The facility is expected to eventually have production capacity of up to 44 GWh, providing localized battery manufacturing and supply-chain capabilities for European customers. The Dunkirk facility is intended to replicate the production model established in Taiwan. Once its first phase is completed, ProLogium expects to have the capacity to supply commercial battery cells to European automakers at a scale suitable for electric vehicle platforms. Mercedes-Benz is also represented on ProLogium’s Board of Directors and has expressed support for the company’s Dunkirk development plans. ProLogium is additionally planning a potential NASDAQ listing in the fourth quarter of 2026. What the Gen4 Battery Could Mean for Future Mercedes EVs The latest agreement does not confirm that ProLogium’s Gen4 cells will be used in a production Mercedes-Benz EV. The technology must first complete Mercedes-Benz’s electrical, thermal and safety evaluation before its suitability for future vehicle applications can be determined. However, the testing highlights the growing importance of advanced battery technology as Mercedes-Benz continues developing its next generation of electric vehicles. If ProLogium’s Gen4 cells meet the automaker’s requirements, the combination of high energy density, fast charging, high power output, low-temperature performance and safety-focused cell architecture could make the technology a candidate for future EV platforms. For ProLogium, the agreement also represents an important step in moving its solid-state battery technology closer to automotive-scale commercialization, particularly as the company prepares to expand production in Europe.

artigo.texto: O aumento da demanda por eletricidade aumentou à medida que a atividade dos Data Centers se expandiu e essa tendência deve continuar nos próximos três a cinco anos. O relatório “IA encontra a rede elétrica: moldando o cenário energético dos Data Centers”, da Capgemini, examina o rápido crescimento das operações de Data Center e destaca como a Inteligência Artificial (IA), a IA Generativa e os agentes de IA podem criar valor nas operações da rede e no desempenho do sistema. Realizada com executivos de energia em 21 países, a pesquisa indica que mais de 60% dos executivos do setor elétrico esperam que a IA desbloqueie ganhos significativos em eficiência e operações. No entanto, apenas 45% das concessionárias usam a IA para otimização da rede, o que revela uma oportunidade significativa para escalar operações digitais e impulsionadas por IA para acompanhar a demanda crescente. Além disso, apenas 16% das empresas elétricas usam atualmente Agentes de IA para otimização e confiabilidade da rede, no entanto, 58% planejam implementá-los nos próximos dois anos. O estudo aponta que as empresas do setor elétrico que aliarem uma modelagem disciplinada da demanda a uma entrega mais rápida e flexível, sustentada por operações impulsionadas por IA e por talentos preparados para o futuro, estarão mais bem posicionadas para liderar a próxima fase de expansão dos data centers e oferecer confiabilidade, resiliência, viabilidade econômica e sustentabilidade na velocidade da era da IA. “O sucesso dependerá da capacidade de alinhar investimentos em infraestrutura, fornecimento de energia e operações habilitadas por IA para gerenciar tanto a escala quanto a volatilidade da demanda, equilibrando confiabilidade, custo e sustentabilidade” conclui Claire Gauthier, VP global de Energia e Utilities da Capgemini. Sobre o estudo A pesquisa examina como o rápido crescimento das operações de Data Centers, especialmente as cargas de trabalho impulsionadas por IA, tem remodelado a demanda por eletricidade e desafiando as organizações do setor energético. Foram pesquisados 612 executivos seniores de eletricidade de nível de diretor e acima que estão trabalhando ativamente com data centers, 175 executivos seniores de organizações proprietárias e operadoras de data centers e cinta com insights de quase 20 executivos seniores do setor nas principais organizações globais. A pesquisa foi realizada em 21 países na América do Norte, Europa, APAC e América Latina, incluindo o Brasil. Sobre a Capgemini A Capgemini é uma parceira global de transformação de negócios e tecnologia impulsionada por Inteligência Artificial, que gera valor tangível no mercado. Imaginamos o futuro das organizações e o tornamos realidade por meio de IA, tecnologia e pessoas. Com nossa sólida trajetória de quase 60 anos, somos um grupo responsável e diverso com 420 mil profissionais, em mais de 50 países. Oferecemos serviços e soluções de ponta a ponta que contam com nossa profunda expertise setorial e um robusto ecossistema de parceiros, elevando nossas capacidades em estratégia, tecnologia, design, engenharia e operações de negócios. O Grupo reportou em 2025 receitas globais de 22,5 bilhões de euros. Serviço www.capgemini.com/br-pt

artigo.texto: VW-backed Gotion claims solid state battery breakthrough, aims for 150 USD/kWh & 400 Wh/kg At the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei, Volkswagen-backed battery maker Gotion announced breakthroughs in producing its solid-state batteries (SSBs). It also published commercialisation benchmarks and is aiming for an energy density of 400 Wh/kg and pricing of 150 USD/kWh. Baby steps towards mass production CarNewsChina previously reported that Gotion locked in on a 2GWh SSB production line design in March 2026. The firm says it has continued work to ready its Jinshi (Gold Rock) SSB cells for real-world commercialisation, including safety testing. Gotion says its SSB cells have endured “extreme testing scenarios”, including puncture and high-temperature evaluations. It claims the new cells produced neither smoke nor flames, proving that safety and energy density can coexist in SSB cells. Potential pricing and specs The battery maker has also disclosed its financial aims for its new cells, with the ultimate goal of bringing SSBs into the “one-yuan era”, referring to the benchmark of 1 yuan/Wh. This is equivalent to 150 USD/kWh, more than double the current average price of LFP cells in China. Gotion has also renewed its energy-density claims, saying the new cell will reach 400 Wh/kg. The firm is using a sulfide-based solid electrolyte in its Jinshi cells and previously claimed an energy density of 350 Wh/kg. More on Gotion Founded in 2006 in Hefei, Gotion High-Tech is China’s fifth-largest battery maker with 20 manufacturing bases worldwide. It is also closely aligned with Volkswagen, its largest shareholder. According to China EV DataTracker, Gotion achieved 4.61 GWh of battery installations in August 2026, trailing behind similar second-tier suppliers like EVE Energy and CALB. It has slipped to fifth place, and SSBs may be an opportunity to leapfrog competitors. The race for SSBs is heating up, with a plethora of Chinese battery makers and automotive brands announcing plans for trial production and vehicle tests in 2027. BYD has made headlines with its upcoming Yangwang flagship sedan, which may become the first SSB-equipped car to hit the market. Source: libattery.net

artigo.texto: Foi aprovado, nesta terça-feira (29), na Câmara de Maringá, um conjunto com Projetos de Lei (PL) para que o município crie uma empresa pública responsável por implantar e operar o data center previsto pela Prefeitura. A proposta é de autoria do executivo. Ao todo, foram 20 votos registrados: 13 favoráveis e seis contrários. Votaram a favor os vereadores Akemi Nishimori (PSD), Angelo Salgueiro (PODE), Bravin Junior (PP), Diogo Altamir da Lotérica (PSDB), Flávio Mantovani (PSD), Guilherme Machado (PL), Jeremias (PL), Luiz Neto (AGIR), Maninho (Republicanos), Mário Hossokawa (PP), Odair Fogueteiro (PP), Uilian da Farmácia (União) e William Gentil (PP), totalizando 13 votos. Votaram contra Daniel Malvezzi (NOVO), Italo Maroneze (PDT), Lemuel do Salvando Vidas (PDT), Mário Verri (PT), Professor Pacífico (NOVO) e Professora Ana Lúcia (PDT), somando seis votos. A proposta O Projeto de Lei nº 18.401/2026 autoriza a criação da Maringá Data e Tecnologia S.A., empresa pública constituída como sociedade anônima de capital fechado e com capital integralmente pertencente ao Município. A companhia terá como finalidade a implantação, operação e exploração de um data center, apresentado no projeto como empreendimento-âncora da futura Zona de Processamento de Exportação (ZPE) de Maringá. Um dos projetos que acompanha a proposta, o PL nº 18.398/2026, autoriza a abertura de um crédito adicional especial de R$10 milhões no orçamento de 2026. O recurso será destinado à constituição e estruturação da nova empresa. Além desse valor inicial, o projeto que cria a empresa prevê que o Município poderá fazer aportes de até R$20 milhões ao longo de quatro anos. Com a aprovação nas duas discussões, o projeto segue para sanção do executivo.

artigo.texto: SpaceX (SPCX) está prestes a levar uma carga muito interessante para a órbita: chips de IA de um de seus maiores rivais. De acordo com uma postagem amplamente compartilhada no X, a Alphabet (GOOG) está lançando os TPUs do Google (os chips personalizados que ela constrói para executar IA) nesta semana em um Falcon 9 da SpaceX para testar data centers de IA em órbita. A resposta de Elon Musk? "A quantidade de computação no espaço obviamente será arredondada para 100% de toda a computação." (Sem hesitação!) Para os investidores da SpaceX, porém, o mais importante é quem está comprando a viagem. Escrevi no início desta semana sobre o cronograma agressivo de Musk para a Lua e Marte. Mas esta parece ser uma daquelas semanas em que décadas acontecem – porque a computação orbital oficialmente não é mais uma aposta exclusiva da SpaceX. A concorrência está pagando para entrar nela. A SpaceX é paga de qualquer maneira Pense na situação aqui. A SpaceX tem seu próprio negócio de IA (olá, Grok). O Google é um de seus rivais mais ferozes em IA. E quando o Google quis testar seus chips em órbita, foi à SpaceX para o lançamento. Se a Coca-Cola tivesse que enviar todas as latas nos caminhões da Pepsi, você gostaria de ser dono da empresa de transporte. A mesma ideia aqui. Quer o Grok ou o Gemini vença a IA no espaço, os chips têm que chegar lá de alguma forma. (Por que o espaço? A versão curta é energia. Na órbita certa, os painéis solares recebem luz solar quase constante, e você não precisa esperar na fila por um espaço em uma rede elétrica lotada.) E o Google já está aumentando os gastos... Como você pode ver, o CapEx está aumentando rapidamente. Mesmo uma pequena fração indo para a órbita seria importante para quem estiver fazendo o lançamento. Vamos testar esses 100 GW Fica maior. O CFO da SpaceX diz que a empresa está no caminho para implantar 100 GW de computação orbital a cada ano até o final da década. Enquanto isso, a FCC aceitou o pedido da SpaceX para implantar até 100.000 satélites Starlink Gen3 para arquivamento em 18 de setembro. E Musk adicionou um detalhe importante: "Cada satélite tem 250 kW e terá um computador Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 projetado pela SpaceX." Então, aqui está uma conta rápida de guardanapo: 100.000 satélites × 250 kW cada = 25 GW. Essa é toda a constelação Gen3 proposta... e é apenas um quarto do que o CFO diz que a SpaceX implantará a cada ano. Mesmo que as cargas úteis provavelmente fiquem maiores... ainda são muitos foguetes. E a SpaceX é dona dos foguetes. A NVIDIA também está pegando carona Observe o que Musk diz que vai dentro de cada um desses satélites: um computador construído com chips da NVIDIA (NVDA). A Nvidia já surfou o boom dos data centers no solo para um grande crescimento de receita... Se Musk estiver mesmo parcialmente certo, a órbita se torna outro mercado para esses chips. Eu chamaria isso de um bom bônus para os acionistas da Nvidia. Aqui está o problema Claro, um lançamento de teste do Falcon 9 é um contrato minúsculo. A computação orbital pode permanecer experimental por anos, e a receita da SpaceX pode não mostrar muito disso até bem depois do final da década. E a SpaceX vai precisar de toda a ajuda que puder obter para atender às expectativas de crescimento dos analistas e manter sua avaliação extraordinariamente rica. Quanto a mim, estou confortável em ficar de fora por enquanto. Há muito risco de execução em jogo aqui, mas a oportunidade, francamente, é enorme. artigo.texto: WEG aumenta a aposta em SC e eleva investimento para R$ 330 milhões em megafábrica de baterias A empresa destacou que a ampliação do projeto da planta em Itajaí faz parte da estratégia da companhia de apoiar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil WEG aumenta a aposta em SC e eleva investimento para R$ 330 milhões em megafábrica de bateriasFoto: WEG/Divulgação/ND Mais A WEG anunciou, nesta sexta-feira (25) a ampliação do projeto de sua nova fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, chamado BESS, em construção em Itajaí, no Litoral Norte de Santa SC. Anunciada em fevereiro deste ano, a nova fábrica terá um investimento total estimado de R$ 330 milhões e capacidade anual de 4 GWh, atendendo à demanda crescente por soluções associadas à transição energética, com início das operações previsto para o segundo semestre de 2027. A empresa destacou que o movimento faz parte da estratégia da companhia de apoiar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil, na iminência do primeiro Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade Armazenamento Nacional, a ser realizado em dezembro de 2026, o projeto atualizado incorpora maior nível de automação e ganhos de eficiência industrial que permitirão ampliar a capacidade produtiva. WEG acredita na forte expansão do mercado de energia “O mercado de armazenamento de energia vive um momento de forte expansão, impulsionado pelo crescimento das fontes renováveis e pela necessidade crescente de maior flexibilidade e segurança para o sistema elétrico. A ampliação deste projeto demonstra a capacidade da WEG de adaptar rapidamente seus investimentos para atender às necessidades do mercado e apoiar o desenvolvimento sustentável do setor energético brasileiro”, Manfred Peter Johann, Vice-Presidente de Automação e Sistemas da WEG. A empresa destacou que a ampliação do projeto da planta em Itajaí faz parte da estratégia da companhia de apoiar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no BrasilFoto: WEG/Divulgação/ND Mais O BESS desempenha papel fundamental nos sistemas elétricos modernos, principalmente na integração das fontes renováveis como solar e eólica, permitindo armazenar energia nos momentos de maior disponibilidade e disponibilizá-la quando necessário. Essa flexibilidade contribui para a estabilidade do sistema elétrico, maior eficiência operacional e aproveitamento dos recursos energéticos. Cláudio Costa é editor-chefe do ND Mais na redação de Itajaí, de onde coordena a equipe local e escreve sobre política, segurança pública, economia e temas relacionados à comunidade. Entre as cidades que cobre estão Balneário Camboriú, Itajaí, Navegantes, Penha e Bombinhas, assim como todo o Litoral Norte de Santa Catarina. Bacharel em Comunicação Social pela Faculdade Ielusc (Instituto Superior e Centro Educacional Luterano), atua no jornalismo desde 2007 e aprofunda suas matérias utilizando sua formação em investigação criminal e perícia criminal. Possui especializações em marketing digital e inteligência artificial, garantindo uma abordagem moderna e informada. Trabalhou nas eleições de 2012 e 2014 como editor no Jornal ND, em Joinville. artigo.texto: EU chooses secrecy over transparency on data centers’ environmental cost The EU faced a choice: reveal the environmental cost of data centers or protect the industry’s secrets. A year-long battle for answers across all 27 member states shows how European authorities chose commercial secrecy – and how a first-of-its-kind legal challenge could change that. European officials faced a political choice over their proposed sustainability rating system for data centers: make consumption figures public or protect the industry’s commercial secrets. A study they commissioned made that choice explicit. They chose secrecy. A year-long investigation by Solomon and its partners found that the proposed system would keep crucial energy and water consumption figures from public view while relying on incomplete and flawed data. Unveiled by the European Commission this month and described in media coverage as potentially the most comprehensive of its kind in the world, the proposal promises “transparent information about the actual use of resources (energy, water)” by data centers. These facilities underpin Europe’s massive digital expansion and contribute to its growing environmental footprint. Yet the rating system would show how efficiently individual facilities use energy and water, while keeping their total consumption and carbon emissions confidential. For communities living near data centers, those totals answer a basic question: How much electricity and water are the facilities around them using? As Europe expands the infrastructure powering artificial intelligence (AI), the answers would help residents assess what that growth means for local supplies. Led by Lighthouse Reports, journalists filed formal records requests with authorities in all 27 EU member states and the Commission. We requested basic information on data centers’ energy use, water consumption and sustainability performance, along with correspondence about the implementation of the reporting system. Hundreds of exchanges, appeals and challenges to refusals uncovered missing reports, seemingly impossible efficiency readings and European officials encouraging submissions even when they contained little or no data. Our investigation – conducted with Mediapart (France), El Confidencial (Spain), Il Manifesto (Italy) and Trouw (the Netherlands) – also examined how industry demands shaped the information the public will be allowed to see. And it revealed how difficult it is to obtain consumption figures that operators are required to report. The secrecy is built into EU rules. Data centers with an installed information technology capacity of at least 500 kilowatts must report their energy and water consumption. But the rules treat individual facilities’ submissions as commercially confidential, shielding them from public disclosure to protect companies’ business interests. Those are the consumption figures we spent a year trying to obtain across the EU. Some governments called them commercial secrets. Others said they were held in Brussels. The Commission, which runs the European database, also refused to release them. Two countries provided partial data that could not be linked to specific facilities. France supplied a spreadsheet but shuffled values between rows, leaving reporters unable to reliably connect a data center’s electricity use with its water consumption. The findings underpin a first-of-its-kind legal challenge launched this week by our reporting consortium under the Aarhus Convention, a binding international treaty protecting access to environmental information. We argue that EU rules treating individual data centers’ environmental information as commercially confidential violate the treaty – both in their wording and in how authorities apply them to deny public access. At stake is the public’s ability to understand – and have a say in – one of the defining environmental developments of our time: the enormous and accelerating build-out of data centers powering the AI boom, and its impact in their communities. “There is a clear public interest in understanding the material impact that infrastructure of this scale may have, including its total water and electricity consumption,” said Nicolás González Casares, a Spanish Socialist Member of the European Parliament (MEP) who works on energy policy and the environmental impact of AI. He added, “Protecting commercially sensitive information when necessary is one thing; systematically preventing the public from understanding this environmental impact is quite another.” In response to our findings, the Commission defended the system, saying it had significantly improved transparency and that its confidentiality rules complied with EU law and the Aarhus Convention. A “fairly useless” system? Data centers are warehouses packed with computers and cooling systems that power everything from everyday online services to AI systems. They are vital to the development of the AI industry. They are also extremely energy-intensive, requiring vast amounts of electricity and, depending on how they are cooled, water. In Ireland, data centers consumed nearly as much electricity as all the country’s homes combined in 2025 — accounting for 23 percent of recorded electricity consumption, compared with 28 percent for households. A decade earlier, data centers’ share was just 5 percent, according to the country’s statistics authority. The EU aims to triple its data center capacity over the next five to seven years. That expansion comes amid a global backlash against data centers over their demands on electricity and water supplies. In parts of the United States, households are already paying higher electricity bills partly because of data centers’ growing demand for power. “Every new data center stakes a claim on something a community needs, from the water we drink to the energy that heats our homes,” said Cori Crider, executive director of the Future of Tech Institute. “A smart plan for European compute

artigo.texto: The nights are drawing in, there’s an autumnal chill in the air and shipping companies are preparing to surrender emissions allowances. The deadline to surrender allowances for the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) is fast approaching and it is important for parties to act now to avoid penalties for non-compliance. EU ETS surrender deadline is just days away Emissions trading schemes, most significantly the EU ETS, set a cap-and-trade system requiring companies from the maritime sector and other industries, to surrender European Union Allowances (EUAs) to offset their annual emissions. The EU ETS requires EUAs to be submitted by 30 September. An annual obligation for maritime companies since 2024, this year, shipping companies must surrender EUAs to cover 70% of reported emissions from 2025. Starting next year, EUAs will need to be surrendered to cover 100% of reported emissions. Don’t leave yourself open to liability: The 30 September deadline is only for the EU ETS. The equivalent UK legislation doesn’t require allowances to be surrendered until 30 April with special measures covering 2026 and 2027 emissions so no surrender is required until 2028. Looking at EU, responsible shipping companies The “shipping company” is responsible for surrendering the right numbers of EUAs. In cases where a ship manager has signed a mandate taking on the responsibility for the “shipping company,” they will have assumed responsibility for EU ETS obligations. Such managers must ensure that sufficient EUAs are transferred into their holding accounts in good time to surrender to the EU. The administrative process for receipt and then surrendering allowances is not always instantaneous, and any delay in procurement or transfer could leave managers exposed. Any managers carrying an EU ETS mandate should already know where their EUAs are coming from or, preferably, have any required EUAs in hand. Otherwise, urgent action will be needed to meet the 30 September deadline. Absent allowances The industry has become more accustomed to EU ETS, the rhythm of the reporting cycle and agreeing clauses in charters, MOAs and ship management agreements. This, however, has led some into complacency with delays in EUAs being transferred from charterers to managers/owners – often despite specific language in the relevant charterparty. While the deadline was a distant thought parties were willing to give one another leeway but, now that it approaches, attitudes are hardening. Although the registered shipping company will almost invariably have some contractual right of recovery against the charterer or the owner, in the case of ship managers, it also remains the entity liable under the EU ETS. The consequences of failing to surrender EUAs on time are severe. A penalty of €100 per allowance, adjusted for inflation, is levied and the shipping company must still surrender the EUAs next year. Persistent defaults can even result in an expulsion order effectively barring the vessel from entering European ports. Shipping companies must ensure that the requisite EUAs are surrendered by the deadline, even if that means purchasing allowances at their own cost and pursuing reimbursement separately.

artigo.texto: Chillicothe — Mayor Luke Feeney discusses the data center issue and the city’s powers concerning it, as well as other considerations about developments at the former paper mill, in an interview. With concerns about data centers in the news – and friction over allowing the “data hall” proposed by Alignment Engine Inc. on the “Chilpaco Innovation Campus,” I asked him for a sit-down interview. This was an offer to respond to Portia Boulger, founder of “Appalachians Against Data Centers,” who had confronted Feeney and other city officials over the February letter the city sent to the developer of the proposed “data hall.” Feeney declined that response, and instead he and I spoke about the data center and the city. Our interview is below, in three parts. He also soon produced a Facebook Reel video where he more thoroughly explained the city’s powers regarding zoning and other regulations: “This short video lays out the facts and timeline as clearly as possible. My goal being to provide the public with accurate information, explain the process, and make clear the difference between a discussion or inquiry, a zoning interpretation, a formal application, an approval, and actual construction. “Relevant documents can be found at this link.” Chillicothe Council will be meeting in the Main Annex of the Chillicothe and Ross County Public Library, behind 140 South Paint Street, at 7pm on Monday, September 28th. - He won’t comment on stories, but will comment on the process - Developing the “Universal Development Code (UDC, which replaced zoning and other powers) was a 19-month process - Regretfully, the process did not touch on data centers - 2025 was a “roller coaster of a year” - The “zoning certification letter” regarding the possibility of a data center - It was not zoning approval or permission to proceed - Such question and letter is almost always a first step - He wishes the data center issue was as big then as now, because they would have considered it in the UDC - The state was still giving out incentives for data centers, until May 2026 - The city did not get any other communications on the proposed data center between February 20th and the July 2 announcement - The city hired legal counsel to advise them, then created the moratorium - He wishes the moratorium had gone to committee for further review - There are still no formal communications about the proposed data center - There was only the email question from the developer - That means the city can’t say yes or no - City’s rules still cover industrial zones: setback, sound, etc. - The February letter is a typical hypothetical request, the start of a conversation - The Universal Development Code was meant to be updated, and has been once already - No matter what happens, data center regulation will go into the UDC - The February letter was very generic, and was sent in an email so it was dated by the email - Again, not want to address Portia Boulger’s statements - What is his perspective on the proposed paper mill development, including restarting The Chief? - The legal procedurals should be looked at completely separate from community impact by actual proposed development - The city has an absolute obligation to apply zoning rules - There are lots of proposals at the paper mill – he is excited about any opportunity to being back jobs - The proposals are speculative, and can’t be guaranteed - The city needs to be responsible about zoning, but also be supporting about jobs and business development - Zoning is city-wide – rules should be applied the same everywhere; can’t spot zone - Could there be a better solution than what has happened and is proposed? - Considering the speed of purchase, moving equipment in, the energy, conversations – better than expected - April 15th, 2025: his birthday, and paper mill closing announced - Across Ohio, paper mills have been closed for decades - His role is to be excited, supported, enthusiastic, and trust…but verify - He must budget for next year – but can’t budget city revenue on income tax from proposed jobs - 350 more people would mean more income tax – but can’t bet on - The city must be reserved, needs to see receipts - But what about claims of backstage deals and corrupt officials? ; ) - Data centers have been controversial – other than covid, he has not seen anything evolve so quickly - The state was incentivizing data centers through May - Similar to the seeming overpopulation of solar fields and windmills? - There is no solid data – only a presentation – is a proposal, a promise - We are all here to do the best for the city - This topic been so confusing, has created confusion, and challenges in communication has added to the confusion - The goal of the moratorium was to slow down the process and listen to the community - There is excitement around the paper mill redevelopment, but uncertainty around the data center - And then my camera battery died

artigo.texto: A Rússia bombardeou a sede da Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia da Ucrânia, e data centers da Vodafone e de provedores locais em Kiev. Os ataques causaram ferimentos em três pessoas e deixaram cerca de 100 mil residências sem acesso à internet. O presidente Volodymyr Zelensky confirmou os impactos na infraestrutura de comunicação, enquanto o governo russo alega que ataca infraestrutura militar e de dados para interromper o fluxo de informações ucraniano. A Rússia atacou neste domingo (27) a sede da Kyivstar, a maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia, informou a empresa à mídia local. O ataque ocorreu enquanto Moscou seguia com bombardeios contra data centers e infraestrutura de comunicações ucranianos. A Kyivstar confirmou à agência de notícias Interfax Ucrânia que sua sede em Kiev havia sido atingida, mas não houve vítimas fatais. Ataques à infraestrutura de dados O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia também informou neste domingo que atingiu um data center pertencente à Vodafone Ucrânia, a segunda maior operadora de telefonia celular do país. A Vodafone Ucrânia não respondeu a um pedido de comentário sobre o ocorrido. Impacto nas telecomunicações e alerta internacional - Alvo estratégico: A sede da Kyivstar, líder do mercado de telefonia ucraniano, foi atingida em Kiev. - Vítimas: O presidente Zelensky afirmou que o ataque a um data center feriu duas crianças e um adulto. - Queda de serviço: Cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev ficaram sem internet após os bombardeios da semana passada. - Segurança digital: O chanceler ucraniano alertou que interromper data centers busca silenciar alertas de mísseis que salvam vidas. - Contexto: Moscou alega atacar infraestrutura militar, mas críticos veem uma ofensiva contra a conectividade civil. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, afirmou que a Rússia atacou um data center em Kiev duas vezes na manhã deste domingo, ferindo duas crianças e um adulto. Moscou também atingiu data centers pertencentes a provedores de internet ucranianos na semana passada, causando interrupções no serviço para cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev e na região circundante, de acordo com o Ministério Digital da Ucrânia. A Rússia tem como alvo os principais data centers ucranianos, buscando interromper o fluxo de informações. Alertas rápidos sobre ameaças de mísseis e drones são essenciais -- eles salvam vidas, escreveu o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha, no X na quarta-feira (23).

artigo.texto: Volkswagen Group, PowerCo and Gotion deepen strategic partnership. Valencia to be developed into European production hub for LFP batteries - The companies are expanding their long-standing strategic partnership to include the industrial production of LFP battery cells and cathode active materials. - Accelerated development of a regional battery supply chain for Europe through the establishment of joint ventures at the Valencia (Spain), Šurany (Slovak Republic) and Kenitra (Morocco) sites. - Valencia to be developed into European production hub for LFP batteries. - Thomas Schmall: “Gotion has been a close partner of the Volkswagen Group for many years. We are now expanding our partnership into joint industrial production of LFP batteries to strengthen Europe’s battery industry. This marks a major breakthrough for both companies.” Salzgitter/Hefei/Valencia. Volkswagen Group, PowerCo SE and Gotion High-tech have agreed to deepen their strategic partnership and jointly accelerate the development of a regional battery supply chain for Europe. Building on their cooperation since 2020, the partners agreed on establishing three joint ventures at the Valencia (Spain), Šurany (Slovak Republic) and Kenitra (Morocco) sites for the industrial production of LFP battery cells and cathode material. The agreement also covers joint procurement and sales activities in Europe. Separately, Volkswagen Group has announced that it has entered into definitive agreements to sell 5.3 % equity stake in Gotion to optimize equity structures and support long-term strategic synergies. Upon completion of the transaction, Volkswagen will continue to hold a significant stake in Gotion. LFP batteries offer competitive costs, a long service life and high levels of robustness, making them a key technology for affordable electric mobility in the volume segment. Demand in Europe is expected to grow strongly in the coming years: According to forecasts, LFP’s market share could rise from around 10 percent today to between 40 and 60 percent by 2030. At the same time, Europe currently has no relevant LFP battery production capacity. The partnership with Gotion strengthens Europe’s position in the global LFP battery market. Together, the partners will expand regional LFP battery production, diversify sources of supply for key cathode active materials, and thereby strengthen supply security and the competitiveness of the European battery industry. Thomas Schmall, Member of the Board of Management of Volkswagen Group for Technology and Chairman of the Supervisory Board of PowerCo SE: “I am delighted that we are expanding our long-standing partnership with Gotion into the joint industrial production of LFP batteries to strengthen Europe’s battery industry. This marks a major breakthrough for both companies and brings us one step closer to the forefront of electric mobility. Volkswagen is the first European automotive manufacturer to cover the entire battery value chain, from development and cathode materials through to production.” Li Zhen, Chairman of Gotion Hith-tech: “Six years of close collaboration between Volkswagen and Gotion have built deep mutual trust and a relationship that empowers both sides—one that has long since moved beyond ordinary business to become a partnership bound by a shared future. Today, together with Volkswagen Group and PowerCo, we are accelerating our global strategic cooperation. Through cross-shareholdings and three joint sites, we are anchoring our shared strategy to localise battery production in Europe, racing to seize the opportunities of global electric mobility, and jointly forging a new paradigm of world-class, win-win cooperation in the lithium battery industry.” Frank Blome, CEO of PowerCo SE: “Volkswagen and PowerCo are building Europe’s battery industry. The partnership with Gotion is the next milestone on this path: It strengthens the resilience of our value chain, accelerates industrialization and combines PowerCo’s capabilities with the strengths of a long-standing partner.” Diversifying the battery supply chain Volkswagen Group, PowerCo and Gotion have been working closely and successfully together since 2020. Gotion is both a cell supplier to the Volkswagen Group and a strategic partner of PowerCo. With the new joint ventures, the partners are strategically expanding this proven cooperation into the industrial production of LFP battery cells and cathode active material. Across the three sites, they will also share investments and industrial responsibilities. The agreement therefore supports Volkswagen Group’s long-term plans to establish a European battery supply chain and strengthens PowerCo’s growth plan. - Valencia / Spain: LFP battery cells The PowerCo gigafactory currently under construction in Valencia is envisaged to be transferred to a joint venture. The agreement provides for PowerCo to hold a 51 percent stake in the joint venture and to remain the majority shareholder. The joint venture is intended to be jointly managed by PowerCo and Gotion. One major goal is to develop the site into a European production hub for Unified Cells based on LFP technology. artigo.texto: Uma nova frente de negócios: créditos de carbono Elétricas ampliam a venda de créditos de carbono e miram nova demanda com avanço do mercado regulado Atualizado Com o desenvolvimento do mercado de carbono nacional, as empresas do setor de energia passaram a enxergar a comercialização de créditos de carbono como uma extensão de seus negócios. Foi uma evolução natural do setor, uma vez que as fontes renováveis respondem por cerca de 85% da matriz elétrica brasileira e que as reduções de emissões de carbono podem dar origem a créditos. Embora essa frente de negócios não seja relevante em termos de faturamento, integra a sustentabilidade das operações. Trata-se de um negócio complementar, cuja relevância pode aumentar com o mercado regulado de carbono, o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE), em implementação. Na Auren Energia, a estratégia ganhou uma área dedicada em 2022 e foi integrada à comercialização. A companhia já vendeu oito milhões de créditos a clientes de mais de 20 países, a maioria deles empresas que precisam neutralizar suas emissões. Ela também mantém o Carbonless, comércio eletrônico para pequenas empresas e pessoas físicas que queiram zerar sua pegada de carbono. Eduardo Diniz, diretor de comercialização, diz que a estratégia da Auren é se tornar um “one-stop-shop” para clientes de energia, de forma que estes possam comprar tanto o fornecimento de energia quanto os créditos para zerar ou compensar as emissões. No momento, a empresa desenvolve um projeto que prevê a restauração de até 2.795 hectares e o plantio de até 5,6 milhões de árvores na bacia do rio Tietê — projetos do tipo geram créditos mais valorizados. Já a Axia Energia comercializou mais de 12 milhões de créditos entre 2013 e 2026. A companhia vê a experiência como credencial para o SBCE, que estabelecerá limites de emissão para agentes regulados e permitirá a negociação de ativos para o cumprimento das metas. A expectativa das empresas é que créditos hoje negociados no mercado voluntário possam, desde que atendam a critérios previstos na regulamentação, ganhar espaço também nesse sistema. “Queremos alcançar empresas que estão começando a jornada de sustentabilidade e empresas maiores com alta demanda de crédito”, diz Cecília Essinger, gerente-executiva de produtos estruturados e ativos ambientais da Axia. Segundo ela, créditos originados em energia renovável são negociados no mercado por cerca de US$ 1 a US$ 3. A Engie atua no mercado de carbono desde 2004. A empresa tem 14 projetos de energia eólica, solar, hidrelétrica e biomassa que geram créditos pela redução de emissões de gases de efeito estufa (GEE). Antes registrados no Mecanismo de Desenvolvimento Limpo (MDL), esses projetos estão sendo adaptados às regras do Acordo de Paris. Nos empreendimentos controlados integralmente pela Engie, as reduções de emissões somaram cerca de 6,5 milhões de toneladas de CO2 e até 2020, sendo que 5,3 milhões de créditos já foram usados para compensar emissões e, por isso, saíram de circulação. A empresa também mantém a plataforma Descarbonize, que ajuda clientes a medir e administrar suas emissões e a comprar créditos para compensá-las. Já na EDP, o Parque Eólico Monte Verde, no Rio Grande do Norte, tornou-se em 2025 o primeiro projeto do grupo no mundo certificado para emitir créditos, evitando a emissão de 533 mil toneladas de CO2 por ano. Como o mercado voluntário de créditos de carbono só se sustenta se houver credibilidade e confiança de que os projetos contribuíram para a redução ou remoção das emissões, as empresas têm buscado verificadoras independentes como Verra e Gold Standard, mecanismos vinculados à ONU e o Global Carbon Council. Nem toda redução de emissões entrega o mesmo resultado climático. Daniela Mota, head de meio ambiente e sustentabilidade do escritório Felsberg Advogados, diz que tecnologia, data de geração, metodologia e certificação influenciam qualidade e preço dos créditos. Entre os riscos estão a falta de adicionalidade — quando a redução ocorreria mesmo sem o projeto —, a dupla contagem e benefícios que não se confirmam. “É muito ruim, do ponto de vista reputacional, ter um projeto de carbono que não entrega aquilo que estava prometendo”, afirma. Enquanto alguns monetizam emissões evitadas e projetos de restauração florestal, uma nova fronteira está nas tecnologias de captura, transporte, utilização e armazenamento de CO2, conhecidas pelas siglas CCS e CCUS. O Decreto nº 13.095/2026, publicado em agosto, reconhece o CCS como atividade de redução ou remoção de GEE, que poderá ser considerada no SBCE. A Petrobras informa ter armazenado 86 milhões de toneladas de CO2 em sistemas de CCUS do pré-sal entre 2008 e 2025, sendo 18 milhões no ano passado. Já o piloto Cabiúnas-São Tomé deverá capturar até 100 mil toneladas anuais por três anos a partir de 2028 e armazená-las em reservatório salino profundo no norte fluminense. A licença ambiental integrada foi emitida em agosto. Apesar da escala, a estatal não tem projeto para gerar créditos destinados à venda; suas compras ou compromissos de aquisição são, a princípio, para uso próprio.
