artigo.texto: As much as 12 gigawatt-hour (GWh) of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity, or roughly one-fifth of the total BESS under construction, faces commissioning delays due to hardening battery prices even as tariffs bid for these projects are lower. Nearly 21 per cent of the under-construction BESS capacity, equivalent to about 12 GWh, faces weak return potential which may lead to some delays in commissioning, Crisil Ratings said in a commentary. Explaining the scenario, Manish Gupta, Senior Director and Deputy Chief Ratings Officer at Crisil Ratings, said “The risk has emerged because battery prices have hardened in 2026, while tariffs bid out for these projects were relatively low. Developers typically procure batteries about a year after securing project bids. Consequently, most projects awarded in 2025 are now exposed to higher battery prices, which have rebounded from the lows witnessed in 2025.” As battery prices were consistently coming down till 2025, developers appear to have bid aggressively on the assumption that prices would continue their downward trajectory, he pointed out. However, in reality, battery prices have increased and at these prevailing levels, project return may be insufficient to achieve a typical target internal rate of return (IRR) of 12-14 per cent. Consequently, developers may defer implementation in anticipation of more favourable battery pricing, the ratings agency said. The analysis covers bids awarded between fiscals 2024 and 2026 across nearly 100 RE developers. BESS projects BESS projects accounted for nearly 40 per cent of the total auctioned capacity in FY26, up sharply from about 5 per cent in FY24 and FY25. As a result, 50-55 GWh of BESS capacity is scheduled for commissioning across FY27 and FY28. Of this, around 40 GWh has been awarded through government-led auctions, where distribution utilities are the offtakers, while the remaining 10-15 GWh is expected to serve commercial and industrial consumers directly or be deployed in the merchant market. Ankit Hakhu, Director at Crisil Ratings, said that around 8-9 GWh out of this 12 GWh of the planned capacity is exposed to an additional challenge--limited implementation experience among project sponsors. “While BESS projects typically face relatively lower land acquisition and connectivity-related challenges compared to conventional renewable energy projects, equipment procurement remains a key risk given the sector’s continued dependence on overseas suppliers for batteries and other critical components,” he added. Developers with limited scale or procurement track records may face challenges in securing equipment on competitive terms, which could adversely impact internal rate of returns (IRRs), Hakhu said. “Consequently, any increase in procurement costs, coupled with execution-related challenges, could moderate IRRs and/or result in delays in project commissioning. Early signs of these pressures are already evident across parts of the under-construction pipeline with projects getting stranded,” he added. The remaining 45-50 GWh of capacity has a higher likelihood of being commissioned during FY27 and FY28. “That said, most awarded capacity remains either in the development stage or in the early phases of construction. The sector continues to depend heavily on overseas suppliers for batteries and other critical components. While long-term battery demand is underpinned by strong structural drivers, the potential impact of geopolitical developments and disruptions to global supply chains warrants close monitoring,” Crisil Ratings emphasised. Published on September 29, 2026

artigo.texto: Evento em São Paulo discute os desafios regulatórios e as oportunidades de negócio para os leilões de armazenamento de energia elétrica (baterias) previstos para dezembro de 2026, com a presença de líderes do setor elétrico. A Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (ABSOLAR) realiza, no dia 30 de setembro, em São Paulo, um evento que reúne autoridades do setor elétrico e empresas para debater as regras dos primeiros leilões de baterias no Brasil. O foco da discussão é o Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade na forma de Armazenamento (LRCAP-BESS), que ocorrerá em dezembro. O principal objetivo do encontro é discutir os avanços necessários na legislação para tornar esses leilões viáveis e competitivos. - O evento reúne reguladores, bancos e empresas de energia. - O foco é resolver problemas legais que travam o investimento em baterias. - Os primeiros leilões acontecerão nos dias 2 e 4 de dezembro de 2026. - Há uma disputa sobre quem deve pagar uma taxa de capacidade no sistema. - O evento busca atrair mais investimentos para a segurança energética. Participantes de peso discutem o futuro do armazenamento Diversas autoridades confirmaram presença no debate. Entre eles estão Reinaldo Garcia, da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE), Gerusa Côrtes, da Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE), Tiago Barros Correa, da RegE, e Mauricio Bernhardt Maciel, do BNDES. Também estão presentes membros da diretoria da ABSOLAR e convidados da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (ANEEL) e do Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS). O evento, chamado de ABSOLAR Storage Leaders, tem como tema central a viabilidade, a regulação e a criação de um novo mercado de capacidade. A programação inclui painéis sobre modelos de contratação, financiamento, inovação tecnológica e como os sistemas de armazenamento podem ser aplicados na prática. O evento conta com o apoio de grandes players do mercado, como Banco BV, Amara NZero, Sungrow, Topband e WEG. Desafios regulatórios exigem atenção imediata Bárbara Rubim, presidente do Conselho de Administração da ABSOLAR, destacou que o caminho para o sucesso dos leilões exige melhorias nas leis. Ela apontou preocupações com dispositivos do edital que podem gerar insegurança jurídica e atrapalhar a atratividade dos investimentos. É importante que o processo de aperfeiçoamento editalício avance de forma a criar condições adequadas para que os projetos de armazenamento possam ser estruturados e financiados, afirmou a presidente. Um ponto crítico, segundo Rodrigo Sauaia, CEO da ABSOLAR, é a forma como a lei atual trata os custos. A Lei nº 15.269/2025 atribui aos empreendedores de geração a responsabilidade de pagar o Encargo de Contratação de Reserva de Capacidade (ERCAP) quando usam sistemas de armazenamento. Isso cria uma assimetria, já que soluções que prestam o mesmo serviço ao Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) recebem tratamentos diferentes, violando o princípio da neutralidade tecnológica. Proposta de lei busca corrigir a desigualdade Para corrigir esse ponto, o deputado federal Arnaldo Jardim autorizou o Projeto de Lei nº 3.716/2026, que propõe alterar essa regra. Esse ajuste representa um importante aperfeiçoamento legal ao eliminar um dispositivo que estabelece tratamento distinto para soluções que prestam o mesmo serviço ao Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), explicou Sauaia. A mudança visa garantir que todos os participantes do mercado sofram os mesmos custos e obrigações, independentemente da tecnologia utilizada. A programação do dia 30 de setembro começa às 8h, com credenciamento e cerimônia de abertura. Em seguida, mesas e painéis serão realizados para detalhar a implantação do armazenamento em larga escala no País. O objetivo é alinhar o setor público e privado para que os desafios econômicos e regulatórios sejam superados, consolidando essa nova frente de investimentos no setor elétrico brasileiro.

artigo.texto: China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and six other government departments have jointly issued a 15th five-year plan for the development of the new-type battery industry, outlining development targets and key tasks through 2030. China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and six other government departments have jointly released a plan for the new-type battery industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), setting out development goals and key priorities. Image Source: MIIT Key Takeaways By 2030, China aims to achieve steady growth in the new-type battery industry, with advances in full-chain innovation, new-type battery systems and solid-state battery commercialization. The plan also sets targets of 15,000 cycles for long-life lithium batteries and PPB-level product defect rates for leading companies. The plan outlines 19 key tasks across five major areas, supported by five dedicated programs. On technology innovation, the plan calls for advances in solid-state battery industrialization technologies and next-generation battery systems, while promoting a product portfolio led by lithium batteries alongside sodium-ion and flow batteries and improving battery recycling. At the industry level, the plan calls for digital and green transformation, optimized regional industrial distribution, and stronger standards, testing, certification, intellectual property and carbon-footprint traceability systems. 2030 targets By 2030, the plan targets steady growth in China’s new-type battery industry and continued improvement in innovation across the value chain. It calls for major progress in new-type battery systems and the initial achievement of scaled application of all-solid-state batteries. Long-life lithium batteries are targeted to reach a cycle life of 15,000 cycles, while leading companies are expected to achieve PPB-level product defect rates. The plan also envisions new-type battery technologies supporting electrification across vehicles, ships, aviation, construction machinery and energy storage, with applications expanding on the power-generation and grid sides as well as in industrial parks and data centers. Technology and industrial development The plan identifies frontier technology research as a priority, including efforts to address key technologies for solid-state battery industrialization and to develop next-generation battery systems. It also calls for improvements in industrial software and high-end equipment, alongside a supply system centered on lithium batteries and supported by sodium-ion and flow batteries. The plan further calls for digitalization and green transformation across the industry, the development of green factories and zero-carbon industrial parks, optimized regional industrial distribution, and the cultivation of high-quality enterprise clusters at different stages of development. International cooperation and implementation For international cooperation, the policy encourages battery companies to expand overseas in an orderly manner, strengthen risk controls for overseas investment, establish international industrial cooperation platforms and respond to technical trade barriers in overseas markets. For implementation, the plan calls for stronger coordination among government departments, coordinated financial support, broader financing channels for key companies, deeper integration between industry and education, and a fair and orderly competitive environment.

artigo.texto: Mensagens entre Motta e Vorcaro citam “sociedade” em negócio e discussão de projeto de mercado de carbono Motta vê insignificância nas conversas e rejeita qualquer relação de favorecimento Conteúdo de mensagens extraídas pela Polícia Federal do celular de Daniel Vorcaro, dono do Banco Master, publicados pelo site Fatos Online e confirmados pela Folha de São Paulo, nesta segunda-feira (28), registra, o presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), mencionando um formato de “sociedade” durante tratativas para a compra de um terreno em João Pessoa (PB), que estava em nome da cunhada do parlamentar. Os diálogos tiveram início em 9 de março de 2024 em meio às negociações para aquisição de uma área onde funcionava uma fábrica de cimento na capital paraibana, e também registraram contatos sobre um projeto de lei relacionado ao mercado de carbono, o Fundo Garantidor de Créditos (FGC) e a disponibilização de uma aeronave. Motta vê insignificância nas conversas e rejeita qualquer relação de favorecimento. Na mensagem a Vorcaro, Motta tratou diretamente da negociação e sugeriu um modelo societário que, segundo ele, já havia sido combinado. “Boa noite amigo. Td bem? Desculpa incomodar no sábado, estou aqui reunido com o pessoal para finalizar a negociação de compra da área aqui de JP”. “Conforme falamos, já temos os documentos assinados passando a empresa para a minha cunhada ela iniciou a negociação com a Adriana mas acredito que ela não tá sabendo do formato de sociedade que ficou combinado“, escreveu Motta, que em seguida pediu orientação ao ex-banqueiro. “Quando puder me orienta como devemos proceder pq o prazo é curto para saldar com Intercement (empresa do ramo de produção de cimento)”. Segundo a Folha, a cunhada de Motta já havia contratado naquele período um empréstimo de ao menos R$ 22 milhões com o Banco Master, valor que teria sido solicitado diretamente pelo presidente da Câmara, com os recursos sendo utilizados na compra do terreno de mais de 400 hectares da antiga fábrica de cimento, dando lugar a um futuro bairro na capital paraibana. Outro diálogo ocorreu quatro dias depois da primeira mensagem, com Motta tratando do andamento da operação, após Vorcaro informar que estava em reunião com o “nosso amigo”, ao que o deputado respondeu; “Certo, meu sogro está até aqui, queria levar ele pq acabamos agora de desenrolar as assinaturas que faltavam para prosseguir o pagamento. Se vc achar conveniente, analisa e me avisa””. Em 15 de março, Motta enviou nova mensagem a Vorcaro, quando disse que estava “passando para agradecer a confiança e a parceria”. “Deu tudo certo a tempo de cumprir o contrato. depois vamos marcar uma conversa para traçar os próximos passos, acredito que vamos ter êxito no projeto! Forte abraço!”. Vorcaro respondeu: “muito feliz de estarmos juntos! Te admiro muito e esse é o início de uma parceria de vida”. Ao que Motta respondeu: “com certeza, meu amigo, a admiração é recíproca!”. O preço pago pelo terreno foi de R$ 45 milhões, enquanto o valor fiscal é de R$ 101 milhões, calculado pela Prefeitura e serve, entre outras finalidades, como referência para tributação. Os diálogos também mostram que a interlocução entre ambos alcançou um assunto em discussão no Congresso Nacional. Em novembro de 2024, os dois conversaram sobre um projeto de lei relacionado ao mercado de carbono. No dia 19 deste mesmo mês, Vorcaro pergunta: “consegue encontrar mais tarde hoje”. Motta respondeu: “sim. Pegando o texto aqui para te mandar”. Em 23 de março de 2024, Motta pediu a Vorcaro que lembrasse sua equipe de preparar um estudo sobre o Fundo Garantidor de Créditos. “Quando puder lembra de pedir ao seu pessoal o estudo daquele assunto do FGC, se você for a Brasília essa semana podemos tentar encaixar esse assunto”. Outro diálogo, de 27 de abril de 2024, indica que Vorcaro colocou uma aeronave à disposição do deputado. Motta perguntou ao ex-banqueiro de onde partiria o avião que faria seu deslocamento até Guarulhos, em São Paulo, para Brasília. “Já vai estar te esperando”, diz Vorcaro. Procurado, Motta afirmou por meio de sua assessoria que sempre manteve interlocução com diferentes setores durante sua atuação parlamentar, e que o empréstimo envolvendo a empresa privada ocorreu antes de se tornarem públicos os fatos e as investigações relacionados ao Banco Master e a Vorcaro. “Reitero que confio nos órgãos responsáveis pelas investigações, a quem cabe responder pelas apurações”, finalizou.

artigo.texto: Tanzanian Carbon Project Suspension Highlights Global Shift Toward High-Integrity Credit Standards Carbon Tanzania halted its Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape Project as international buyers pivot to Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market principles, exposing domestic regulatory and data gaps. Market Realities Force Project Halt Carbon Tanzania has temporarily suspended its Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape Project, a major REDD+ forest protection initiative in northern Tanzania, citing a sharp decline in funding driven by shifting global market demands and rising compliance costs. The suspension highlights a critical tension in the voluntary carbon market, where international buyers are increasingly prioritizing carbon credits certified under the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market’s (ICVCM) Core Carbon Principles (CCP). This shift toward high-integrity standards is inadvertently sidelining legacy projects in developing nations that lack the resources to meet the new, more stringent methodologies. Sally Capper, Chief Executive Officer of Carbon Tanzania, explained that the decision to halt the project was necessary to allow stakeholders to address the financial and regulatory challenges and to identify solutions that will enable the project to transition to CCP-labelled standards and secure long-term funding. The suspension underscores the vulnerability of community-based conservation projects to the evolving preferences of global corporate buyers seeking to mitigate reputational risks associated with low-quality carbon offsets. Impact on Local Communities and Conservation The Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape Project protects approximately 108,000 hectares of dryland forest in the ancestral homeland of the Hadza hunter-gatherers, who have inhabited the area for thousands of years. Implemented since 2013 through a partnership between Carbon Tanzania and the Hadza and Datooga communities, the project works with 11 villages involving about 63,000 people across the Manyara and Arusha regions. The initiative has been a vital source of revenue for these communities, funding local development, healthcare, and education while incentivizing the protection of critical biodiversity. The disruption of revenues caused by the changing voluntary carbon market threatens the livelihoods of these communities and could lead to increased deforestation and land degradation if alternative funding mechanisms are not found. Capper noted that the combination of changing market expectations and prohibitive domestic regulatory costs has severely impacted the financial viability of the project, forcing a temporary pause in operations while the organization seeks to upgrade its methodologies to meet the new global standards. The Shift to Core Carbon Principles The global voluntary carbon market is undergoing a significant transformation as buyers demand greater transparency, additionality, and permanence in carbon offset projects. The ICVCM's Core Carbon Principles represent a new benchmark for quality, requiring projects to demonstrate rigorous baselines, robust monitoring, and clear social and environmental safeguards. While this shift is intended to improve the integrity of the carbon market and ensure that emissions reductions are real and measurable, it imposes high costs on project developers who must invest in new technologies, data collection, and third-party verification. Carbon Tanzania faces the additional challenge of a lack of national datasets required under the new CCP methodologies, making it difficult to quickly transition its credits to meet emerging global standards. This data gap is a common issue across many African nations, where historical deforestation rates and carbon stock measurements are often incomplete or outdated, creating a barrier to entry for local developers seeking to access the premium segment of the carbon market. Regulatory and Structural Challenges Beyond the technical requirements of the CCP, domestic regulatory frameworks in Tanzania and other developing nations often pose significant hurdles for carbon project developers. Capper highlighted that the existing regulatory environment makes it costly for local projects to meet the new standards, with complex permitting processes and unclear revenue-sharing rules adding to the financial burden. The suspension of the Yaeda-Eyasi project has prompted stakeholders to call for comprehensive reforms to the carbon trading framework in Tanzania, urging the government to streamline regulations, provide technical support for data collection, and create a more enabling environment for high-integrity carbon projects. These reforms are essential to ensure that African nations can continue to participate in the global carbon market and benefit from the financial flows associated with climate mitigation. Without such interventions, there is a risk that the voluntary carbon market will become dominated by large, well-funded projects in developed countries, marginalizing the community-based initiatives that are often most effective at protecting forests and supporting indigenous livelihoods. Future Prospects and Market Adaptation The temporary suspension of the Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape Project serves as a wake-up call for the entire voluntary carbon market, highlighting the need for a more inclusive and equitable approach to setting quality standards. While the pursuit of high-integrity credits is necessary to maintain market credibility, it must be balanced with support for projects in developing nations that face structural and financial constraints. Carbon Tanzania and its partners are now working to secure the necessary funding and technical assistance to upgrade the project to CCP standards, a process that will require significant investment and collaboration with international donors and technical experts. The outcome of this transition will be closely watched by other project developers across Africa and the Global South, as it will set a precedent

artigo.texto: Fumaça sobe sobre a sede da operadora Kyivstar, em Kiev, na Ucrânia — Foto: Reuters A Rússia atacou neste domingo (27) a sede da Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia, informou a empresa à mídia local. O ataque ocorreu enquanto Moscou mantinha bombardeios contra data centers e infraestrutura de comunicações do país. A Kyivstar informou à agência de notícias Interfax Ucrânia que sua sede em Kiev foi atingida, mas não houve vítimas. O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia também informou neste domingo que atingiu um data center da Vodafone Ucrânia, segunda maior operadora de telefonia celular do país. A Vodafone Ucrânia não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, afirmou que a Rússia atacou duas vezes um data center em Kiev na manhã deste domingo, ferindo duas crianças e um adulto. Moscou também atingiu, na semana passada, data centers de provedores de internet ucranianos, provocando interrupções no serviço para cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev e arredores, de acordo com o Ministério Digital da Ucrânia. "A Rússia tem como alvo os principais data centers ucranianos, buscando interromper o fluxo de informações. Alertas rápidos sobre ameaças de mísseis e drones são essenciais -- eles salvam vidas", escreveu o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha, no X na quarta-feira (23).

artigo.texto: JA, a global leader in photovoltaic products and integrated energy solutions, is expanding its European range of commercial and industrial (C&I) battery storage systems (BESS) with the launch of JAPlanet Fusion and JAPlanet 2.0. JAPlanet Fusion is a DC-coupled hybrid solution for PV and battery storage that combines inverters, battery storage and backup functionality in one system. In parallel, JAPlanet 2.0 is the latest generation of JA’s established AC-coupled C&I battery storage system, adding higher efficiency, optimized thermal management, and improved operation and maintenance (O&M) capabilities to the JAPlanet platform. Both systems are designed to provide C&I customers and project partners with greater flexibility in the design of storage systems for different site, grid and operational requirements. JAPlanet Fusion: PV, storage and backup in one system JAPlanet Fusion integrates inverters, battery storage, and backup functionality into one coordinated system, simplifying system planning, installation, and commissioning. Component integration reduces system interfaces, cabling overhead, and reduces space requirements. It can also reduce the risk of compatibility issues between separately procured components. The system has a battery cabinet with a capacity of 261 kWh and a nominal power of 125 kW. Thanks to the modular architecture, up to 10 units can be operated in parallel in grid-connected operation and up to six units in island operation, allowing the system capacity to be flexibly adapted to project requirements. JAPlanet Fusion is particularly suitable for solar repowering projects. The system can accommodate a PV input power of up to 250 kWp, enabling the installation of additional PV power on the DC side with up to 20 strings and 10 MPP trackers, while keeping the AC output power within the grid power limit allowed at the site. For plant operators, this opens up the opportunity to make better use of existing solar systems and grid connections, integrate energy storage and increase operational resilience. At the same time, coordination with distribution system operators is simplified by reducing complexity and time required for projects that would otherwise require an increase in grid connection capacity. For backup applications, an integrated static transfer switch (STS) detects a power failure and switches the system to island mode within 10 milliseconds to maintain the supply of critical loads. The system also includes liquid cooling, continuous monitoring of temperature, smoke and gases, integrated aerosol fire suppression, and redundant dual-channel ventilation in accordance with NFPA 69. “Across Europe, there is a growing potential to upgrade aging solar installations with more powerful technology. However, grid constraints can make increasing generation capacity complex and time-consuming. At the same time, companies want more control over their energy consumption and greater resilience to grid disruptions,” says Ignacio Espinosa Gil, Head of the European Technical Team at JA. “JAPlanet Fusion was developed with this next generation of C&I projects in mind. By integrating PV, storage and fast backup functionality into a single system, we can offer our partners a more efficient approach to system planning and implementation, while enabling better utilization of PV generation and greater resilience based on existing site infrastructure.” JAPlanet 2.0: AC-coupled BESS of the latest generation In addition to JAPlanet Fusion, JAPlanet 2.0 brings the latest generation of JA’s AC-coupled C&I battery storage technology to Europe. The 261 kWh system achieves a maximum round-trip efficiency of over 90% and can operate at ambient temperatures of up to 50 °C without reducing power. Intelligent thermal management reduces auxiliary energy consumption by 20% compared to conventional systems, improving system efficiency while supporting operation in different environmental conditions. High product safety is ensured by cell-level monitoring as well as UL-9540A testing of the entire battery system. JAPlanet 2.0 is equipped with JANebula, a new integrated energy management system (EMS) for applications such as time-of-use optimization, peak shaving or a higher PV self-consumption rate. The system complies with EU regulations on product safety. JAPlanet Fusion and JAPlanet 2.0 will be available for pre-order in Europe from the second half of September 2026. The first deliveries of JAPlanet Fusion are scheduled for the end of the fourth quarter of 2026. Both systems will also be presented as part of the JA customer roadshow Journey Ahead 2026, which runs until the end of October 2026. Further information at www.journeyahead.eu. JAPlanet Fusion

artigo.texto: URBANA — Dozens of students and community members gathered in front of Foellinger Auditorium on the Main Quad at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign to show their opposition to the construction of AI data centers in Champaign County. The protest on Friday, Sept. 25 was organized by the Students for Environmental Concerns (SECS), a registered student organization at the U of I. Gabi DelSanto, SECS president and a U of I senior, said the group got involved with data center matters after meeting the co-founders of Resist AI Data Centers in Champaign County — Ruth Yontz and Antonia Herbstreit. “So that really lit a fire under us,” DelSanto said. “We started planning out ways that we would get involved with them and involved with other organizations to stop [data centers] from being built in Champaign.” Yontz and Herbstreit were also at Friday’s protest. Herbstreit said she worries about the Mahomet Aquifer. “If our aquifer gets polluted, there is no way to clean that back up to drinking water,” she said. The Mahomet Aquifer supplies water to about 1 million people across 14 counties in central Illinois. Herbstreit said she worries that if this source were to become contaminated or drained by data centers, communities across the region would be harmed. Lauryn Barnett, a sophomore in political science at the U of I, said she attended the protest to voice her concerns about protecting nature more broadly. “I think it’s very important that we take care of our environment,” Barnett said. “We know what these data centers are doing, not only in Champaign, but in Chicago and all across the country. We want to make sure that we are protecting our environment the same way it has been doing for us for the last centuries.” The protest hosted speakers from Prairie Rivers Network, Black Students for Revolution and Students for Socialism, and the U of I’s Thomas M. Siebel Center for Computer Science. The speakers shared personal testimony and insights about data centers and the harm they could cause to humans and the environment. Next steps for a local data center ordinance Emotions are high as community members await news from the Champaign County Data Center and Activities Task Force, which is developing a local ordinance to regulate new construction of data centers in the county. The county’s 12-month moratorium on data centers with at least 10,000 square feet of processing space expires in April 2027. Officials say that since Champaign County is not a home-rule county, its authority is limited by powers granted by the state. So, an outright ban is not possible, they say — but they can pass an ordinance to regulate land usage through zoning. While they wait for news about the ordinance, Yontz said she and Herbstreit will continue to provide public input at the Data Center Task Force’s meetings. The task force is considering adding a required decommissioning bond for data center developers, which would require developers to put money aside so that if the data center were to shut down, they can properly remove all internal equipment so the property can be repurposed for future use. “We are already talking to them,” Yontz said. “We are going to their meetings. We [are] providing all different aspects of the ordinance that they’re working on.” The task force discussed several potential regulations at its meeting on Monday, Sept. 21. Task force chair Emily Rodriguez, vice chair of the Champaign County Board, says they hope to have a draft ordinance finalized by November.

artigo.texto: Not content with building the world’s fastest production car, BYD’s ultra-high-end offshoot Yangwang is taking on Rolls-Royce in its bid for industry domination. The company is hard at work developing a flagship luxury sedan, as seen in these images the company’s general manager Hu Xiaoqing shared on Weibo. Not much is known officially, save for its internal codename HU (no relation, surely?). However, the images gives us a glimpse of what the car will look like, even if the camouflage obscures much of the design details. As you can see, the car is very long, certainly well north of five metres. The styling carries all the tropes of big-car design – an upright body (not quite as upright as a Rolls-Royce, but still), thick C-pillars and, of course, RR-style suicide doors. The wheels are surprisingly small for such a vehicle, however, at only 21 inches in diameter. Very much unlike the U7, which lifts its design language from the U9 supercar, this new model (U10?) takes after the U8 SUV instead. The headlights feature a wavy design said to be inspired by a celestial gate and, on this particular model, come with jewel-like projectors and frosted light signatures. As yet, it is unclear if the car is fully electric like the U7 and U9, or a range-extended EV like the U8. The long bonnet suggests it hides an engine underneath; however, it’s also been reported by Autohome that it will feature BYD’s first solid-state battery, hinting at a long range without the need of a generator. It should also support the carmaker’s new 1,500 kW Flash Charging technology, allowing it to be topped up from 10 to 70% in just five minutes. The news comes as BYD prepares Yangwang for an global rollout, following in the footsteps of Denza. The brand has already launched in the Middle East earlier and is planned to enter Europe and the UK next year, according to Autocar.

artigo.texto: The India Energy Storage Alliance (IESA) has introduced its ‘BESS for C&I’ initiative in Mumbai to accelerate battery energy storage adoption among commercial and industrial (C&I) consumers. The initiative aims to empower 300 C&I consumers with storage solutions over the next three years. India’s C&I battery storage capacity has increased from 40 MWh to 650 MWh and is projected to reach nearly 4 GWh by FY2027. However, high upfront costs, evolving regulations, limited financing options and gaps in user awareness continue to constrain wider adoption. Starting October 2026, BESS for C&I will conduct monthly sessions bringing together industry representatives, developers and policymakers to discuss deployment, economics and best practices. The initiative will operate as a free workgroup for C&I consumers and provide policy updates, technology trends and pricing insights, along with access to B2B meetings, technology tours and masterclasses. “The BESS for C&I platform is designed to address the unique challenges faced by commercial and industrial energy consumers as battery storage becomes essential for grid flexibility and business resilience. No single technology can meet all system needs; collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and innovation across the value chain are critical to accelerating adoption and shaping India’s battery storage future,” said Debmalya Sen, President, IESA. Industry participants highlighted the need for domestic cell and component manufacturing, stronger supply chains and clearer regulations to support the sector. Bharat Chhittarka, Director, Trex Energy, called for states to establish clear policies covering time-of-day tariffs, energy arbitrage and peak shaving to encourage large-scale BESS deployment. Bimal Jindal, CEO, Energy Business, JBM Renewables Private Limited, emphasised the need to build a domestic battery ecosystem covering component manufacturing, lithium carbonate, cell production and R&D. He also suggested increasing mandated BESS deployment and reducing GST on BESS from 18 per cent to 5 per cent. Sushmita R. Ajwani, Head of Business Development (C&I), Aditya Birla Renewables, highlighted domestic cell manufacturing, regulatory clarity and targeted incentives as important factors for accelerating adoption. Meanwhile, Inder Bhambra, COO-BESS and Chief Business Officer, India region, Envision Energy India Limited, called for local development of cell technologies and DC container assembly, along with rationalisation of open-access and transmission-related charges. IESA said utility-scale battery storage capex has risen 15 per cent in recent months, adding to project cost volatility. Through IESA Connect, the alliance plans to extend the initiative to cities and industrial clusters across India, involving C&I consumers in discussions around policy, standards and safety. The initiative will operate as a free workgroup for C&I consumers and provide policy updates, technology trends and pricing insights, along with access to B2B meetings, technology tours and masterclasses.“The BESS for C&I platform is designed to address the unique challenges faced by commercial and industrial energy consumers as battery storage becomes essential for grid flexibility and business resilience. artigo.texto: The Walker County Data Center Development Standards Study Committee reconvened recently for its third meeting, undertaking a section-by-section review of the county’s initial draft data center ordinance. Key discussions focused on parcel size thresholds, conditional use options, water capacity limits, and a tense exchange regarding committee transparency and industry conflicts. Draft Ordinance Review: Parcel Minimums and Micro-Facility Rules Planning & Zoning Director Jon Pursley and Economic Development Director Stephanie Watkins opened the session by outlining updates to the draft ordinance. Following recommendations from prior meetings, staff added Section 15, which mandates upfront performance and decommissioning bonds to protect the county from abandoned infrastructure. Under Section 3 (Land Use), the draft restricts data centers to industrially zoned districts and establishes a 10-acre minimum parcel size. Committee members debated whether a 10-acre requirement is suitable for smaller “micro-facilities” or fiber “booster stations” which can occupy as little as 5,000 square feet and consume minimal power and water. District 1 Appointee Barney Danks said restricting data centers strictly to the industrial zone could make land disappear quickly. He questioned why would the county force an industry to locate on 10-acres, if it only needs two. “I think commercial sites, whether existing in the county today or in the future, may want to have a ‘data center’ that is small.” He encouraged the committee to focus industrial zone requirements on hyper-scale operations. “Not every data center is the same as another data center.” The other District 1 appointee, Jason Rader, suggested restrictions for data centers with a footprint greater than 50,000 square feet. “I think smaller ones should be allowed in commercial. It’s no different than other buildings. It could be a dollar store or anything else.” Pursley explained that developers seeking smaller footprints or commercial locations (such as C1 or C2 zones) can apply for a conditional use permit or variance, allowing the Board of Commissioners case-by-case oversight. County records show Walker County contains 63 industrial-zoned parcels with a majority of the acreage located within the Walker County Business Park (400 acres) and the Northwest Georgia Business Park in Rock Spring (50 acres). Appointees agreed to consult legal counsel to confirm whether restricting facilities strictly to established industrial parks is legally defensible. Closed Loop Cooling Systems and Committee Member Experience District 3 Appointee Laura Owsley questioned District 1 Appointee Barney Danks regarding his industry holdings. Danks mentioned he operates an 8-megawatt Bitcoin mining facility on 2.5 acres along Glentana Road using open-air cooling fans. Owsley raised concerns over a lack of prior disclosure and questioned whether Danks resides in Walker County. Danks clarified that while he owns commercial property and businesses in Rossville and Walker County, he resides elsewhere. He acknowledged that his 6-year-old facility relies on older open-air technology, which generates noise and would not comply with proposed modern standards, and expressed support for requiring closed-loop cooling systems for future developments. Committee members appear favorable toward recommending closed-loop system requirements in their report. Water Capacity Limits, Utility Easements, and Power Restrictions Resource protection remained a core focus. While Walker County Water and Sewer maintains an excess capacity of 4.5 to 5 million gallons per day, officials noted that upcoming commercial developments (such as the Pilgrim’s prepared foods facility) and residential housing growth will absorb much of that margin. To prevent unexpected grid strain, the committee agreed to require developers to submit utility capacity confirmation letters covering all project phases prior to permit approval. On power infrastructure, Danks noted the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) now requires major power users to pay $1.5 million per megawatt upfront for infrastructure expansion. The committee discussed prohibiting on-site fossil fuel power plants and requiring data center developers, and not utility companies or the county, to secure their own utility easements to prevent the use of eminent domain through residential neighborhoods. Setbacks, Green Space, and Environmental Protections The committee reviewed physical development standards under Section 4: - Setbacks & Buffers: The draft establishes a 100-foot setback between adjacent industrial properties and a 400-foot setback from residential properties, matching the county’s restrictive poultry house standards. - Green Space & Height: Parcels must maintain a 15% minimum green space buffer, and buildings are capped at a maximum height of 50 feet. HVAC units and generators must be placed on roofs or oriented away from residential borders. - Environmental & Historic Protections: Owsley advocated adding an anti-clustering clause to prevent cumulative air quality impacts and urged prohibiting data centers in historic districts such as McLemore Cove. Next Steps and Data Center Tour Committee members will take a tour early next month of regional data centers and booster stations to see operations firsthand. At their next meeting, they plan to discuss sound/noise and lighting restrictions. The committee is working toward a December 4 deadline to finalize its draft recommendations. Once complete, the proposed ordinance will move to the Planning & Zoning Board for public hearings before reaching the Board of Commissioners for a final vote in early 2027. artigo.texto: WEG (WEGE3) anuncia plano de investimento de R$ 840 milhões de olho na expansão de data centers; veja A WEG (WEGE3) anunciou nesta segunda-feira (28) um plano de investimento de US$ 165 milhões, aproximadamente R$ 840 milhões, para expandir sua capacidade de produção de geradores na América do Norte. De acordo com o comunicado ao mercado, o projeto se dará em duas fases, visando atender à crescente demanda por soluções de geração de energia para aplicações críticas nos Estados Unidos, especialmente impulsionada pela expansão dos data centers. “A iniciativa representa mais um passo na estratégia de crescimento dos negócios incorporados à companhia por meio da aquisição da Marathon”, diz a WEG. Vale recordar que, em setembro de 2023, a WEG anunciou a aquisição dos negócios de motores elétricos industriais e geradores da norte-americana Regal Rexnord no valor de US$ 400 milhões. A transação, conforme anunciado à época, teve como foco os negócios de motores elétricos industriais e geradores, vendidos sob as marcas Marathon, Cemp e Rotor. Receba gratuitamente as newsletters do Money Times As fases do investimento A primeira fase do projeto da WEG contempla investimentos de US$ 24 milhões para aquisição e adequação de um prédio industrial localizado ao lado do atual Parque Industrial de Quma I, em Atotonilco de Tula, no México. A unidade será destinada à montagem de geradores e contribuirá para a expansão da capacidade produtiva da companhia, com início das operações previsto para o segundo trimestre de 2027. Na segunda fase, em local ainda a ser definido na América do Norte, a WEG investirá US$ 141 milhões na construção de duas novas instalações industriais. O projeto prevê a implantação de uma estrutura produtiva verticalizada que abrangerá processos estratégicos como fabricação de lâminas, bobinas de baixa e média tensão, eixos e carcaças, aumentando a eficiência operacional e a competitividade da operação. Ao fim da segunda fase, prevista para ser concluída em 2030, a companhia terá capacidade global de fabricar cerca de 50 geradores por dia em suas fábricas no México, EUA, Brasil e China, ante a atual capacidade de 10 geradores por dia.

artigo.texto: Why Calumet County hasn't passed a data center moratorium CHILTON (WLUK) -- While other cities and counties are passing data center moratoriums, Calumet County has not. It's because their zoning ordinance already doesn't allow data centers in the county. "We didn't need to [pass a moratorium]," said Calumet County Administrator Todd Romenesko. "Our current ordinance does not allow it as permissible use." A legal adviser said because it isn't allowed as permissible use, a moratorium would be redundant. "From my standpoint, you don't need a moratorium in Calumet County," said Rebecca Roeker, attorney at Attolles Law, who advised the county on Monday night. "Again, because of your existing ordinances and because of the modifications that the elected officials are going to consider in the near future." - RELATED: Manitowoc County Board votes unanimously to impose 18-month moratorium on data centers - RELATED: Winnebago County will pursue 12-month data center moratorium Any modifications would likely just be to close any potential legal loopholes. These zoning ordinances apply to townships in the county, but not necessarily villages or cities. For example, it'll apply in the town of Woodville, but may not in the city of Chilton, as villages and cities may have their own separate zoning ordinances. Romenesko said there are no current data center proposals in the county. The discussion comes as the Chicago-based Invenergy has proposed a natural gas energy project and wind energy project in the county, which has raised concerns from residents about the possibility of a new data center in the county. County Administrator Todd Romenesko says there's no link. "This just happened to be something we were trying to be proactive on regarding trying to regulate anything regarding data centers," said Romenesko. The county does already have several small data centers, according to Romenesko. Because Calumet County has lots of open land, it could be the target of a major data center development.

artigo.texto: VERNON — Residents of Vernon and the surrounding area asked questions about fire safety, chemical emissions, employment, taxes and noise during a recent public community forum put on by PowerTransitions, the Texas company that is studying the Vermont Yankee nuclear power plant site for potential reuse. The community gathering, held last Wednesday at the Governor Hunt House community center, drew a large crowd as PowerTransitions officials were questioned about their stated priority to build a battery energy storage facility on a portion of the site. Area residents asked questions about potential employment, noise, property taxes, and fire safety with the large batteries and PowerTransitions' timetable. One woman said the town is concerned about the impact of any battery storage facility's noise – both the frequency emitted by batteries that large or the sound itself, on the nearby organic dairy cows at the Miller Farm. Carrie Cullen Hitt, a spokeswoman for PowerTransitions, said the company is committed to following Vernon's wishes, and as a result, it had dropped earlier plans for a data center or even a solar installation. There was no mention of a modular nuclear reactor, which has been mentioned earlier. "We have heard loud and clear," she said, "no data center and no solar." Hitt said PowerTransitions was in the process of studying the site, evaluating it and coming up with a plan. She did say that as a result of questions raised in Vernon during earlier meetings, PowerTransitions brought a fire safety expert to Wednesday's meeting to address concerns. Rocky Edwards, an engineer with TetraTech, said that battery technology is changing rapidly, and the batteries are safer than they were 10 years ago. He told the gathering that any fire at a battery storage facility would be fought with water. Two fires at battery storage facilities in other parts of the country have led to concern about the projects' safety. The batteries themselves are about the size of a trailer on a tractor-trailer unit, and would contain smoke detectors. The batteries have a life of between 15 to 20 years. They are typically eight feet wide, 22 feet long and 10 to 12 feet tall. The outside is "very plain," Edwards said. "It's really just a white box," he said, and he noted the batteries would be spaced apart. "If there's a fire, it will not affect the one right next to it," he said. Another PowerTransitions consultant, Derek Porter of Miami, said the size of the battery facility could range from 110 megawatts to 440 megawatts, and as a result, Vernon and the state of Vermont would benefit, tax wise, on the amount of power stored and then released back on the grid. Hitt said an important role for battery storage facilities is to "smooth out the peaks and valleys" on the electric grid, and make the electric grid more stable and reliable. He said the company is thinking of applying to ISO-New England, the regional electric grid operator, for a place on its next "interconnect queue" for joining the grid, in preparation for its project. The battery storage facility would take electricity off the grid during low-usage times, and put it back on the grid at high demand times. PowerTransitions has a lease with NorthStar Group Services, the owner of the 140-acre Yankee site. While demolition and cleanup is almost complete at Yankee, its 42 years of high-level radioactive waste in the form of its old fuel rods, would remain in the steel and concrete casks. Kerrick Johnson, Vermont's commissioner of the Department of Public Service, said the state's position on PowerTransitions' plans would be made after a proposal is made. "Of course our Department’s position will be determined by what is actually, formally proposed and the facts in the matter," Johnson said via email on Tuesday. "My general view though is that done right, a battery could serve as an affordable reliability and grid flexibility asset, and could also serve as a complementary piece to a generator of some sort that could be co-located on that site." "In that way the site could be fully utilized in a manner that delivers the greatest value to the community, state and region," said Johnson, who has said previously he wanted Vermont ratepayers' investment in the VELCO switchyard to have some return. A battery storage facility has never been built near a nuclear fuel storage facility, the PowerTransitions people said, although they had consulted with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission about it. Hitt said that assuming PowerTransitions does go forward with the battery storage facility in Vernon, it would reserve the right to install some additional kind of power generation there as well. She didn't say what kind. No mention was made by PowerTransitions during the two-hour session about the possibility of a small modular nuclear reactor. But one women said at the end, "I don't think a nuke plant would be very welcome." Hitt had apologized at the beginning of the session for originally asking for RSVPs when the company first sent out notice of the meeting. She said the company backed off that request in the face of questions. She said PowerTransitions is not compiling a list of names, phone numbers or email addresses. Hitt said the Vermont Yankee site was a very complicated one. "You have a very unique site," she said. "Very interesting, very complex and very challenging. It's very challenging." But she emphasized that if the town is not supportive, PowerTransitions would not go forward, either in applying to the state for a Section 248 permit, or applying to ISO-New England. "We will be back," Hitt said at the end of the two-hour session. "This is Step One."

artigo.texto: Battery energy storage system is beginning to look like solar did a decade ago — a technology whose importance is moving rapidly from the drawing board to the electricity market. And, increasingly, the market itself is sending the signal. Government agencies are beginning to adapt the rules to make storage easier to deploy. The latest example is the Central Transmission Utility of India (CTUIL), which last week issued a procedure for BESS projects that have grid connectivity to seek an increase in their energy-storage capacity (MWh) without increasing their approved charging/discharging capacity (MW). The distinction is significant. A 100 MW/200 MWh battery can, for instance, become a 100 MW/400 MWh battery by adding storage capacity while retaining the same grid connection and power conversion capacity. CTUIL’s move gives developers a regulatory route to do this rather than having to treat the increase in MWh as an increase in grid connectivity. CTUIL is also seeking clarity from the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission over whether the ₹2 lakh per MW ‘Connectivity Bank Guarantee-3’ would apply when the increase is only in MWh. Pending clarification, it is not seeking BG-3 for such applications. But the strongest case for BESS may be coming from the electricity market. Former Grid-India CMD SR Narasimhan recently did a study by modelling the arbitrage potential of a 1 MW BESS using four years of day-ahead market data — 96 time blocks a day, 365 days a year, six storage durations and two operating models. The exercise shows that arbitrage opportunities have generally strengthened, with FY2025-26 emerging as the strongest year for most configurations. The other finding is equally interesting: longer-duration batteries earn more, but with diminishing returns. Moving from one hour to six hours of storage gives six times the energy capacity, but arbitrage revenue rises only 3.5–4.4 times. The battery captures the most attractive price spreads first. And the market is changing with solar. Cheap charging opportunities are increasingly moving from winter nights to solar-heavy afternoons, while discharge opportunities are emerging around demand peaks, including mornings. Then there is the ₹20-a-unit signal. Between September 6 and 17, the high price day-ahead market on IEX repeatedly touched its ₹20 per kWh ceiling, with much of the trading occurring in non-solar hours. At the same time, India’s peak demand touched a September record of 269 GW on September 10. Gas-based generation jumped 80.32 per cent year-on-year during September 1–9 as the system leaned on flexible generation to meet the evening shortfall. Meanwhile, solar capacity reached 168 GW as of August 31, according to data from the ministry of new and renewable energy. The message is becoming difficult to miss. Increasingly, India needs not just more electricity but also electricity at the right time. Solar solved the generation problem. BESS may solve the timing problem. And if ₹20 electricity is the price of getting power at the wrong hour, then the battery suddenly starts looking less like an accessory to renewable energy and more like the thing that makes renewable energy truly useful. artigo.texto: DICKINSON The city council next month will consider for final adoption an ordinance that would place more stringent regulations on battery energy storage systems, replicating a similar ordinance League City passed in July 2024, officials said Tuesday. The proposed regulations would classify battery energy storage systems as major utilities, a category that includes electric and gas generation plants, require operators to obtain a conditional use permit and impose extensive fire, safety and emergency-response requirements. Battery energy storage systems are being developed all over the country and county because they can provide on-demand electricity to supplement traditional power generation during periods of peak demand. That proliferation has caused concern among residents and city leaders about where the facilities are built in relation to neighborhoods and the risk of fires. At the Sept. 22 meeting, the council amended the proposal to require developers to pay the cost of an independent safety review up front before unanimously approving the ordinance on first reading. The proposed regulations come about five years after a battery storage facility was first built in Dickinson. Built in 2021, Dickinson’s battery energy storage facility has a capacity of almost 10 megawatts, which is enough to power about 2,500 homes during peak hours, according to the Electric Reliability Council of Texas. Councilman Mark Townsend, who proposed the initial ordinance, said he did so out of an abundance of caution. While there haven’t been any incidents at the Dickinson facility, battery fires are among the primary safety considerations, Townsend said. “You can’t put them out,” Townsend said. “They’re like a chemical reaction; you just have to let them burn out.” Battery energy storage systems stockpile electricity when it is inexpensive, storing it in battery banks until it is sold and released back into the grid during periods of higher demand, Townsend said. Proponents of the technology say the systems can reduce the risk of blackouts and increase the reliability of electrical grids where they are installed. Opponents have focused on the possibility of thermal runaway, a chain reaction that can occur when batteries are damaged or malfunction and can result in uncontrolled heating and fire that can be difficult to extinguish. Fires involving lithium-ion batteries, which are commonly used in battery storage facilities, can release toxic smoke containing hydrogen fluoride, according to a 2017 study published in the journal Scientific Reports. Much of the ordinance under consideration in Dickinson was taken directly from League City’s ordinance, Townsend said. “There’s no need to recreate the wheel, if you’ve got an ordinance that you can look at and adjust to your own town,” Townsend said. As Dickinson considers new regulations for battery storage systems, some municipalities around the country have faced public resistance to the facilities. Dickinson Fire Marshal Amber Phillips made recommendations on the proposed ordinance, including requirements that comply with the provisionally adopted 2024 International Fire Code, which addresses battery energy storage systems, she said. “The codes the city adopted establish requirements for items such as separation distances, fire protection features, emergency planning, and overall system safety,” Phillips said. “If a proposed facility meets the applicable code requirements and successfully completes the required review and permitting process it would be evaluated under the same nationally recognized standards that apply to any similar situation.” The second and final reading is scheduled to go before city council on Tuesday, Townsend said. A meeting agenda had not yet been posted at the time of publication.

artigo.texto: SALT LAKE CITY — In central Utah, plans are underway to build the world’s largest data center. In northwest Utah, a proposed data center and its famous backer have garnered protests. Politicians who advanced the project lost reelection bids in the recent primary contests. Yet, data centers already enjoy a certain ubiquity. By one count, Utah has 48 of them. Most of them are much smaller than the hyperscale ones being developed today. “This is the trend moving forward is bigger, larger data centers,” said Shon Hiatt, a professor at the University of Southern California who has studied Utah’s data center landscape. The centers store electronic data and provide the computing that fuels modern life – emails, text messages, web searches and social media scrolling. Surging through discussions like ones and zeroes are concerns about electricity, gas and water. And there are questions about who really benefits from data centers. “We sort of solve one problem,” said Michele Beck, who advocates for ratepayers as the director of the Utah Office of Consumer Services, “then we identify the next problem.” A team of journalists at FOX 13 News has spent months looking at how data centers are impacting Utah – and how they could change the state. In the coming weeks, we will tell you: - The military ties to the most-controversial data center. - What it’s like to live next to a data center. - What really happens inside one. - How data centers are changing rural Utah. - What data about you is stored. - Whether data centers could one day increase what Utahns pay for their utilities. “It's a really polarized world,” said Mark White, a professor at the University of Illinois who has been studying the rise of data centers in rural communities. “And this is one of those issues that seems to be uniting people from all different political persuasions.”

artigo.texto: WASHINGTON (CBS19 NEWS) -- Virginia Sen. Mark Warner is calling for stronger federal requirements for data centers, saying a proposal expected to come before the Senate does not go far enough to protect communities and utility customers. The Senate is expected to vote Wednesday on the Ratepayer Protection Act. The measure would direct states to consider requiring certain large data centers to cover infrastructure costs associated with their development. States would have two years to consider the standard, but they would not be required to adopt it. Warner criticized that approach during remarks on the Senate floor Tuesday, arguing Congress should establish requirements rather than leave the decision entirely to individual states. “I think we need real legislation on this,” Warner said. “We need legislation that actually has some boundaries. This should not be optional.” Warner is instead promoting his Data Center Tax Accountability and Disclosure Act. His proposal would require greater public disclosure of information including data centers’ energy and water consumption, backup power systems and environmental impacts. The legislation would also connect certain federal tax benefits to whether developers meet standards involving energy, water use, building efficiency, setbacks from neighborhoods and community transparency. Warner pointed to Virginia’s large data center industry while explaining why he believes additional federal action is necessary. “Virginia is the capital of data centers in our country, and there is enormous concern from neighbors, from communities,” Warner said. Under his proposal, developers that fail to meet certain requirements could lose access to some federal tax benefits. Warner said Tuesday that he had not decided how he would vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act. He urged senators to consider his proposal as an alternative with mandatory requirements and penalties for companies that fail to meet them.

artigo.texto: A Unidade de Recuperação Energética (URE) de Barueri terá uma reunião aberta à comunidade no dia 27 de outubro para apresentar o projeto de créditos de carbono que será desenvolvido na usina. O encontro será às 14h, na Avenida Pirarucu, 3.891, no bairro Nova Aldeinha. A reunião será promovida pela Orizon Valorização de Resíduos, empresa responsável pelo empreendimento, e é aberta a moradores e demais interessados. A participação, no entanto, exige confirmação prévia, devido à limitação do espaço físico. Os interessados devem informar o nome completo pelo telefone (11) 91087-9116 ou pelo e-mail comunicacao.social@orizonvr.com.br. Segundo a companhia, serão apresentados os principais aspectos do processo de certificação do projeto junto à Verra, organização internacional que administra padrões para projetos do mercado voluntário de carbono. O encontro também abordará os benefícios ambientais previstos, a geração de energia renovável e a emissão de créditos de carbono. De acordo com a Orizon, haverá espaço para que os participantes tirem dúvidas sobre a usina e apresentem contribuições. O que são os créditos de carbono O projeto pretende transformar em créditos parte das reduções de gases de efeito estufa associadas à operação da URE. De forma geral, um crédito de carbono corresponde a uma tonelada de dióxido de carbono equivalente (CO₂e) que deixou de ser emitida ou foi removida da atmosfera. A emissão dos créditos, porém, não é automática. O projeto precisa seguir uma metodologia reconhecida, demonstrar como as reduções são calculadas e passar por processos de validação e verificação. É nesse contexto que ocorre o processo de certificação junto à Verra que será apresentado durante a reunião. A Orizon estima que a operação da URE evitará a emissão de 128 mil toneladas de CO₂ equivalente por ano. Documentos financeiros do empreendimento também consideram a futura comercialização dos créditos como uma das fontes de receita da usina. Como funciona a URE A URE de Barueri é uma usina projetada para transformar resíduos urbanos não recicláveis em energia elétrica por meio de uma tecnologia conhecida como waste-to-energy (resíduos para energia, em tradução livre). Depois da separação dos materiais que podem ser reciclados, os rejeitos são submetidos a tratamento térmico em altas temperaturas. O calor produzido nesse processo aquece água em uma caldeira e gera vapor. Esse vapor movimenta uma turbina ligada a um gerador, produzindo eletricidade. A unidade terá capacidade para processar cerca de 870 toneladas de resíduos por dia, aproximadamente 300 mil toneladas por ano, provenientes de Barueri, Santana de Parnaíba e Carapicuíba. A potência instalada será de 20 megawatts (MW), suficiente, segundo a empresa, para atender o consumo equivalente a mais de 75 mil residências. A proposta é reduzir a quantidade de resíduos destinada a aterros sanitários, aproveitando a parcela que não pode ser reciclada para a produção de energia. Questionada pela reportagem, a Orizon confirmou que a previsão é de que a URE entre em funcionamento no primeiro semestre de 2027. O Brasil bateu uma marca importante no segmento de ônibus elétricos: chegou a 1.883 unidades circulando pelo país, no primeiro semestre, superando a Colômbia (que tem 1.737 unidades) e ficando apenas atrás do Chile (onde rodam 4.808 veículos), países precursores na eletrificação da frota pública na América Latina. Especialistas afirmam que este é um ponto de virada para esse mercado no país, que vem ganhando tração e atraindo cada vez mais a atenção dos fabricantes: pelo menos 12 empresas estão de olho no potencial brasileiro, sendo que oito já fabricam ônibus elétricos por aqui.
— O crescimento da produção e das vendas, nos últimos dois anos, vem sendo forte. Nos últimos meses, mais ainda. Já temos oito empresas fabricando no Brasil e mais chinesas têm intenção de produzir aqui, aproveitando as regras do Mercosul para exportar para a região — diz Carlos Eduardo de Souza, diretor-conselheiro da Associação Brasileira do Veículo Elétrico (ABVE) e CEO da Tevx, companhia focada em eletromobilidade e infraestrutura de transporte sustentável no Brasil.
Transição em curso
Os números mais recentes refletem o aumento da procura: foram emplacadas 932 unidades entre janeiro e agosto de 2026, um crescimento de 82,03% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025 (quando foram emplacados 512 veículos). Apenas em agosto, o volume de emplacamentos de ônibus elétricos saltou de 89 (julho) para 254 unidades.
- Novas fontes de receita: rede de atacarejo Assaí expande negócios e anuncia compra de postos de combustíveis em São Paulo
São Paulo vem puxando a transição da frota a diesel para os veículos elétricos, com cerca de 80% do total em circulação, porque conta com um modelo de financiamento junto a instituições como o BNDES, que inclui as operadoras, além de ter implementado metas rígidas de descarbonização, que preveem zerar as emissões de gases do transporte público até 2038.
A Secretaria Municipal de Mobilidade Urbana e Transporte (SMT) determinou, em 2022, que seria aceita apenas a inclusão de ônibus movidos a energia limpa na frota, medida fundamental para a renovação dos veículos com modelos elétricos. O programa de metas 2025-2028 determina a substituição de 2.200 ônibus por veículos de matriz energética mais limpa. As concessionárias do transporte paulistano são responsáveis pela contratação da empresa que fará a instalação dos carregadores e pela garantia de abastecimento dos modelos. Atualmente, a infraestrutura de carregamento conta com 455 pontos instalados, diz a SMT.
Na sexta-feira, o BNDES aprovou financiamento de R$ 329 milhões para a cidade do Rio eletrificar a frota por meio de parceria público-privada. O projeto prevê a aquisição de 175 ônibus elétricos.

Nvidia amplia seu programa de recompra de ações que chegará a US$ 235 bilhões, um recorde
Operação deve ser concluída em 2028 e supera a que foi feita pela Apple em 2024, até então a maior da História
A Nvidia, fabricante de chips que está no centro do boom de inteligência artificial, informou nesta segunda-feira que autorizou mais US$ 150 bilhões (R$ 781 bilhões) para seu programa de recompra de ações, tornando-o, segundo a própria empresa, o maior programa de recompra de ações da história, refletindo a confiança do CEO Jensen Huang na continuidade do crescimento da empresa.
- Nova ferramenta: Nvidia lança sistema projetado para impedir que agentes de IA saiam do controle
- ‘Coach’ de robô: Veja como brasileiros ganham dinheiro gravando tarefas como faxina para treinar IA
Com este acréscimo, o valor total de recompra de ações da companhia chegará a US$ 235 bilhões (R$ 1,22 trilhão). O anúncio supera em muito o recorde anterior da Apple, de US$ 110 bilhões (R$ 573,3 bilhões), autorizado em 2024.
A Nvidia espera concluir até a operação até 2028, informou a empresa em um comunicado divulgado na segunda-feira.
“O crescimento da Nvidia está sendo impulsionado por uma mudança de plataforma que ocorre uma vez a cada geração, em direção à inteligência artificial e à computação acelerada”, afirmou Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, no comunicado.
“Nosso forte fluxo de geração de caixa nos dá capacidade para investir nas tecnologias que impulsionam essa transformação e devolver capital aos acionistas. Essa autorização reflete nossa confiança na oportunidade de longo prazo que temos pela frente”, acrescentou Huang.
As ações da fabricante de chips dispararam em meio ao boom de inteligência artificial. Os chips da Nvidia são o elemento central dos gigantescos data centers de IA, e a demanda por esses chips tornou-se um indicador da crescente demanda pela tecnologia.
Outras empresas vêm comprando dezenas de bilhões de dólares em chips da Nvidia, tornando a companhia a empresa de capital aberto mais valiosa do mundo, com uma capitalização de mercado de cerca de US$ 5 trilhões.
A recompra ocorre após a empresa informar, no mês passado, que sua receita mais que dobrou, para US$ 96,22 bilhões, no trimestre encerrado em julho. Apenas três anos atrás, o lucro trimestral da Nvidia era de US$ 6,2 bilhões.
Em agosto, a Nvidia informou aos investidores que sua receita projetada para o trimestre atual aumentaria 90% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior, chegando a US$ 108 bilhões — um sinal de que o boom da inteligência artificial ainda tem bastante força.

Empresário revela a lição sobre dinheiro que mudou sua visão sobre investimentos
À frente da Novo Ideal desde 2016, Léo Casellato conta como o contato com mais de 2.500 endividados mudou sua visão sobre dinheiro, e por que renda alta não é sinônimo de vida financeira organizada
Quando fundou a Novo Ideal, em 2016, o empresário e educador financeiro Léo Casellato tinha uma certeza que os anos seguintes se encarregariam de desmontar: a de que o problema de quem se endivida é, no fundo, falta de dinheiro. Depois de participar da negociação de cerca de R$ 1 bilhão em dívidas e atender mais de 2.500 clientes, ele chegou a uma conclusão diferente.
"Entrei achando que o problema das pessoas era falta de dinheiro. Depois de negociar cerca de R$ 1 bilhão em dívidas e atender mais de 2.500 clientes, entendi que raramente o problema é quanto a pessoa ganha: é a relação que ela tem com o próprio dinheiro", afirma.
Na prática, diz Casellato, a renda isolada explica pouco. Ao longo da operação, ele conta ter encontrado dos dois lados do balcão: profissionais de salário alto afogados em dívidas e famílias de renda modesta com as contas em dia e uma reserva montada. O que separava um grupo do outro, segundo ele, não era o valor do contracheque, mas os hábitos por trás dele.
Foi essa percepção que mudou também a forma como o empresário enxerga o investimento. Para ele, o erro mais comum de quem quer começar é pular etapas: procurar produtos financeiros antes de entender o próprio comportamento de consumo.
"Investir não começa na corretora, começa no comportamento. Antes de falar em ação, FII ou renda fixa, a pessoa precisa entender para onde o dinheiro dela vai todo mês", explica.
O primeiro passo que recomenda é menos sofisticado do que se imagina: acompanhar, por um ou dois meses, cada real que entra e sai. Sem esse mapa, argumenta, qualquer escolha de investimento vira aposta, porque a pessoa não sabe quanto sobra de verdade nem para onde o dinheiro está escapando. A educação financeira, nesse raciocínio, tem menos a ver com decorar produtos e mais com construir uma disciplina que sustente as decisões no longo prazo.
O ponto de virada da própria trajetória, ele reconhece, veio do contato diário com o endividamento, inclusive como lição pessoal.
"A dívida me ensinou que investir é, antes de tudo, uma questão de consciência e disciplina, não de sorte ou de 'ter muito dinheiro'", conclui.

'Ninho de cobras': Guerra entre cartéis rivais faz crescer assassinatos e desaparecimentos de mulheres no México
Confrontos tornaram-se tão generalizados que as fronteiras entre violência doméstica, violência de gênero e retaliação dos cartéis frequentemente se sobrepõem
Faz quase um ano que sua irmã mais nova, Cecilia, desapareceu, e Nadia Berrelleza mal consegue dormir. Em vez disso, ela passa as noites em busca de pistas, refazendo os últimos passos de Cecilia e examinando mensagens, fotografias e vídeos que supostamente revelam seu destino. Uma das imagens que ela recebeu mostrava uma jovem de cabelos longos, cacheados e negros — iguais aos de Cecilia — ajoelhada e vendada, com as mãos amarradas, cercada por homens armados. Os investigadores disseram que a imagem foi gerada por inteligência artificial. Outro vídeo enviado pelo Facebook mostrava uma mulher sendo agredida sexualmente. O remetente exigiu uma recompensa.
- Quer morar fora? Veja guia interativo que reúne informações sobre 36 países
- Quer mais notícias de Mundo? Acompanhe o canal no WhatsApp
— Conheço perfeitamente o rosto dela; jamais acreditaria que fosse ela — disse Nadia Berrelleza. — Mas ainda assim é horrível ver aquilo.
Cecilia Berrelleza, de 31 anos, desapareceu em julho de 2025 após almoçar com amigos em Mazatlán, cidade litorânea do estado mexicano de Sinaloa. Desde então, Nadia tem feito apelos às autoridades e ao público, chegando a oferecer seu carro como recompensa pelo paradeiro de Cecilia. A atenção recebida, segundo ela, gerou diversas pistas, mas também oportunistas que tentam extorqui-la com falsas alegações sobre o paradeiro de Cecilia.
O desaparecimento faz parte de uma onda de violência que tornou o estado de Sinaloa o mais perigoso do país para as mulheres. Coincide também com uma guerra entre duas facções do Cartel de Sinaloa, que enfraqueceu a segurança e aterrorizou o estado durante dois anos. Os confrontos tornaram-se tão generalizados que as fronteiras entre violência doméstica, violência de gênero e retaliação dos cartéis frequentemente se sobrepõem.
- Sob pressão de Trump: México envia 37 acusados de integrar cartéis aos Estados Unidos
No ano passado, 105 mulheres foram assassinadas em Sinaloa, o maior número em 14 anos e quase o dobro do total do ano anterior, enquanto outras 299 desapareceram. Setenta e três desses assassinatos foram investigados como feminicídios, termo usado para descrever crimes motivados por questões de gênero. Em julho, Sinaloa voltou a liderar o país em número de mulheres assassinadas, e 153 mulheres desapareceram.
Em março de 2025, Vivian Karely Aispuro, de 26 anos, foi a uma festa com a irmã e as amigas. Ela nunca voltou para casa. Dias depois, seu corpo foi encontrado em uma estrada de terra em Culiacán. Seus familiares acreditam que uma conhecida a dopou e a levou para a casa do ex-namorado, acusado de seu assassinato. Os promotores afirmam que ele a golpeou no rosto com uma caneca de cerveja e a deixou sangrar até a morte

Vítima de estelionato virtual lamenta críticas: 'Está sendo duro'
Delegado faz um paralelo com caso retratado em novela e diz que é preciso ‘redobrar a atenção’ com pedidos feitos por pessoas conhecidas em aplicativos de namoro
Atualizado
O delegado Felipe Santoro recorreu às redes sociais, no fim de semana, para traçar um paralelo entre um inquérito recém-concluído e “Quem Ama Cuida”, da TV Globo. “Engraçado como a novela, muitas vezes, imita a vida real, de forma simultânea”, escreveu o policial. Santoro se referia ao indiciamento de um homem por estelionato sentimental — crime em que uma relação afetiva é usada como instrumento para obter vantagem financeira. Na ficção, Carmita, personagem de Deborah Evelyn, também cai em um golpe amoroso aplicado pelo namorado, Edson (Vandré Silveira).
- Falsa intenção: veja como funciona o golpe em aplicativos de namoro e como se proteger
- 'Não sou bandida', diz Verônica Costa: veja chegada da Mãe Loira do funk à sede da Polinter após ser presa por tortura
O caso real que chegou à 37ª DP (Ilha do Governador) envolve uma mulher que prefere não ser identificada na reportagem, mas conta ter tido coragem de procurar a polícia para denunciar o golpista:
— Hoje estou bem abalada. Reviver tudo e ler críticas de pessoas dizendo “como você cai em um golpe em 2026” está sendo duro. Mas existem outras mulheres que são vítimas e se calam por vergonha; por isso ele continua agindo. Eu estou com vergonha, mas não vou me calar.
Ligação do chefe
